the opposite and cited no source — it had pinned whatever `CanSlap` happened
to do.

**Amended the same day.** A captive answers to its **jailer alone**, its own
keeper included — *"a keeper can't slap its own creature in someone else's
dungeon"* (owner). Prison is the only place this simulation puts a creature in
another's dungeon, so that is the whole reachable rule; reach in general is not.

**Left open.** The animation is presentation. The Skeleton cap **is** enforced —
at the maximum a withering prisoner dies to a corpse on the rim instead of rising
(owner) — but what it counts is unknown, so nothing enforces it yet (Q307).

**Consequences.** No state field and no stored quantity changed, so `HashVersion`
and the pin stand.

## ADR-0141 — Construction state backs door and trap trigger counts

**Date:** 2026-09-11 · **Status:** accepted · Q249–Q253, Q281, Q284 · Research: `docs/research/doors-and-traps.md`

**Context.** ADR-0106 retained authored doors and traps but declined conditions
27 and 28 because their runtime predicates were absent. Reading both complete
class vtables, their constructors, THINGS loaders and save ranges establishes
how the authored records seed those predicates.

**Decision.** Add hashed `UnderConstruction` state to doors and traps. A door
starts under construction exactly when authored `Flags` bit 1 is set. A trap
starts under construction exactly when authored `NumberOfShots` is zero; that
field is a Boolean construction marker in the loader, not a consumable count.
The verbatim authored fields remain for ADR-0106 compatibility.

Implement the counting modes of player conditions 27 and 28. Flag bit 3 counts
under-construction instances; bit 4 counts constructed instances; otherwise
zero `TargetId` counts all owned instances and a nonzero id filters by type.
Type 28's named Boulder Trap path also counts owned live Boulder objects.
Availability mode (`Comparison == 0`) remains declined because availability is
separate state and no shipped condition uses that mode.

**Door blocking is deliberately out of scope.** The binary read establishes
that constructed locked doors mark the navigation grid and that the update
toggles an open state from nearby creatures, but reproducing this touches
`DK2.Pathfinding`, imp task routing and every routed scenario. Neither trigger
condition needs it, and the open/close eligibility partitions are not fully
named, so it must arrive as its own measured mechanic rather than a side effect.

**Consequences.** Version 56 was taken by parallel work; `HashVersion` and
snapshot `FormatVersion` become **57**. The branch-base determinism literal is
re-pinned from a computed run. At 1,200 ticks the
campaign oracle moves `stalls / moved / after1` from **53 / 62 / 11** to
**46 / 62 / 11**; foreclosed gates fall from 145 to 124. Doors still do not
open, close or block movement; traps still do not fire.


## ADR-0142 — The prison drain is a relationship, not a flag

**Date:** 2026-09-11 · **Status:** accepted · Q266, Q302, Q308

**Context.** The owner: a campaign map can hold a creature in a prison **without
draining it**, so a script can release it when a keeper finds the place — "an
optional flag, on by default". The search began on the creature's `Flags` byte,
whose bits 5 and 6 are the only ones shipped data varies. It ended at the drain
itself, `FUN_0047B7C0`, read whole.

**Decision.** There is no flag. The drain runs every 16 ticks — four game
seconds, `variable 19 << 2`, which is where the original's coarser −12 comes
from — and takes health off only when all of these hold:

1. `HungerFill` scaled by level is non-zero (the Q173 gate, already built);
2. the creature is **in a room** at all, `+0x3B9` non-zero;
3. the room's owner and the creature's own owner **differ**, or they agree and
   that owner is **not the neutral player**.

So **a neutral creature in an unclaimed prison waits there indefinitely**, and
claiming the prison starts its clock. That is the campaign trick, and it needs no
per-creature switch. `PrisonRules.Withers` is the third gate in our terms.

**Two globals settle with it — Q266, open since 2026-09-08.** The drain
exempts `word[0x006F2548]`, an exemption that only makes sense for the player an
unclaimed room belongs to; the corpus places `NEUTRAL_CREATURE` records on prison
tiles, and the player frame returns early for the same id. **`0x006F2548` is the
neutral player and `0x006F254C` the hero one**, the latter already ours from the
party counter. Flame's map agrees; cited, not adopted.

**The flag hunt was not wasted, and its result is recorded rather than dropped.**
Shipped data uses four values of the `Flags` byte — `0x09` (the constructor's
own default), `0x29`, `0x49`, `0x69` — so bits 0 and 3 are universal and only
5 and 6 vary. Bit 6 is read **once in the whole binary** and sets state 76, whose
handler DK2 files in `KeeperState.cpp`; bit 5 twice, in a routine taking a room
and a creature. Neither is the drain (Q302).

**One caveat withdrawn the same day.** This ADR first called DK2's drain "wider"
than ours for keying on the room rather than on imprisonment. It is not:
`FUN_0047B7C0` is the **prison state's own** per-tick hook, so it runs for a
creature already in that state and the room lookup only chooses whose ownership
to compare. Nobody merely walking through drains — and nobody merely walking
through is stopped either, the confinement being the prisoner's and not the
prison's (owner). The gate is **inert today**: nothing here
imprisons a creature the map placed, so no neutral prisoner can arise. Built
anyway, because the rule it replaces said every prisoner that eats withers, and
that is wrong however few creatures reach it.

**Consequences.** No state field and no stored quantity changed; the pin stands.

## ADR-0143 — The Skeleton ceiling is per keeper, over that keeper's prisons

**Date:** 2026-09-11 · **Status:** accepted · Q307

**Context.** The owner: the ceiling is *"not global, not global per prisons on
the map, it is per keeper, per keeper's prisons"*, and asked for it against the
binary. The route in was `ModifyHealth`: when a health change is **exactly the
prison drain** and the creature's definition leaves a body, it hands the room
the creature is standing in a position and asks it to make a creature
(`0x004B3231`). If that returns zero it sets `DeadBodyOnDestroy` instead
(`0x004B323A`) — so the refusal and the corpse are the same branch.

**What the room does** — `FUN_004E30F0`, and it is two walks:

1. from the room's **owner**, walk that player's own room list (`player+0x36`),
   keep the rooms whose `TypeId` is 11, and **sum their
   `SafeCreatureCapacity`** (`0x004E3123`);
2. from the same owner, walk that player's **creature list**
   (`player+0x06`, `ThingsOwnedList[0]`) and count the ones whose type is the
   room definition's `CreatedCreatureId` (`0x004E315C`).

`count >= sum` refuses. **The owner's claim is confirmed exactly**, and the two
walks answer more than was asked: the ceiling is the sum over the keeper's
prisons, so a second prison raises it for both and selling one lowers it; and the
tally counts the keeper's Skeletons **anywhere on the map**, so one that walked
out of the cell it rose in still occupies the ceiling.

**Decision.** Build both walks — `PrisonRules.SkeletonCap` and
`SkeletonCount` — and have `PrisonSystem` route a refused prisoner into the
body-on-the-rim path ADR-0140 already built, which is what DK2's
`DeadBodyOnDestroy` amounts to here.

**Independent corroboration of the offsets.** `player+0x36` as the room list and
`player+0x06` as `ThingsOwnedList[0]` are DK2's own dumper names
(`player-object.md`), read months before this, and `room+0x4B` as
`SafeCreatureCapacity` likewise. Nothing here needed a new inference.

**A route that did not work, recorded so nobody repeats it.** The tooltip string
2586 carries the number, and its builder's argument descriptors use two different
vtables — which looked like two data sources and is not: both are string
**formatting-tag** classes, multi-byte and unicode. The display told us nothing
about where the value comes from.

**Consequences.** No state field and no stored quantity changed; the pin stands.

## ADR-0144 — Action type 17 is read, and deliberately not built

**Date:** 2026-09-11 · **Status:** accepted · Q237, Q309

**Context.** Type 17 was the next build candidate: 291 records across 40 levels
**including level 1**, so unlike types 1, 7 and 8 a level-1 replay would exercise
it and a capture could measure it. The arm at `0x00519257` was read end to end
first, to size the work. It turned out to size it at zero.

**What the arm does** — resolve the `ActionPointId`; **succeed and do nothing
if it does not resolve**; walk the point's rectangle inclusively; per slab set or
clear **one bit of the slab's flag word** according to body byte 1; then send one
rectangle-shaped notification. Full detail, including the multi-slab chain case,
in `trigger-dispatch-tables.md`.

**Decision.** Build nothing, and leave type 17 reported as `Partial`. Two
independent findings support it, either sufficient:

1. **Every reader found for that slab bit is display** — one overhead-map
   painter, in which a set bit suppresses the tile's colour. That painter tests
   the **fog** bit (slab `+0xB` bit `0x40`, `fog-of-war.md` §11) separately in
   the same expression, which rules fog out as this bit's meaning and
   corroborates the fog finding from a second direction for free.
2. **The notifications enter an optional sink** — one forwarder, 47 call
   sites across every subsystem, which returns success and does nothing when no
   handler object is installed. A channel the engine runs correctly without does
   not carry simulation state.

**What this buys even though no code changed.** Type 17's `Partial` is now a read
result rather than an absence of one, and 291 records stop being a to-do. The
rectangle corner **order** (`StartX +0x38`, `StartY +0x3A`, `EndX +0x3C`,
`EndY +0x3E`) moves from STRONGLY INFERRED to CONFIRMED, because the walk indexes
the slab array with one pair as the column and multiplies the other by the map
width. Q237's open half — *who walks a point's rectangle, and when* —
gains a named answer: this arm does, once, when the action runs.

**Rejected: modelling the bit as hashed tile state.** It would bump
`HashVersion` to store a field no rule reads, on a meaning nothing has pinned
— pinning a guess in the one place the project treats as settled.

**Left open.** What the bit *means* is UNKNOWN and is Q309. **"No simulation
reader found" is not "no simulation reader"**, and a mask that folded this bit
with neighbours would not appear in a scan for the constant.

**Consequences.** No state field, no stored quantity and no behaviour changed;
the pin stands.

## ADR-0145 — Q204's two flags were already named in files we had

**Date:** 2026-09-11 · **Status:** accepted · Q204

**Context.** Two flags gate DK2's job path and neither was identified: a
per-player bit in the dispatcher, and a per-creature-type bit in all three
choosers. Both were opened as Q204 in the sitting that reversed
`job-selection.md`, and the plan carried the first as the candidate for a
**fallen dungeon heart**, which would have made it the next feature's key.

**Decision.** Record both answers, build neither, and withdraw the defeat
hypothesis.

**`player+0x76` bit 2 is `CallToArmsOn`.** The player debug dumper reaches
`+0x76` once per bit; at `0x004BD31B` it shifts right by **2**, masks 1, and
prints `CallToArmsOn %d`. The shift is the evidence — the order of the names
already transcribed in `player-object.md` only corroborates it. The guard takes
the creature's **owner** (`+0x2A`, Q262's pointer), so the flag is the keeper's:
set, the dispatcher jumps past its whole `0..0x1C` table and admits jobs 10 and
16 alone. Job 10 sets state **194**, shipped label `leaving Dungeon`. **So a
Call To Arms suspends voluntary job-taking for that keeper's whole workforce.**

**`def+0x686 & 0x4000` is `IsHorny`.** The loader copies file `0xEFC` into
runtime `+0x686` unchanged, so `0x4000` is bit 14, which `CreatureEnums.cs` has
named `IsHorny` since it was written. Verified the ADR-0086 way rather than
trusted: the bit is set on **exactly one of the 46 shipped creatures**.

**Nothing is built, and the first cannot be.** This simulation has no Call To
Arms, so there is no state to drive that gate from; the omission is recorded at
`CreatureJobSystem` so it lands when Call To Arms does. The second is inert for
a different reason — Horny is never created here.

**What this cost, and the pattern it makes.** Both answers were already inside
this repository: one in a research doc transcribed for Q264, one in an enum
written months ago. **Nobody had put either beside the question.** That is the
second instance in one day — the first being the same `IsHorny` bit — so
the lesson is not about these two flags: **when a question names an offset or a
mask, search the repo for the offset before searching the binary.**

**Consequences.** No state field and no stored quantity changed; the pin stands.
Defeat loses its candidate flag and needs a new one (Q93, Q207).

## ADR-0146 — Auto furniture is reconciled from room shape

**Date:** 2026-09-11 · **Status:** accepted · Q89, Q270

**Context.** DK2 attraction needs room `TotalCapacity`, but that value counts
room-owned furniture rather than geometry. The simulation had no way to
distinguish such furniture from objects placed by creatures, the level, or a
keeper. Binary evidence for the implemented placement subset is recorded once
in `auto-placed-furniture.md`.

**Decision.** Add a hashed and snapshotted `ObjectState.AutoPlaced` bit. After
room construction each tick, derive the desired generic floor and wall furniture,
Temple Hand, and Hatchery coops from current room shapes, then reconcile only
objects bearing that bit. Object type choice uses DK2's coordinate-stable
selector, not the simulation RNG.

Room instances remain derived views. Storing a second furniture list on them
would duplicate world-object state and need invalidation whenever room tiles
change. Reconciliation preserves keeper-, creature-, and level-placed objects,
even at an identical tile and type.

**Boundary.** Wall placement requires both `Solid` and `AllowRoomWalls`; the binary's
extra grid test is its cached `Solid` classification. Sorted tiles stand in for
its linked-list phase. Object rotation, sub-tile offsets, and room-specific
decorative passes remain open. The five known capacity arms are exposed;
portal attraction is separate work.

**Consequences.** `HashVersion` and snapshot format become 58. Existing saves
are intentionally rejected; the determinism pin changes with the added bit.
## ADR-0147 — Attraction is a per-type budget, and the Lair is exempt

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-14.

**Context.** `PortalRules.IsAttracted` answered attraction as a boolean with no
cap, so a keeper with one Temple received Dark Angels for ever. The owner saw
otherwise on 2026-09-11 — a 3x5 Temple produced none, a 5x5 produced exactly
**two**, and other types kept arriving throughout, so the portal was firing and
declining her. `binary-entrance.md` §4/§4.1 had the mechanism read and
unbuilt for want of room furniture, which ADR-0146 has since supplied.

**Decision.** A fifth gate, `AttractionBudget.Admits`, after ADR-0042's four.
For the creature's **first** attraction slot — the only one the original's
builder reads — sum each matching room's contribution and admit the type while
that sum **exceeds** the number of that type the keeper already holds.

| Room | Contributes | |
|---|---|---|
| Lair | never capped: the arm stores a flat 1.0 and jumps past the draw-down | CONFIRMED |
| Temple | **2** while it holds object 66, the Temple Hand, else 0 | CONFIRMED |
| Prison, Combat Pit | the room's interior cells (amended 2026-09-30) | STRONGLY INFERRED |
| every other | `AutoFurnitureRules.TryTotalCapacity` | CONFIRMED |

Whole numbers where the original uses 12-bit fixed point: every contribution is
shifted left 12 and every subtraction is exactly 1.0, so the comparison is the
same one and no rounding enters.

**Consequences.**

- **Goblins are unchanged**, because they are the Lair case. That is why level 1
  still matches and no scenario moved.
- Nine of the ten attracting types are capped where they were unbounded.
- No world state is added, so `HashVersion` is untouched.

**Assumptions, stated rather than hidden.**

- **Amended 2026-09-30:** `0x00454110` tests `byte[slab+0x0C] == 0xFF`, the
  interior marker, before its type switch, so a Prison or Combat Pit contributes
  its interior cells only, never its rim (record `00454110`). Built as
  `InteriorTileIndices.Count`; a 3x3 prison gives 1, not 9.
- The Lair arm has a second branch giving 3.0 when a creature byte `+0x771` is
  **22**. Unexplained, and harmless here: the draw-down is skipped either way, so
  1.0 and 3.0 both admit for ever.
- Slot 1 is never budgeted, only required to exist (`PortalRules.IsAttracted`).

## ADR-0148 — Two disposal tiles, and the prison decides at the door

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-15.

**Context.** Owner play on 2026-09-13 recorded three divergences and built none
of them. Two are behavioural rules with no missing rooms behind them: disposal
has **two** unwalkable targets rather than one, and a prison refuses a delivery
**at the door** rather than before the imp sets off.

**Decision 1: `DisposalRules`, and the two targets are exclusive.** A portal's
hole takes anything that is not a worker; a dungeon heart's raised platform takes
a worker and nothing else. Both bypass the walkability refusal in
`HandSystem.Drop`, as the hole alone did (ADR-0084); neither bypasses ownership,
so a rival's heart is refused the way a rival's portal already was. A captive is
refused both, which is now CONFIRMED rather than the conservative fallback it was
chosen as.

**Decision 2: capacity is checked at delivery** (amended by ADR-0354: not when every prison is already full). `PrisonRules.DeliveryTileIn`
gives a free cell where one exists and the nearest full prison's **rim** where
none does, so the imp sets off either way; `PrisonRules.AdmitsAt` decides at the
door, and a prison that filled during the walk turns the body away. The manual's
*"imps stop collecting prisoners"* describes a keeper with **no** prison, which
is still -1 and still nobody setting off.

**Consequences.**

- A keeper whose prisons are full now has imps that carry and are refused,
  leaving bodies on the rim. That is work where there was none, and it is what
  DK2 does. **Amended by ADR-0354:** only a Prison that fills during the carry
  refuses; with every Prison already full, no imp sets off.
- `HashVersion` is untouched: no world state is added, and no scenario moved.

**Assumptions, stated rather than hidden.**

- ~~Three assumptions about the heart~~ **withdrawn 2026-09-15**: the owner
  supplied screenshots of both halves (Q312, closed). It is the **single centre
  tile** of a heart that takes an imp, not the raised 3x3; the imp's **gold
  vanishes with it**; and a **goblin is refused** the heart outright, so the two
  disposal tiles really are exclusive. A dungeon heart is **always 5x5**.
- **Ours, not DK2's:** a body already lying at a prison that will not take it is
  not picked up again, or the imp would carry it round the room for ever. The
  end state is the owner's; the guard is ours.
- Which rim tile a refused body lands on, and how ties between eligible prisons
  break, remain UNKNOWN.

## ADR-0149 — Persistent Temple history follows a deterministic room anchor

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-15.

**Context.** DK2 keeps a three-offering ring on each Temple room, but our
`RoomInstance` is rebuilt from tiles and deliberately carries no persistent
state (ADR-0027). Sacrifice therefore needs stable ownership without turning
all derived rooms into stored entities. DK2's identity across edits is UNKNOWN.

**Decision.** `WorldState` stores ordered `TempleSacrificeState` records keyed
by the lowest tile index of the derived Temple plus its owner. Reconciliation
runs after room build/sell and before creatures act; Hand intake also reconciles
before use. History follows the component only while that anchor and owner
remain a current Temple.

Thus extending without changing the lowest tile preserves history. On a split,
the component retaining the anchor inherits it. On a merge, the lowest-anchor
component survives and the others are discarded. Removing the anchor, adding a
new lower tile, selling the room, changing its type, or changing its owner resets
the affected history. These topology rules are ours, not claims about DK2.

**Consequences.** Histories are sorted by anchor, hashed, and snapshotted.
`HashVersion` and snapshot `FormatVersion` move 58 → 59; the pin becomes
`0x659AB04378E4C2FE`. `RoomInstance` remains wholly derived.

## ADR-0150 — A scenario states its timings in game seconds, and asserts them

**Status:** Accepted (2026-09-15)

**Context.** Twenty-five of the twenty-seven scenarios asserted nothing; they
were prose with an event log attached. Populating the expectation blocks
(ADR-0147's gate) found that **six of the twenty-seven were no longer
demonstrating their own question**, and four of the six had been disarmed by one
unrelated change: ADR-0089 moved a game second from twenty ticks to four, and
every scenario that had been tuned in ticks silently stopped reaching its
subject. A bird landed 350 seconds into a cell whose occupants die at 83. A dig
that needed two applications was given one, so three scenarios claimed nothing
and then had their builds refused `NotYourLand` — for months, with green tests.

**Decision.**

1. **Every scenario whose claim is an event carries an `expect` block**, and
   `EveryScenario_MeetsItsExpectations` is the gate. Twenty-three do; the other
   four say in the file why they cannot, rather than looking unfinished.
2. **A scenario's timings are stated in game seconds and derived into ticks in
   the comment beside them.** A bare tick number is a unit waiting to change
   under it.
3. **An experiment broken by a unit change is repaired to its authored intent**,
   not re-described. Moving the bird back to seventy game seconds is restoring
   the experiment; re-writing the prose to say the captives die first is
   abandoning it.
4. **Where the repair is not determined by the authored intent, the scenario is
   left recording its own regression instead.** A tick that meant seventy game
   seconds converts to one answer; "how much unclaimed ground is little enough"
   has none. `an_imp_drags_an_enemy_to_prison` (Q315) and
   `the_keeper_picks_up_an_imp_and_slaps_it` (Q317) now assert what they do
   today, with a `because` that names the question. Picking a new map or a new
   seam for them would be redesigning an experiment to make a check green, which
   is the failure mode the gate exists to prevent.

**Consequences.** The corpus is a regression corpus. A run report names its
claims and whether they held, and the harness exits non-zero when one fails, so
the CLI and the test gate agree. The cost is that four scenarios now carry a
WARNING paragraph saying they no longer answer their own title — which is the
honest state of them, and was true and unsaid before.

## ADR-0151 — Graveyard life-force belongs to a persistent room anchor

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-16.

**Context.** The Graveyard room dump names one room field, the dword
`DecomposeValue`. Burial supplies the creature field of the same name; shipped
variable 25 requires 1000 and the room's `CreatedCreatureId` is Vampire. A
Goblin supplies 200, independently agreeing with the five-corpse account (Q165).
`RoomInstance` remains derived, so the tally needs persistent identity.

**Decision.** `WorldState` stores ordered `GraveyardState` records keyed by the
room's lowest tile index and owner, reconciled by ADR-0149's Temple policy.
Only successful burial adds life-force; death does not, because Horny and Jack
have value 200 but produce no body. At the threshold the room raises its
`CreatedCreatureId`, and `corpse_buried` reports `tally` plus `raised=Vampire
as=N`, matching the Prison's creation event shape.

Four unresolved edges use explicit project defaults: spawn on the last burial
tile (Q318), subtract 1000 rather than zeroing (Q319), at most one Vampire per
burial (Q320), and clear the tally once reconciliation observes the room absent
(Q321). These are not claims about DK2.

**Consequences.** Tallies are hashed and snapshotted. `HashVersion` and snapshot
`FormatVersion` move 59 → 60; the pin becomes `0xE44F66372F8963D9`.

## ADR-0152 — Creature trigger roots join the per-turn entity pass

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-16.

**Context.** THINGS creatures carry a trigger root, but projection discarded it
and the executor walked only action points and players. The binary's creature
setter snapshots the root condition's repeat byte; its per-turn condition and
action dispatchers delegate creature → owner player → world. The separate
event-filter caller is not a tree walk and remains out of scope.

**Decision.** Project each creature's root and its initial repeat snapshot,
hash and snapshot both, then walk creature roots in THINGS order once per game
turn after action points. Q330 records that relative ordering as UNKNOWN. The
creature dispatcher evaluates health percentage (36), carried-gold percentage
(37), and level (49). Types 3–16, 50, 54, 55, 63 and 65 return DK2's constant
false on this path. The ten creature-owned action types report `Partial`: their
success return is known, but their effects are not implemented by guesswork.

**Consequences.** In the 14,400-turn shipped corpus, executed records rise
3144 → 3793 and the creature-only bucket falls 1138 → 504. The declined
condition frontier stays 128: the newly reached event arms are intentionally
false here, while their firing path remains future work. Level16 still reports
two world-type-64 stalls gating two records, but its 48 creature roots are now
walked. `HashVersion` and snapshot `FormatVersion` move 60 → 61; the pin becomes
`0x57435BC71CE1BBDC`.

## ADR-0153 — The melee damage formula is built as a rule nothing calls

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-16.

**Context.** Q8 is now read end to end (`combat-damage.md`). The three helpers
the accessor uses are a fixed-point add, divide and multiply, not the clamps
`combat.md` §5.1 guessed; its three attacker arms are mutually exclusive and all
three flags were already named in our own `creature-object.md`; and there is no
resistance step anywhere between the accessor and the health routine. What the
simulation does not have is an attack state, target acquisition, or the cadence
of `combat-cadence.md`.

**Decision.** Implement §2–§4 as `MeleeDamageRules`, a pure static class with
tests, and **wire it to nothing**. Reproduce the original's two rounding
behaviours rather than tidying them: the damage is negated before the bonuses,
so every `/ 100` truncates toward zero, and a blow that rounds to zero never
reaches the health routine at all. Take the bearing as a raw angle rather than
reimplementing `atan2`. Mark the possession percentage `Hypothesis`, alone in
the class, because the scalar the original reads has no writer (Q337).

**Consequences.** 22 new tests, 5 of them install-gated and re-reading the three
shipped inputs so the synthetic fixture cannot drift from the install. No
simulation state, so `HashVersion` is unchanged at 61 and no scenario moves.
The Combat Pit's shipped 100 is an increment against a ceiling of 100, so a pit
fighter hits for **double** — the variable's name argues for the other reading
and is now pinned by a test. Combat still does not happen; this buys the attack
state a formula instead of a guess when someone writes it.

**Amended 2026-09-30.** The bearing is no longer raw: `FightRules` passes
`Bearing.Of`, which reproduces `0x0065FB54`'s own table (Q370).

## ADR-0154 — A captive dropped on a Temple is sacrificed, not freed

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-16.

**Context.** ADR-0064's release rule — *dropped anywhere that is not a prison
tile, a prisoner goes free* — is CONFIRMED by the owner, and ADR-0149's Temple
intake consumes any creature dropped on a Temple. The two collide on one tile,
and `HandSystem` resolved it by excluding captives from the intake, under a
comment saying the confirmed rule wins until asked. Q314 asked.

**Decision.** The Temple wins. **Owner, 2026-09-16: a wizard captive dropped on
a Temple was sacrificed** — *"the gods have accepted your sacrifice"*. The
`!PrisonRules.IsImprisoned` guard comes out of the creature-drop path, so the
intake is tested before the release, and ADR-0064's rule carries an explicit
Temple exception rather than a silent one.

**Consequences.** One guard removed, one test inverted —
`APrisonerDroppedOnATempleGoesFreeRatherThanBeingSacrificed` asserted the wrong
half for a day and is now
`APrisonerDroppedOnATempleIsSacrificedRatherThanFreed`. It had named its own
doubt in a comment, which is why it was findable the moment the answer arrived.
No hashed state changes and no scenario covers the path, so `HashVersion` stays
at 61 and the determinism pin does not move. A captive is an offering like any
other: it enters the Temple's three-entry recipe history under its creature type
and current level.

## ADR-0155 — The pathfinder's replacement target is known, and not chosen

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-16 · amended the same day, twice: the owner confirms creatures push each other (Q345), and that a long off-diagonal route runs **straight** (Q341). The divergence is no longer structural-but-invisible — both the routing and the mover are now wrong in ways that can be watched. Amended again the same day: the original's search is read end to end (Q341, `navigation-mesh-and-search.md`) — greedy best-first from both ends, shorter funnelled route kept — so the rebuild decision is now informable; only the triangulation's internals remain (Q347). Amended once more: the triangulation is read at the algorithm level as well — a rectangle-decomposed, constrained, non-Delaunay mesh (`navigation-mesh-and-search.md` §2.1) — so the rebuild waits on nothing UNKNOWN beyond Q348's flag bits. Q348 is read too: the bits are per-edge width classes for a clearance mechanism the shipped game never engages, and region ids that nothing in routing consults. **Owner, 2026-09-16: rebuild.** The design is ADR-0157.

**Context.** ADR-0012 shipped `GridPathfinder` as an admitted placeholder
because DK2's routing was unread. It is now read at the architectural level
(`navigation-and-steering.md`, Q5): the original routes over a **triangulated
navigation mesh**, reduces a corridor of gates to waypoints, and follows it with
a **steering system** of eight named behaviours. Ours is eight-connected A* over
tiles.

**Decision.** Record the divergence and change no code. Replacing a grid search
with a navmesh and a force-based mover is an architectural decision with a cost
far beyond this finding, and the owner makes it. `GridPathfinder` keeps its
`Dk2Behavior` confidence and its docstring gains a pointer to the research.

**Consequences.** The two observed facts ADR-0012 rests on survive, because they
were measured against the running game rather than inferred: eight-connectivity
with corner-cutting (Q28) and no terrain weighting (Q30). Any replacement must
still satisfy both. What does not survive is the interface's premise that a tile
route is what DK2 computes. No behaviour changes, so `HashVersion` stays at 61
and the determinism pin does not move. Q341–Q344 carried the unread
algorithms; all four are now answered and built (ADR-0157).

## ADR-0156 — Separation is built as a rule and wired to nothing

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-16 · the wiring it declined arrived the next day
with ADR-0157 phase 3: `SeparationBehaviour` is one of the four forces
`CreatureMovementSystem` combines, so ours push each other apart as the owner
describes (Q345).

**Context.** The owner confirms creatures push each other (Q345) and ours walk
through each other. DK2's force law is now read end to end
(`navigation-and-steering.md` §3.2): a gate on overlap, an octile distance, a
ratio against summed radii and three arms.

**Decision.** Build `SeparationRules` as pure arithmetic reproducing the
original's operations, and call it from nothing. Wiring needs two things this
project does not have: DK2's rule for combining five behaviour forces into
motion (Q343, unread), and a mover with a velocity to accept one. Inventing
either would put a guess underneath every creature's position, which is the
one place this project has agreed not to guess.

**Consequences.** Creatures passed through each other until phase 3, and that
was a known, recorded divergence rather than a silent one. The arithmetic is
transcribed rather than reinterpreted — including an integer square root kept
because it stops at its first converged guess. The branch that would not
reconcile was answered by reading the caller instead (Q346, Q343): every force
is truncated to `max_force` before weighting, so the two arms agree downstream.
No
simulation state moves, so `HashVersion` stays at 61 and the determinism pin
does not move. Same shape as ADR-0153 for the damage formula, for the same
reason: the rule is knowable now, the integration is not.

## ADR-0157 — The router is rebuilt on the original's mesh, search and funnel

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-16 · phase 1 (`NavMesh`, `MeshRouter`, `Funnel`)
landed the same day · phase 2 (`DK2.Simulation.Steering`: four behaviours, route
window, turn, `SteeringIntegrator`) and `GateWalk` (Q344) landed 2026-09-17 ·
**phase 3** the same day: `WorldSteering` and `CreatureMovementSystem` drive
every creature; `HashVersion` 62.

**Context.** ADR-0155 recorded that DK2 routes over a navigation mesh and moves
by steering, and left the rebuild to the owner. Since then the owner has watched
routes run straight where a grid must bend (Q341) and creatures push each other
(Q345), and every algorithm is read: the triangulation (Q347, Q348), the greedy
two-ended search (Q341), the funnel and gate midpoints (Q342), the behaviours
and their integration (Q343). **The owner decided on 2026-09-16 to rebuild.**

**Decision.** Three phases, each landing tested and the first two unwired.
1. **Router library** in `DK2.Pathfinding`: `INavByteGrid` (the §5.4 byte per
   tile), `NavMesh` (two-triangle reset; maximal uniform rectangles; corners as
   points; sides as constraints inserted by orientation-guided flips; same-byte
   coarsening), `MeshRouter` (min-heap of 1024, key
   `minVertexDist² << (2·cost−2)`, no accumulated cost, run from both ends,
   shorter funnelled route kept), `Funnel` (Route2path) and `GateWalk` (the gate
   re-walk; midpoints of kept gates). Output is waypoints in 1/256-tile units.
2. **Steering library**, after `avoid_walls`, `repel_obstacle`, `follow_path`'s
   body and `grtc:` (Q344) are read: the steering body, four behaviours, the
   combiner and integrator already specified in `navigation-and-steering.md`.
3. **Wiring**: continuous position and velocity on the creature, a waypoint
   window, the movement system replaced, `IPathfinder`'s callers moved to the
   router. `HashVersion` moves and the pin is re-baselined there.

**Consequences.**
- `GridPathfinder` survives only behind `TryFindNearest`, a labelled stand-in:
  DK2 chooses work by kind lists and ring scans (ADR-0058), never by walking
  distance. A target the grid reaches and the mesh cannot (Q28) is skipped.
- Deliberately omitted, because the shipped game never engages them and no route
  changes: edge width classes and mover classes; region ids, which only the
  reachability pre-check reads and a failed search stands in for. Recorded on
  `NavMesh` so nobody mistakes the omission for ignorance.
- Known residuals, each labelled in code: point location is a scan, not the
  original's walk; the constraint-insertion flip order is Sloan's, not the
  original's unread one; `GateWalk` drops kept gates past 256 where the original
  overruns its buffer.
- **Amended 2026-09-18 (Q351).** The whole-map rebuild is now read whole: a
  −256…1280 canvas, the map stamped as one byte-0 rectangle, scanned byte-0
  rectangles skipped, no vertex removal, coarsening by shortest diagonal within
  one byte and never in rock. Level 10's points are ours exactly and 94 % of its
  triangles; corridors match in 84 % of 20,859 requests, against 33 %.
- Priority (4) applies with force: the router **must** be greedy and non-optimal
  in the original's way. A shortest-path router here is a fidelity bug.

## ADR-0158 — Doors enter the navigation byte

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-17 · `HashVersion` 63 · Q353 · Research:
`docs/research/doors-and-traps.md`, `navigation-mesh-and-search.md` §4,
`navigation-captures.md`.

**Context.** The first oracle capture of routing (§7 of the mesh doc) put 968
of DK2's route failures on hero doors that our navigation byte did not know:
the largest measured divergence, and the cost function's door arms had been
read but had nothing to read. The door update, the byte writer and the lock
transition were then read: a completed door is **open** while an eligible
allied creature stands on its tile or beside it, **lock mode** 3 keeps it
shut, and the tile's byte is `owner << 4 | lock bit | tile-tag bit` while
closed and plain floor while open. The cost function stops a mover at any
foreign door and any locked own door when its state passed option bit 7, at a
locked own door only otherwise, and never when option bit 1 is set.

**Decision.**
- `DoorState` gains `LockMode` (authored flag bit 0 → 3) and `Open`, recomputed
  every tick by `DoorSystem` before movement; both are hashed and snapshotted.
- `WorldSteering.Refresh` overlays each closed, completed door's byte
  (`NavBytes.Door`) on the terrain byte; an open door leaves floor.
- `MoverProfile` carries the owner and the option word's three door bits, set
  once per request and kept on the creature (`RouteOptions`) as DK2 keeps them
  at `creature+0x3E6`, so re-requests and wall probes judge doors alike.
- `MeshRouter.TransitionCost(to, from, mover)` gains the door arms as read, and
  the search passes the tile walked into as `to` in both directions, which the
  original's two push orders do and the earlier code did not.
- The alliance test is "same owner": alliances were unbuilt (built in ADR-0159).

**Consequences.**
- Replaying Level 7's log, every one of the 968 door-blocked searches now
  reproduces for a keeper-owned mover, and four more routes agree.
- A creature attacking with option word 0 routes through a closed foreign door,
  as DK2's router does; stopping it there is combat's job, not the router's.
- Which tiles beside a door count, the creature flag the update skips, the
  door type that always reads as locked and the lock transition's callers are
  Q353; until the transition is built no door changes mode after loading.

## ADR-0159 — The rest of the door model: alliances, the lock command, the picked lock

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-18 · `HashVersion` 64 · Research:
`docs/research/doors-and-traps.md`.

**Context.** ADR-0158 built the door update with three pieces missing, each
named there: the alliance test stood in as "same owner", nothing could change a
lock mode after loading, and the lock-pick timer the update reads had neither a
field nor a reader. All three are now read from the binary rather than inferred.
`0x004BF3D0` answers yes for the same player and otherwise returns the byte at
`player+0x1AE+other`; the make and break handlers (`0x00513FF0`, `0x00513F60`)
write **both** players' arrays and nothing else writes them; the lock command
`0x00513800` takes no mode and **toggles** an unlocked door to 3 and any other
to 0; and the update tests the timer at `+0x115` **before** the lock mode, so a
picked lock holds even a mode-3 door open (`0x004A5D52`).

**Decision.**
- `PlayerState.AlliedWith`, one bit per player id, with `WorldState.AreAllied`
  and a symmetric `SetAllied`. `DoorSystem.Eligible` asks it instead of
  comparing owners.
- `SetAllianceCommand` and `AllianceSystem`, ordered before `DoorSystem` so a
  pact made on a tick is honoured on it. One command with a flag where the
  original has two handlers; neither checks that the issuer is one of the pair,
  so neither does this.
- `LockDoorCommand`, applied by `DoorSystem` before it recomputes anything: the
  owner's own door only, and a toggle, which is half of why modes 1 and 2 are
  unreachable.
- `DoorState.LockPickTicks`, counted down one per update ahead of the
  construction bypass and read ahead of the lock mode.

**Consequences.**
- **Nothing starts a picked lock.** Its only writer is `0x004A6DF0`, reached
  from the effect handler `0x00474F80` through an ability descriptor table;
  which ability owns it is UNKNOWN and abilities are unbuilt. The field is
  hashed anyway, on version 53's reasoning: state the simulation can be *given*
  is testable where a hardcoded false is not.
- The duration that writer computes is a product of two globals in
  uninitialised data, so its value stays unread; only the shape is built.
- Trigger action 18 is the third writer of the alliance array (`0x0051DCEB`,
  STRONGLY INFERRED). It has no arm in the executor and gains none here.
- Our eligibility still uses `CreatureDeathRules.IsDown` where DK2 tests
  `CreatureDying` alone, a door wider than the original's by at most the tick
  window in which a creature is out of health and not yet booked as collapsed.

## ADR-0160 — Trigger actions 44 and 45 control saved world gates

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-21 · `HashVersion` 65 · Research:
`docs/research/trigger-dispatch-tables.md`, `creature-anger.md`.

**Context.** Level 1 reaches one action of each type on its first turn and the
executor reported both Partial. Their adjacent world-dispatch arms had not been
read. ADR-0120 also forecast that player action 38 would mutate spell
availability; reading that arm refuted the forecast.

**Decision.** Preserve the world byte's low option bits on `TriggerState`,
initially `0x07` as DK2 initialises them. Type 44 replaces bit 0 and type 45 bit
1; only parameter value 1 enables a bit. Bit 0 gates every simulated anger
delta while leaving mood recomputation intact. Bit 1 is exposed as the ordinary
player-message gate, including messages consumed by keeper AI
(`computer-keeper-messages.md`; corrected 2026-09-28). It drives no queue in
this simulation yet. Hash and snapshot the whole byte.

**Consequences.** Types 44 and 45 leave the Partial census. Level 1's first
turn therefore has five Partial action groups instead of seven. Keeper-spell
availability remains level data: action 38 is a presentation command, not its
writer. The third initially-set bit is retained but unnamed; action 51 and its
consumer remain unimplemented.

## ADR-0161 — Availability is mutable per-player world state

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-21 · `HashVersion` 66 · Research:
`docs/research/trigger-dispatch-tables.md`.

**Context.** The executor's 600-turn corpus census ranks action 6 third among
missing effects by unique reached records. The two larger arms cannot be built:
type 17 writes display-facing slab state with no simulated reader (ADR-0144),
and type 24 still has an unread parameter (Q227). Action 6's world arm and all
five callees establish its complete effect.

**Decision.** Copy each keeper's level availability rows into `PlayerState`.
Action 6 selects room, creature, door, trap or spell by bytes 1 and 2, then
writes state 1 when byte 3 is zero and state 3 otherwise. It changes an existing
row only; a missing row is a successful no-op. Portal unlocks and trigger spell
conditions read the live state. Hash and snapshot every row.

**Consequences.** Action 6 leaves `Partial`: 29 unique records reached during
the measured corpus run now perform their effect. Room building and the
availability modes of conditions 25, 27 and 28 remain unimplemented consumers;
their shipped records do not use those modes. Q226 no longer includes action
6's selectors. `HashVersion` and snapshot format advance together to 66.

## ADR-0162 — A game ends once: `Status`, the heart's fall, and the verdict

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-22 · `HashVersion` 67 · Research:
`docs/research/win-and-defeat.md`.

**Context.** The plan's own words were "no level is winnable": nothing held a
verdict, `WIN_GAME` and `LOSE_GAME` were `Partial`, and a fallen heart had no
state (Q40, Q93, Q207). DK2 keeps one field, `Status` at `player+0x19A`, written
by one routine that returns if it is already set. 39 of the 40 shipped `WIN_GAME`
records hang off flag or timer conditions the executor already evaluates.

**Decision.** `PlayerState.Status` takes DK2's codes — 0 playing, 1 conquered,
2 won, 3 lost — and `WorldState.EndGame` writes it once. Actions 10 and 11 are
performed for the player of the player or creature tree that reached them and
refused in a world tree, as the dispatchers do. The heart is health on the
player, from `DungeonHeartObjectHealth`: `DamageHeart` stamps `KilledByPlayerId`
at zero; `DungeonHeartSystem`, last in the tick, regenerates once a second, ruins
the room one turn after death (`+0x9A` bit 0, Q263), turns a stamped killer into
*lost* or *conquered* by side, and awards the win to the last keeper standing.
A ruined heart stores no gold and can be claimed.

**Consequences.** Every campaign level's win is reachable by the executor.
Snapshot format and `HashVersion` advance to 67; six test fixtures gain the two
heart variables the shipped global table always carries. Not built and named
so: what a defeat does to creatures, rooms and gold (Q358, built below), and alliance
propagation of verdicts (Q359). Nothing in the tick order damages a heart until
combat lands.

**Amended 2026-09-23 (Q358 read).** The consequences are built, hash-neutral, as
`DefeatRules` run by `DungeonHeartSystem` every turn a killer is stamped — DK2's general
arm `0x004DAA10`: the heart's gold to neutral piles, every room but the heart and the
hero gates to the neutral player, roomless owned tiles to their destroyed terrain on the
death turn; workers killed and the rest set leaving from the fifth turn (`LeavingRules`,
the deserter's walk shared). The local player's collapse `0x004DAE40` is research only
(`win-and-defeat.md` §7). Combat has landed on the heart since ADR-0164.

## ADR-0163 — Acquisition is `SelectAVictim`; the Blocker arm is built first

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-22 · `HashVersion` 68 · Research:
`docs/research/combat-acquisition.md`.

**Context.** Target selection's five arms were read (combat-target-selection.md)
but not the routine that dispatches to them, when it runs, or what happens to
its answer. Reading it named it — DK2's own `SelectAVictim` — and showed six
scans, a tick throttle, a per-tick attackability recompute and the enemy heart
entering as its nearest Arch Pillar. Nothing in the simulation could yet decide
to fight.

**Decision.** `CombatSystem` runs `ProcessFight` for every unpossessed creature
before movement and the job systems, as DK2's creature update does: neutral
creatures never look; the gate and the ten-tick (Imp: four) standing throttle
are DK2's. `SelectAVictim` is built for `FightStyle.Blocker` only — the shared
scan with score `d`, the alignment discount, `IsAttackable` as a predicate,
sight by DK2's line walk and reach by DK2's route sum, the route check, the
final gate, melee commit, registration in the target's eight melee slots and
`AttackRangeSquared`. A creature that engages enters `CreatureActivity.Fighting`
(state 199), holds its target while it exists and is attackable, and is skipped
by every job system. The other four arms, the spell survey, the who-attacks-me,
door and pillar scans and the flee check are named in the document and not
built, so nothing half-built runs.

**Consequences.** A Blocker within four tiles of an enemy it can see, or walk to
in under four tiles, now engages it; nothing yet swings, so health is untouched
until `spFighting` is read and built. Snapshot format and `HashVersion` advance
to 68. The fixture's Bile Demon takes its shipped `Blocker` style and gains a
`Knight`. Open: Q360–Q366.

## ADR-0164 — Melee lands: `spFighting`'s two clocks, the approach, the answer, the heart

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-22 · `HashVersion` 69 · Research:
`docs/research/combat-fight-state.md`.

**Context.** ADR-0163 let a Blocker choose an enemy and stand. `spFighting`
(DK2's own name) was then read end to end: a melee swing is creature action 17,
started at most every `MeleeRecharge` ticks and landing `def+0x5CA` ticks later
on the target it began at, with no range test at the blow; out of reach the
creature looks again every tick and routes to the target's position; a struck
creature turns on its attacker only when its own target is already fought by
more than one; the health routine takes the attacker's player as the source.

**Decision.** `FightRules` and `CombatSystem.Fight` run that order for melee.
`MeleeHitDelay` is parsed from file `0xCF9` (its shipped name stays Q336) and
both clocks are kept in ticks. The blow is `MeleeDamageRules.Blow` with no
stance, the bearing from target to attacker and no player modifier, into
`CreatureHealthRules.Apply`; a heart takes it through `WorldState.DamageHeart`
with the heart's ring tile standing in for the Arch Pillar (Q363). The four
fighting arms' scores are built so every fight style but `NonFighter` fights.
Retaliation is built for melee with the spell survey replaced by melee.

**Consequences.** A level can now be lost and won by play: creatures fall to
blows and hearts to creatures. Nobody flees, celebrates or casts yet, and those
are named (Q367–Q369). Snapshot format and `HashVersion` advance to 69; the
fixture's Goblin and Bile Demon take their shipped recharge; the two-keepers
scenario spaces its rivals beyond sight so it stays about work.

**Amended 2026-09-23.** Gate B corrected against the disassembly: a zero stamp swings
at once, and the recharge — like the spell cooldown — divides by the work rate and its
enhancement (`EfficiencyRules.Modifier`, 0.8 fresh), so a fresh creature waits a quarter
longer than the file's seconds (`creature-status-effects.md` §4, `CombatRules.Scaled`).

**Amended 2026-09-23 (Q363 read).** The pillar is a proxy: DK2's health routine hands a
blow on an Arch Pillar to the owner's heart routine `0x004DA200`, which adds it flat and
stamps the source; regeneration goes through the same routine with the owner's tag.
`DamageHeart` was already that; `RegenerateHeart` now stamps the owner
(`win-and-defeat.md` §3.1). The ring tile still stands in for the pillar object.

## ADR-0165 — Fear: threat radiated every tick, the back-off, the withdrawal

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-22 · `HashVersion` 70 · Research:
`docs/research/combat-fear.md`.

**Context.** Fighters fought to the death. The binary's fear was read: every
tick a creature radiates its level-scaled `Threat`, split among its engagements,
into the `TempFear` of each opponent it can see; its own `CurrentFear` is last
tick's intake scaled by its distance from its heart, nothing beside it; three
ticks over its level-scaled `Fear`, with an escape tile free, it enters state 203
for a `BackOffTimer` between the two BackOff variables, shorter the more afraid,
then runs for its lair, its heart two tiles off, one of three random rooms or a
neighbouring tile; under a third of its health and over five tiles from its
heart it runs at once, from the fight or from the acquirer. The fight's entry
sets the run speed, not a cue.

**Decision.** `FearRules` builds that order, run by `CombatSystem` after each
creature's fight processing. `CreatureActivity.Fleeing` is state 203,
`Withdrawing` the walk to state 202; `Running` is the body's speed cap. The step
back is a short route away from the target, and a state ending lets the
engagement go — both named as approximations (Q373). Heroes fear in full and
never withdraw for want of a creature flag and hero gates (Q372); the Scout's
alarm (Q374; built in ADR-0166, routed as read in ADR-0332) and three per-type owner modifiers (Q375) are not built.

**Consequences.** Frightened creatures back off and run; a fight near one's own
heart holds and one far from it breaks. `HashVersion` 70; the fixture's Knight and
Warlock are fearless so the retaliation tests keep their premise; the fixture
carries the BackOff and guard-room variables.

## ADR-0166 — The worker's arm: fight at the heart, withdraw from a hero, or raise the alarm

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-23 · `HashVersion` 71 · Research:
`docs/research/combat-alarm.md`.

**Context.** Imps and the other `NonFighter` never reacted to an enemy. The arm
was read to its exits: within 3.6 tiles of its own heart a worker judges every
hostile creature by plain distance — an Imp within a tile — and fights; elsewhere
it looks only at heroes in sight that have no target or target it, and never
fights them: away from its rooms it withdraws; near them it counts heads within
five tiles and, outnumbered, a `Scout` runs to its nearest room and raises the
alarm — that room's creatures run to the hero until their `Threat` covers the
deficit and stand thirty ticks there acquiring by the ordinary scan. An earlier
reading had taken the alarm's call for a commit to a fight.

**Decision.** `CombatTargetRules.NonFighter` builds the arm and `FearRules` the
alarm: `RaisingAlarm` is state 6 toward 251, `Reporting` state 6 toward 254 and 254
itself; a room job whose tile lies in the alarm's room stands for `RoomId`; the
responders run at their own speed where DK2 gives them the raiser's; state 252
ends at once. The room's spot, `state+0x3C` and action 79 (Q391) are not
modelled. **Amended 2026-09-23:** the escape byte is the candidate's base creature
type (Q390, Codex): an enemy Imp is judged by the shared template anywhere — built.

**Consequences.** Imps scatter from heroes, defend the heart, and call a room to
arms when outnumbered — the last visible piece of creature-side combat before the
spell arms. `HashVersion` 71.

## ADR-0167 — The attack spells and their shots: a cast is action 16 firing a shot thing

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-23 · `HashVersion` 72 · Research:
`docs/research/combat-spells.md`, `docs/research/shots.md`.

**Context.** Every creature fought with melee because the spell survey was not
built, and a caster without shots would have stood at range firing nothing. Both
halves were read to the byte: the survey keeps the castable attack spell whose
next-ready time is latest; in reach and off cooldown the caster stamps the slot
and starts action 16, whose handler fires a shot of the spell's `ShotTypeId`
`ShotDelay` ticks later, aimed with a lead of the target's last move per tile; the
shot flies `Speed` position units a tick, hits the first thing of its collide class
within its radius, never its caster, deals `ShotData1` **flat, unscaled by level**
through the melee blow's health routine, and chains hit and death shots that
inherit its data words.

**Decision.** `SpellRules` (survey, cooldown, ranges), `FightRules.StartCast` /
`CastFires` / `FireSpell`, `CombatSystem.CannotCast`; `ShotState` as a world
collection with its own id counter, `ShotSystem` after movement, `ShotRules`
(launch, finder, contact and area damage, chaining). Creature state gains the
three stamps, the spell slot, the action's kind and slot, and its last position.
Approximations are named in Q398: flat flight, the overlap test, the origin
vector, a stopped shot's countdown, the idle fallback, the thing order.

**Consequences.** Warlocks, Mistresses, Dark Elves, Salamanders and every other
caster fight at range with the shipped spells; a Support never melees. The
status spells (Freeze, Slow, Haste, Heal, Armour, Invulnerable, Invisible,
Lightning, Drain) flew and landed doing nothing until ADR-0168 built their
creature side; the friendly arm waits on the buff table (Q394). `HashVersion` 72.

## ADR-0168 — Status effects are tick countdowns on the creature, read by the health routine and the gates

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-23 · `HashVersion` 73 · Research:
`docs/research/creature-status-effects.md`, `docs/research/shots.md` §8.

**Context.** ADR-0167 landed the status shots and left their handlers stubs:
Freeze, Slow, Haste, Armour, Invulnerable, Invisible, Lightning, Drain and Poison
Spit flew and did nothing. The creature side was read to the byte: one routine
steps every status word down a tick and is skipped whole for `IsHorny`; the
health routine scales every negative change by 128ths — stunned +128, frozen +32,
armoured or possessed −64 — and refuses `IsHorny`, `OnlyAttackableByHorny` and a
creature in the hand; freeze is state 218 standing while its word runs; Lightning
and the Reaper Fireball stun into state 255 for `StunDuration`; Haste and Slow
pin the body speed between a quarter of the walk and four tiles a tick; Invisible
drops the attackers and clears the targetable bit; Poison bleeds a fixed amount a
tick while not frozen; fire is display only. A hit writes the struck thing into
the shot's target word before the handler runs.

**Decision.** `StatusEffectRules` holds the multipliers (`Hurt`), the setters and
the speed cap; `CreatureStatusSystem` runs the countdowns before `CombatSystem`;
`ShotRules.Process` dispatches `ShotProcessFlags` events 0x40 (first tick) and
0x4 (thing struck) to the nine process types with a creature side;
`CreatureActivity.Frozen` and `Stunned` are standing states the job systems leave
alone (`CombatRules.Preoccupied`) and the fight gate refuses; `IsAttackable`
refuses an invisible creature; the melee blow, contact and area damage refuse an
invulnerable one and pass through `Hurt`. Ten words enter `CreatureState`, the
hash and the snapshot. Approximations are named in Q399.

**Consequences.** A Mistress's Freeze holds its target forty ticks at
five-quarters damage; a Warlock's Armour halves damage for twenty seconds; a
Thief vanishes from every attacker for fifteen; Lightning stuns and doubles the
damage that follows; the Reaper Fireball doubles its own. `CreatureFlags2` bit 0
is Lightning immunity (Q210). `HashVersion` 73.

## ADR-0169 — State 8 is a flag on the fighter, and a kill ends in a fixed pause

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-23 · `HashVersion` 74 · Research:
`docs/research/combat-approach-and-victory.md`.

**Context.** Our fighter re-routed to its target every tick and let a dead
target go at once. DK2's walk to a fight is its own state, 8: it chooses an
ordinary creature target afresh every tick and ends when the choice changes,
runs the fear counter without the low-health withdrawal, gives up a fleeing or
withdrawing target after `GoodCreaturesChaseEnemyDurationSeconds` (3) or
`EvilCreaturesChaseEnemyDurationSeconds` (7), ends strictly in reach with line
of sight, and refreshes its route every tenth call even when the target has not
moved — a Flanker aiming behind the target. A kill leaves every attacker the
`0xF` nibble; `spFighting` then celebrates in state 260 for one animation
instance, or for `NeedBodyForFightIdle` walks to a corpse within `0x2000`
squared and celebrates there; the celebrant is attackable and does not turn.

**Decision.** `ApproachRules` runs while `CreatureState.Approaching` is set,
entered by `CombatSystem.Fight` out of reach; `VictoryRules` holds the death
unlink, the victory arm, `Celebrating` and `GoingToBody`; both are states the job
systems leave alone and the retaliation path returns from. The pause is a fixed
8 ticks, a stated stand-in until slot 35's length is known (Q376); the other
approximations — velocity for facing, the engagement let go, the body's arrival
reach, a corpse under any owner — are Q400. Six words enter the state, hash and
snapshot.

**Consequences.** A fighter now walks to a stale point for up to ten ticks when
its target moves, and a hero gives up a fleeing creature in three seconds where
an evil one chases for seven. A killer stands two seconds after a kill, open to
a blow it will not answer. The old per-tick re-route had crawled: targets now
arrive, so a struck Warlock turns to its fists as DK2's retaliation says, and
two spell tests freeze their targets to keep the caster casting. `HashVersion` 74.

## ADR-0170 — The friendly spell arm: the last castable buff, on the nearest own fighter under a quarter health

**Status.** Accepted 2026-09-23 · `HashVersion` 74 (no state added) · Research:
`docs/research/spell-friendly-arm.md`, `docs/research/shots.md` §4a and §8.

**Context.** Heal, Haste, Cast Armour, Invulnerable and the Invisibles flew and
landed since ADR-0168 but nobody cast them: the friendly survey was unread until
Codex's Q394 (merged, reviewed). It settles: the survey keeps the **last**
castable friendly slot; Invisible is cast on the caster alone; every other buff
goes to the nearest of the caster's own creatures — the caster included, allies
never — in the Combat state category, under a quarter of its level-scaled
health, that the spell's applicability routine accepts (Haste: no speed effect;
Heal: under half health; Armour, Invulnerable, Invisible: their word zero); the
cast is made once and the target let go. `spFighting` step 8 makes a Support
re-acquire every tick, which is how a healer in melee reach turns to its ally.
Reading Heal's chain reached two more facts: type 34 moves the shot onto its
target, type 3 heals the lesser of the data word and the missing health (and
Disruption's five-percent floor); the overlap test is a box half the radii's
sum wide with the shot's radius doubled.

**Decision.** `SpellRules.SurveyFriendly` and `BuffApplies`; scan F and
`EngageAlly` in `CombatTargetRules` after the hostile scans; `FightRules.Reacquire`
(step 8) and `CastOnAlly`; `ShotRules.Overlaps`, `ModifyHealth` and the instant
handler; the finder admits the caster when it is the target. The fixture gains a
Priest (Haste, Armour, Heal) and a Thief (Invisible). No creature state is added.

**Consequences.** A Priest heals a fighter under a quarter health for the missing
amount, then armours it, then hastens it; a Thief in a fight vanishes on its own
spell; a hurt fighter at half health gets nothing. A Support that was struck turns
to melee for one tick and is back on its spell the next. A Haste at 3686 units a
tick can pass a standing ally, as DK2's per-tick finder would (Q401, an owner
question). Not built: the Support's escape gate on the survey, the Turncoat, pit
and torture refusals, the Imp's Teleport and Haste paths (Q401).

## ADR-0171 — A cell bites in fours, and anger cools in seven states not three
**Date:** 2026-09-23 · **Status:** accepted · closes Q402, closes Q123's live divergence · Research: `docs/research/state-category-hooks.md` §3, `state-categories.md` §7.2, `prison.md`, `creature-anger.md`

**Context.** Reading all 36 state-category hook bodies reached two mechanics this project had already built, and both were built differently from the original. The stop rule in that brief recorded them as Q402 rather than changing behaviour on a research branch.

**Decision.** Both are corrected to the original.

1. **The prison charges in lumps.** `0x0047B7C0` reloads `variable19 << 2` and applies `4 × PrisonModifyCreatureHealthPerSecond` (−12) once every four game seconds, where ours took −3 every second. The average is identical and the moment of death is not, so a prisoner dies on a four-second boundary and a keeper's chicken has a coarser window. The phase is per creature, set by the enter hook at the moment of imprisonment, so two prisoners taken a second apart wither on different seconds — that needs state, and it is `CreatureState.PrisonWitherTicks`.
2. **A cell angers as well as withers.** The same hook adds `ModifyAngerInCompanyOfHatedCreaturesPerSecond` (150, and 100 on campaign level 1) to bucket 0 with complaint selector 9, in the same breath as the health. It is **not** scaled by the four-second interval: the variable passes through whole, so a prisoner gains 150 an application, not 600. This is the variable's *second* reader; the mixed-alignment room rule is the other and is still unbuilt.
3. **Cooling is category-gated, not bed-gated.** The lair effect `0x004DFF00` is called from the per-tick hooks of categories 6, 9 and 10 — seven states: 79 looking for the Lair, 80 making a home, 81 going to bed, 82/83/84 sleeping, 85 sulking. It tests nothing about tile or bed, so awake creatures cool too. `LairRules.CoolsAngerInLair` replaces `AsleepInOwnBed` at the anger site.

**Consequences.**
- **Healing is deliberately not widened.** The same routine heals behind a predicate that has not been read, so whether an awake creature gains health in a lair stays UNKNOWN (Q123). `CreatureHealthRules` keeps `AsleepInOwnBed`.
- **One known over-cool.** `CreatureActivity.SeekingLair` folds states 79 and 80 together with the walk between them, which DK2 spends in a movement state that does not cool. It resolves when travel retires into the utility slot (ADR-0135); until then ours cools for the length of that walk.
- The old cooling rule had a test, and it only ever covered the sleeping case — which is why the divergence survived from 2026-09-07 with a green suite. The widened rule is pinned on the awake arms and on a negative (`AtWork` at a non-lair job) so it cannot degrade into "cooling always happens".
- `HashVersion` and `FormatVersion` **77**, pin `0x2EC7D308858908C2`. `Dk2TerrainFixture` gains variable 78, which only a prison reads.

## ADR-0172 — Rebellion is not a roll: the Portal first, and turning Good is the fallback
**Date:** 2026-09-23 · **Status:** accepted · closes Q116, sharpens Q204, opens Q410–Q413 · Research: `docs/research/rebellion.md`

**Context.** `CreatureAngerSystem` has picked angry job 16 since ADR-0061 and done nothing with it, and the three `Rebel*Percentage` variables plus `RebelMaxFollowers` were parsed and read by nothing. Q116 held two irreconcilable accounts of what rebelling is: the wiki's, that it is the fallback when the exit is unreachable, and the creature record's, that `AngryJobs` is a weighted table. Job 16's handler `0x00475170` and state 271's handler `0x004750B0` were read in full to settle it.

**Decision.** Rebellion is built as the original has it, and the original has no roll in it.

1. **Job 16 tries the Portal first.** Three guards — not a captive, not a Combat Pit fighter, not in the Hand — then the nearest Portal belonging to the creature's *own* keeper, routed to in state 194 `leaving Dungeon`, which is the state job 10 `Leave` also sets. A rebel with a way out is a deserter.
2. **With no way out it turns Good.** State 271, a 30-tick deadline — 7.5 game seconds, which is why `RebelCountdownTicks` runs per tick rather than with the anger ladder — then the owner becomes the hero player and the creature is given job 19 `KillPlayer` naming the keeper it left. Both are one call in DK2, into the remembered-job triple at `creature+0x409`.
3. **Q116 is answered by separating the levels.** The table picks between jobs 10 and 16 and is the record's; portal-then-Good is inside job 16 and is an engine rule. Both accounts were true of different things.
4. **The four `Rebel*` variables are dead.** Each global's address occurs exactly once in the whole image, at its loader store, against two positive controls that returned their documented reader counts. `RebelLeader` is written twice and tested nowhere, so the follower mechanic the names describe was never wired.

**Consequences.**
- **Job 16 probes before it commits, and job 10 does not.** `Leave` releases the bed the moment it decides, which is DK2's job 10 setting state 194 blind. Job 16 checks first, so a rebel that cannot leave keeps its bed. That asymmetry is the original's and is the one place the two jobs visibly differ.
- **`RebelActive` and `RebelLeader` are recorded, not modelled** (`+0x3E6` bits 3 and 4, DK2's own dumper names). Bit 4 has no reader anywhere; both of bit 3's readers are unbuilt here. Naming bit 3 closes an UNKNOWN in `state-category-hooks.md`, and why category 26's leave hook clears it is Q411.
- **`KillPlayer` is remembered and not performed**; job 19 has no handler. Creature action 43 and notification type 19 are not built either.
- **Ours, not DK2's:** a world without the hero player has nobody to defect to, so the countdown stalls and says so. DK2 reads the id from a global that always names a player.
- **Two loose ends in the chooser close on the way.** Its per-creature abort flag is `InHand`, which this project already had from the other side. And Q204's `IsHorny` diversion, answered in ADR-0145 without reading what it *does*, lands an angry Horned Reaper in state 238 — a category-28 state losing 10 health a tick. That is where "an angry Horny kills itself" starts; unbuilt, and out of scope here.
- `HashVersion` and `FormatVersion` **78**, pin `0x00C68551383ADF89`.

## ADR-0173 — A bed is a hospital: a wounded creature sleeps until it is whole
**Date:** 2026-09-23 · **Status:** accepted · closes Q403 · Research: `docs/research/lair-acquisition.md` §9

**Context.** Codex's read of states 79–84 reached a mechanic this project had already built and found it built differently, and the brief's stop rule recorded it as Q403 rather than changing behaviour on a research branch — the same route Q402 took the day before. State 83's exit test was re-derived instruction by instruction before merging: it reads `SleepNeeded`, stays while positive, then compares current health against the level-scaled maximum and stays while it is short.

**Decision.** Waking requires both. `LairRules.HasSleptEnough` takes the `GameDatabase` and returns true only when `SleepTicks` has reached `TimeSleep` **and** `Health` has reached `CreatureHealthRules.MaxHealth`. A wounded creature sleeps past its record's `TimeSleep` until it is whole.

**Consequences.**
- **It only became visible when combat landed.** Before ADR-0163–0170 nothing wounded a creature that then went to bed, so a time-only wake and DK2's agreed on every run. It is live on every level now, and a Goblin that lies down at 300 of 1500 is in bed for twelve seconds where it used to be up at nine.
- **A creature that cannot heal to full would sleep for ever.** So would DK2's; losing the bed is the way out of both, and `CreatureSleepSystem` already wakes on `BedStillValid` failing.
- **The pinned world exercises none of it**, so the literal moved only because `HashVersion` is folded into the hash. That is the point of the bump: two builds that disagree about when a creature wakes must not compare states. Verified by flipping the predicate off and watching both tests fail, so neither is a vacuous pin (Q206's lesson).
- **Not adopted:** DK2 counts `SleepNeeded` **down** from `TimeSleep` in the category hook, gated on the state id, where ours counts `SleepTicks` up in the system. Same clock read the other way; it costs a hashed field to change and buys nothing until the state machine is wired, so it waits for ADR-0135.
- `HashVersion` and `FormatVersion` **79**, pin `0x6ACE9686C2A3E64E`.

## ADR-0174 — One door into the state machine, built before anything walks through it
**Date:** 2026-09-23 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0135 (step one), opens Q414 · Research: `docs/research/creature-state-table.md` §2.1, §2.2

**Context.** ADR-0135 made DK2's state id the authoritative representation and retires the 30-value `CreatureActivity` enum one group at a time. The pieces it needs now all exist: the 281-state table, the 32 categories, the resume pair on `CreatureState`, and the transition rule with all 78,680 ordered pairs resolved and pinned (Q300). What did not exist is the one thing that makes an incremental retirement safe — a single place a state id may change.

**Decision.** `CreatureStateMachine` is that place, and it is built **now, while nothing writes a state id**.

1. **`TrySetState` is DK2's `SetState`** (`0x00476D30`): it classifies through `CreatureStateTransitions`, refuses an illegal move, and returns whether the move was taken. A refusal is an answer, not an error — the creature keeps the state it has, which is the original's behaviour.
2. **`Begin` is the only unjudged entry**, and it throws on a creature that already has a state. Without that, a second `Begin` would reach any state from any state and the gate would be decoration.
3. **Entering a utility state writes `StateBeforeUtilityState`** and leaving one clears it. That half of the resume pair is CONFIRMED; the other half is not (below).
4. **An architecture test forbids every other write.** `NothingOutsideTheStateMachineAssignsADk2StateId` sweeps `src/` and exempts three files: the gate, the field's declaration, and the snapshot reader, which restores a state some gate already allowed. It asserts the exemptions still match, so a pattern that silently stopped matching fails rather than passing everything.

**Consequences.**
- **It adds no behaviour and is inert by construction.** That is the argument for it, not against: each of the twenty-nine remaining retirements that landed without it would be an opportunity to invent a transition rule DK2 does not have, and AGENTS.md forbids inventing what can be researched.
- **One deviation, and it is ours (Q414).** `CreatureStateTransitions.Classify` **throws** when a creature is in a travel state with no resume target — there is no state −1 to look up. DK2 presumably never asks, because the slot is written before the travel state is entered, but nothing has read *who* writes it. Until then this project can reach the unset case, so the gate judges the travel state by itself. Pinned by its own test so it cannot later be mistaken for the original.
- **The gate is not a second opinion.** Every ordered pair of the 281 states is driven through both the rule and the gate, and a single disagreement fails — 78,680 pairs, so the wrapper cannot quietly add a rule.
- **No hash change.** Nothing hashed moved and no behaviour did; the pin is untouched. The next step, retiring `Sleeping` onto state 83, is the first one that bumps it.

## ADR-0175 — The resume slot has no "unset", so the gate stops pretending it does
**Date:** 2026-09-23 · **Status:** accepted · follows ADR-0174, applies Q414 · Research: `docs/research/travel-states.md` §2–§4

**Context.** ADR-0174 shipped the transition gate a few hours before Q414 was answered, and guessed at the one thing it could not read: what a travel state holds when no errand is waiting. It used −1, which is not a state, so `CreatureStateTransitions.Classify` threw and the gate needed a fallback that judged a travel state by itself. That fallback was recorded as ours and pinned by a test. Q414's read retires it.

**Decision.** Follow the original exactly.

1. **Neither slot carries a sentinel.** DK2's state-object constructor writes 0 to `StateBeforeUtilityState` and `UtilityNewState`, and every arrival writes **1** to the resume slot. Both default to 0 here. `Dk2StateId` keeps its −1, which is a *migration* sentinel — no activity has retired onto this creature yet — and not a claim about DK2.
2. **`BeginTravel` and `Arrive` model the two route helpers and the arrival branch.** The caller's whole contribution in the original is one call with a target, a resume state and an option word: the helper enters the travel state and *then* writes the slot, and the mover hands over and resets the slot to 1. Neither is a caller's job, so neither is exposed as one.
3. **Two things that look like oversights are reproduced.** Leaving a utility state does **not** clear the saved caller, so the save goes stale and the rule keeps judging by it. And a travel-to-travel move recurses through `SetState(1)` first, so the save ends up 1 rather than the walk it came from.
4. **The fallback is deleted**, with the test that pinned it.

**Consequences.**
- **The handover can never be refused by the rule alone**, and a test now says so over all 281 resume states. Leaving a travel state is judged by the resume state, and the target *is* the resume state, so the comparison is a state against itself. Every refusal the original checks for comes from the enter hook of the resume's category — which nothing here has yet, and which is why the branch looked live.
- `HashVersion` and `FormatVersion` **80**, pin `0xF53826B464578C5B`. A composition bump: both fields hold their default for the whole pinned run.
- **This is what the re-derivation practice is for.** ADR-0174 was reviewed, tested and committed, and was still wrong in three places — the sentinel, the stale save, and the travel-to-travel case. All three were found by reading the original rather than by a failing test, because no test this project could have written would have caught them.

## ADR-0176 — Eating is the first errand on DK2's own state ids
**Date:** 2026-09-23 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0135 (step two, first slice) · Research: `docs/research/travel-states.md` §8, `eating.md` §2

**Context.** With the gate built (ADR-0174), corrected to the read protocol (ADR-0175) and Q414 answered, the thirteen travelling activities can retire onto the utility pair. Each needs the DK2 state its original caller passes as the resume, and for most of the thirteen that mapping is not written down: `travel-states.md` §9 notes that the 138 route-helper call sites "are reproduced by the caller scan and not copied here". Eating is the exception — Codex traced it end to end, 91 → 7 → 92 → 6 → 93 → 94 — so it goes first, as the pattern the rest will copy.

**Decision.**
1. **The state id rides beside the activity.** `CreatureEatSystem` writes the chain through `CreatureStateMachine` at the points our activity changes: into 91 from idle; `BeginTravel(7, 92)` for the hatchery; `BeginTravel(6, 93)` for the bird; `Arrive` at each; 94 after the meal; 92 again or 1. Behaviour is still driven by `Activity`, so nothing a player sees changes.
2. **The room helper's shortcut is reproduced.** A creature already standing in a hatchery takes DK2's already-inside path — `SetState(1)`, then 92, no walk — rather than a walk of length zero.
3. **The migration rule: a creature holds a state id only while it is in a retired activity.** `CreatureStateMachine.Release` hands the id back. The eat system releases on leaving the chain, and at the top of every pass it releases any creature whose activity is no longer an eating one — the hand, a fight and a death still set `Activity` directly, and would otherwise leave a creature holding a state it is not in. `Release` is a shim, not DK2, and goes when the last activity retires.
4. **A refusal is reported, not forced.** The whole chain is legal under DK2's rule — checked against the gate before building — so a refused move would mean the mapping is wrong. It emits `state_refused` and the creature keeps its state, as the original would.

**Consequences.**
- **This is the first time DK2's transition rule has met a real errand**, and it said yes to every step. That is corroboration between two independent reads: the rule from the table and the chain from the handlers.
- **Pinned by the trace, not by the hash.** The pinned world never grows hungry, so the literal moved on the version alone. `TheWalksAreDk2sStateSevenToTheRoomAndStateSixToTheBird` asserts the sequence using the saved caller as evidence, because states inside one tick are transient; it was verified to fail with the two travel states swapped.
