  differs from the capture (Q507).

## ADR-0315 — A room drag is priced whole before a tile is laid
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `rooms-and-gold.md`, *What a room costs*; `room-slab-chain.md` §2

**Context.** Level 3's recording: the player drags a 12-tile Workshop at 1009 with 3290 gold
and again at 1073 with 7181, and DK2 places nothing either time; the same drag at 1100 with
7667 places all twelve, and a one-tile drag between them costs 600. Ours charged per tile
and laid what it could afford, so it held four Workshop tiles at 1009 and twelve at 1073,
91 turns before DK2, and refused the player's third drag as occupied. The pre-check
`0x004C5A20` counts the tiles the placement predicate accepts and compares their cost with
the player's money before the wave `0x004C7380` starts (knowledge base; message `0x37`).

**Decision.** `RoomBuildSystem` counts the placeable tiles of a `BuildRoomCommand` first and
refuses the whole order, charging nothing, when `cost × count` exceeds the keeper's gold.
The per-tile charge stays for what passes. The count is of placeable tiles, not the
rectangle's area: the recording cannot tell the two apart (every refused drag was wholly
placeable) and the record reads "the tiles that may be placed".

**Consequences.** No state changes; `HashVersion` stays 149. `RoomTests` gains the whole-drag
refusal and the placeable-count pricing; `AKeeperWhoCanAffordSomeTilesGetsSomeTiles` and the
`build_a_treasury` scenario pinned the refuted partial build and now expect the refusal.
Level 3's drag at 1009 is now refused as DK2's is; at 1073 ours still places (DK2 had 7181
against 7200), so the richer economy is the next divergence there. Measured with ADR-0316 on
2c6ea95, seeds 1–20: Level 1 19/20, wins 1764–2016, unchanged; Level 2 9/20 → 7/20, all in
the ten Library seeds, wins 2980–3560 (DK2: 1 of 2 Library seeds, at 3421).

## ADR-0316 — A portal does not read the creature-availability table
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `portals.md`, *How they compose*; `binary-entrance.md` §1

**Context.** Level 3's trigger 79 fires at the start and makes the Firefly, Goblin and Warlock
UNAVAILABLE for player 3 — the campaign's only three disabling action-6 records. DK2's portal
still produced a Firefly at 1002, Goblins at 1506 and 1694 and Warlocks from 2398. Ours sent
only Trolls, the one pooled type the script never disabled, and reached five creatures at
2172 against DK2's 1506, which is the condition that starts the level's hero chain. The pick
`0x004DBF90`, decompiled whole, tests the pool through `0x00506400` (a type's remaining count
is non-zero), the two creature flags, `Creature_IsAttractedByDungeon` and the capacity. It
never touches the player's creature table at `+0x4E/+0x52`. The gate was an inference from
Level 1 unlocking exactly one creature, which Level 1's pool explains on its own.

**Decision.** `PortalSystem.Pick` drops the `IsUnlocked` gate. The table stays per player
and action 6 still writes it, for its other readers. `ACreatureThisLevelHasNotUnlockedNeverArrives`
pinned the refuted gate and is replaced by `ACreatureMadeUnavailableStillComesThroughThePortal`.

**Consequences.** No state changes. Every shipped level pools exactly the creatures it marks
AVAILABLE, so only Level 3's three disables change behaviour. Each portal roll now emits a
`roll` event naming the candidates and each pooled type's refusing gate. Level 3 against the
seed 01 recording, with ADR-0315: arrivals 975/1327/1479/1667 (DK2 1002/1354/1506/1694),
five creatures at 1480 (1506), the hero chain's timer at 1976 (1998), the final party at 3176
(3198); the win at 3683 is not reached by 3704 because that party's two Thieves outlive DK2's.
Open: DK2's pool is a draining count the creator decrements (Q474), and the portal tally fell
from 6 to 5 when the Firefly died at 1796 (Q508), which is why our later arrivals drift late.

## ADR-0323 — A withdrawal aims at the room's position word, and a heart's sits past its centre
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `combat-fear.md` §5; `room-object.md`; Q515

**Context.** Level 3's hero phase diverged before the heart fight. DK2's first Dwarf party
(1291) stands in the one corridor between the gold seam at (31,20) and the dungeon from 1386
to 1604; every imp carrying gold meets it, withdraws, re-chooses its mine task and walks back
into it, so nobody deposits (the Heart sits at 15,500 for 650 turns) and the Dwarves, with no
target left in sight, go back to their action point and reach the heart only at 1825. Ours
sent every withdrawing imp to the Heart's corners, so the Dwarves followed the stream into the
heart's defenders and died at 1605 and 1699, 330 turns early, while our economy ran on. The
capture shows where DK2's imps landed: the heart 6 times in 21, other rooms 15. The withdraw
state (`0x004611D0`, read in `combat-fear.md` §5) aims two tiles off the heart's `+0x27/+0x29`
word on each axis, each sign a `random(2)`, and falls to a random room when the point does not
route. Three captures put a 5×5 heart's word one tile past its centre — Level 3 (27,37) for the
heart at (24,34) — so three of its four points are reinforced wall. Ours aimed at the true
centre, where all four points are heart floor.

**Decision.** `RoomInstance.CentreFieldX/Y` is the room word: the bounding box's centre rounded
down, one tile further on each axis for a Dungeon Heart — STRONGLY INFERRED, from three captured
5×5 hearts and no read of the writer (Q515). `FearRules.Withdraw` step 3 draws a heart as
`0x004C6460` does (`random(count)`, one draw even for one heart), aims at that word ±2 and
falls through when the point does not route; step 4's room centres use the same word.

**Consequences.** No state changes. `TheWithdrawalRunsForTheHeart_TwoTilesOffOnEachAxis`
pinned the centre and is replaced by the word version plus the fall-through and the word test.
The withdraw spends one more random draw, so every replay shifts. Measured on 7b66fd7, seeds
1–20: Level 1 20/20 (1760–1976, was 1760–2000), Level 2 7/20 (seeds 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 16, 18;
was 3, 7, 9, 10, 15, 18, 19), both unchanged in count. Level 3 against seed 01: our imps now
land on DK2's seven tiles, gold deliveries stop from 1500 to 1700 as DK2's do, the first
Dwarves die at 1860 and 1892 (DK2 1937 and 1943; before 1605 and 1699), the chain's Dwarf at
1968 (DK2 1998; before 2096). The win at 3683 is still not reached: the final party's Thieves
outlive DK2's. Open: why the heart's word is one past its centre (Q515); the hero job's return
to its action point. Reviewed against the binary (2026-10-02): step 3 and the single draw are
as read; the review also found that step 4's room pick (`0x004C63D0`) counts bridges into its
index and that a failed pick ends the withdraw with no destination, where `PickRoom` skips
bridges and falls to step 5 — pre-existing since ADR-0165, left as is here and to be read.

## ADR-0330 — The Guard Post: its room, a patrol's visit and its report
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0212 and ADR-0321 · Research: `guard-room.md` §4, §6, §7; `traps.md` §3; Q450, Q517

**Context.** A guard's deadline in state 98 only ever reset, since `0x00463190` looks for a
Guard Post and the trap had no room; the trap update's flag-`0x800` arm was unread. Read now:
trap `+0x113` is written only by the constructor and that arm, both with `0x004C61C0(9)`, the
owner's Guard Room whose first slab is nearest the trap, anywhere on the map; the arm reports
the first enemy within v191 tiles to that room with the alarm's dispatch loop (state 254);
state 100 walks the guard back to a random tile of its room.

**Decision.** `TrapState.GuardRoomTile` holds `+0x113` as that room's first slab tile (rooms
have no ids), seeded by `TrapRules.Seed` and refreshed by `TrapRules.GuardPost` on turns whose
sum with the trap's id has bit 3 set. `GuardStep` visits a post past its deadline and runs
state 100. `TrapRules.ReportToRoom` is combat-alarm.md §3's loop on the held place, with the
Imp's route flag as read. A trap with shot 0 runs the recharge gate, as DK2's does, and fires
nothing. The Crypt's states 274–277, which share category 11, are read and not built.

**Consequences.** HashVersion and FormatVersion 161 (158 before master took 160). Prediction,
written before measuring: only a world with a Guard Post behaves differently, and none of the
41 scenarios nor Levels 1 and 2 holds one, so every scenario's events and both rigs' per-seed
lines stay as they are, and the scenarios with traps change hash only. Measured on 1aa98db:
all 41 event logs and worlds byte-identical; Levels 1 and 2 identical per seed (20/20; 7/20,
seeds 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 16, 18). `TrapsFireOnRealDataTests`: 649 traps fire, 653 run the gate (Level 9's four hero
Guard Posts, all reporting to one hero Guard Room). The alarm's own loop routes the Imp the
reverse way (Q517), left for its owner. Not built: `state+0x3C` (Q391), the post's effect.

## ADR-0326 — A trap's upkeep, its no-mana message, and the shots that damage it
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0321 · Research: `traps.md` §3, §9, §10; `shots.md` §4a; Q59

**Context.** Q59 measured the upkeep and named its field; its charge, the message a trap short
of mana posts, and who damages a trap were unread. Read now: `0x004C1B60` puts def `+0x96`
(`Traps.kwd` `0x202`) on the keeper's drain and off its income word, so it is paid after the
income cap; `0x004C1A30` posts message 53 with Data1 1 at most every 15 s on player `+0xAA`; of
`0x004B2CE0`'s 80 call sites, a trap is reached by a shot's collision (`0x004B5800` admits any
completed trap) and contact damage, and by area damage type 2 (`0x004AC6D0`), whose re-read
also showed every hit overwrites the damage word for the next.

**Decision.** `ManaRules.TrapUpkeepPerSecond` joins the second's drain for a keeper's completed
traps, recounted each second (the paired register and release keep DK2's total equal); hero
traps are left out because DK2 never pays a hero and ours pays every player. `TrapRules.NoMana`
posts through `PlayerState.TrapNoManaMessageAt`. `ShotRules.FindTrapHit` and
`ContactDamageTrap` strike traps; `AreaDamage` walks the tile box in order, hits traps and doors
except for gas, and compounds the damage word. A possessed creature's swing, the only one that
reaches a trap, is not built; area damage on objects is not built.

**Consequences.** HashVersion and FormatVersion 162 (159 before master took 160). Prediction, written before measuring:
Levels 1 and 2 hold no traps, so only the compounding can move them, where an area shot strikes
two things in one tick; L1 unchanged, L2 unchanged or nearly. Scenarios with traps change mana
and may change fights. Measured on 1aa98db: both rigs identical per seed; the nine keeper
scenarios on trap levels diverge at their first mana payment (Level 17's keeper pays 95 more a
second), and no scenario has a shot strike a trap or door.

## ADR-0338 — A Troll, Thief, Rogue or Guard reveals an enemy's hidden traps around it
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0321 · Research: `traps.md` §11; `combat-acquisition.md` §6; Q362, Q450

**Context.** A trap with definition flag `0x20` starts hidden; firing with flag `0x2` clears it (built,
ADR-0321). The creature update's third writer was unread: a creature whose definition has
`RevealsAdjacentTraps` (the Troll, Thief, Rogue and Guard), on entering a new tile, reveals every
hidden enemy trap on the nine tiles around it (`0x004AA110`) and sets its fight counter to 10. Of the
bit's readers, the view (`0x004A9F10`) and the pick test (`0x004AA050`) are the local player's; two are
possession's; one is the victim selector's scan D, which walks each hostile player's **trap** list
(`player+0xC`, class 3) and admits only a completed, revealed trap other than trap 16. The computer
keeper reads no hidden bit.

**Decision.** `TrapRules.RevealAround` runs from the combat pass after the fight processing, as DK2's
creature update does. No view: what a foreign keeper may see is the presentation's, and `KeeperView`
keeps listing every trap, as DK2's keeper code tests no hidden bit. Scan D — creatures choosing a
revealed trap as a victim, and the fight against it — was built later (ADR-0340); Q362 is answered as traps.

**Consequences.** No new state, no version bump. Prediction, written before measuring: Levels 1 and 2
hold no traps, so the rigs stay identical; a scenario's events change only where a Troll, Thief, Rogue
or Guard enters a tile beside an enemy's hidden trap, which then logs `trap_revealed` and may scan for a
fight a tick earlier. Measured on b5a4e1f: every scenario's hash and events and every rig seed's events
identical (L1 20/20, L2 7/20): no revealer meets a hidden enemy trap there.

## ADR-0337 — The Jack In The Box springs a Jack that wears out walking to a heart and explodes
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0321 · Research: `jack-in-the-box.md`; `traps.md` §12; Q450, Q524

**Context.** Trap 16's shot runs process 39, which makes a creature in state 273; neither was read.
Read now: process 39 (`0x004B02E0`), state 273 (`0x0046E820`), the travel state's and the health
routine's arms for type `0x2E`, and trap 16's write of its target's tag into the shot's second
data word, which the shot's own area damage then uses as its radius. That arithmetic is 32-bit
(`0x004AC6D0`) and wraps from 12 tiles. Category 7 has no hooks. No shipped level places the trap.

**Decision.**
1. `JackInTheBoxRules` and `JackInTheBoxSystem` build process 39, state 273, the toll of a point a
   tick standing or walking, fifty at the target tile, and the explosion (shot 65), once per Jack.
2. A creature gains `HeartTargetPlayerId` (`+0x2F5`) and `DeathShotFired`.
3. Trap 16 writes its target's creature id where DK2 writes its thing tag: we hold no thing slots,
   so the first strike's reach is ours, not DK2's (named in the research doc).
4. `ShotRules.AreaDamage` uses DK2's 32-bit arithmetic for every area shot.
5. The Trigger fires trap 16 at its creature unseen (traps.md §9), which `Propagate` lacked.

**Consequences.** New state, so `HashVersion` 165. Prediction, written before measuring: no shipped
level places trap 16 and no shipped area shot reaches 12 tiles, so every scenario's events and every
rig seed stay identical; 959 traps stay `FiringBuilt`. Measured on 1001b9a: all identical, event
file for event file (L1 20/20, L2 7/20).

## ADR-0333 — The Boulder rolls, strikes and wears as object process state 17
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0321 and ADR-0331 · Research: `boulder.md`; `traps.md` §12; Q450, Q513, Q520

**Context.** The 97 shipped Boulder traps did not fire: their shot's process 22 makes object 74,
and nothing modelled a moving object. Read now: process 22 (`0x004AEBD0`), object state 17
(`0x004A1390`) with its strike, roll, step, four turn handlers and terrain wear, the blocked
test `0x00453C10`, the floor height `0x004545C0`, and state 256, which jumps to 255's handler.
Every constant is a shipped variable (157–162) or a definition field.

**Decision.**
1. `ObjectState` gains the header's `Health` (seeded from `Hp` for every object) and position,
   and the Boulder's union: direction, speed, wear and the launch signs. `BoulderSystem` runs
   state 17 after the shots and before the traps, DK2's class-list order.
2. `ShotRules` runs process 22 through `BoulderRules.Launch`; `FiringBuilt` admits it.
3. The strike's heart object is the owner's heart health at its centre tile; a trap the boulder
   crosses fires at its position with no target thing, as no shot strikes an object here.
4. State 256 is `StatusEffectRules.StunInto(256)`, counted down and ended as 255 is.
5. Not built: a shot or a slap striking the boulder, creatures steering round it, the heading
   and every effect. Ours orders a tile's things creatures first, then objects, heart, trap, door.

**Consequences.** New state, so `HashVersion` 164. Prediction, written before measuring: all 959
placed traps are `FiringBuilt` (955 fire, 4 Guard Posts gate); Levels 1 and 2 hold no traps, so the
rigs stay identical per seed; of the 42 scenarios only those on Level 17 (player 4's Boulders at
(10,20) and (13,16)) and Level 11A (nine) can change their events, and only if an enemy comes
within three tiles of one in sight. Measured on aaebf56: 959 built; every scenario's event log and
every L1/L2 seed's event file identical (L1 20/20, L2 7/20): no enemy meets those Boulders.

## ADR-0332 — The alarm routes the Imp with the door bit and everyone else without
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · corrects ADR-0166 · Research: `combat-alarm.md` §2, §3; `guard-room.md` §6; Q517

**Context.** The raiser `0x004752B0` (`0x0047542A`) and state 251's dispatch (`0x0047583F`)
push `+0x36F == 1 ? 0x80 : 0` as the route word; `+0x36F` is the dumper's `TypeId` and 1 is
the Imp. `FearRules.RaiseAlarm` and `RespondToThreat` had the reverse since ADR-0166. The
Guard Post's report (`0x004A89B5`, ADR-0330) already had it right. Bit 7 is the cost
function's door rule, and the word is kept in `CreatureState.RouteOptions`, which is hashed.

**Decision.** Both `FearRules` sites push `MoveOptions.Loose` for the Imp and
`MoveOptions.Plain` for anyone else, as the binary does. The raiser needs `JobClass` Scout,
which the Imp is, and the dispatch skips workers, so in practice the raising Imp now respects
doors and every responder ignores them.

**Consequences.** No new state; the hash moves through `RouteOptions`, so `HashVersion` 163.
Prediction, written before measuring: every run with an alarm changes its hash series from
the first alarm on — of the 42 scenarios only `keepers-level17-harkan-call-to-arms-001`
(an Imp's alarm at tick 79); of the rigs the L1 seeds 1–6, 11–15, 18 and 20 and the L2 seeds
1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 15, 16, 18 and 19, all raised by Imps. A route itself differs only where a
foreign or locked door stands on it, so no rig outcome changes unless one does. Measured on
51b13a4: every scenario's event log is identical and every rig seed's line too (L1 20/20, L2
7/20, seeds 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 16, 18): no alarm route there crosses a door. Every final hash moves
with the version, which the hash folds in.

## ADR-0331 — The Alarm, Fear, Spike and Gas traps fire; the Boulder and the Jack In The Box wait
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0321 · Research: `shots.md` §7, §8; `traps.md` §12; Q395, Q450

**Context.** Six trap types did not fire because a handler of their shot was unread. Read now
(`0x004AD1B0`'s table): process 12 posts message 47 with the shot's tile; 21 is a stub
returning 0; 31's threat counts nobody and its worker kick needs damage type 0, which no
shipped shot has; damage type 1 hurts creatures in a half-open square, the 2×2 to the
north-west for `data2` 1; 22 rolls a boulder object; 39 makes a creature in state 273.

**Decision.** `ShotRules` handles 12 (`PlayerMessageKind.AlarmRaised`, fifty seconds, its row
`0x2032`), 21 and 31 (nothing), and `SquareDamage` for type 1, its object arm left out as
objects are not hit. `TrapRules.FiringBuilt` admits them and refuses a process-31 shot of damage
type 0. The Boulder and the Jack In The Box waited (built later, ADR-0333, ADR-0337): neither a rolling object nor state
273 exists here, and building on either would be a guess.

**Consequences.** No new field and no hashing change, so no version bump: the pin's world holds
no trap and the hash's shape is unchanged. The 16 Hero Alarm traps post 47 to the hero player,
which DK2 may refuse (Q519). 858 of the 959
placed traps fire (649 before ADR-0330) and 4 run the gate, against a prediction of 862 in all.
Prediction, written before measuring: Levels 1 and 2 hold no traps and stay identical per
seed; scenarios diverge only where an enemy meets one of the four. Measured on 8d53f95: both
rigs identical per seed, and every scenario's events identical to ADR-0326's: none meets them.

## ADR-0329 — Defer disarming with no identified fresh-game initiator in v1.70
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0321 · Research: `traps.md` §11; Q455, Q451

**Context.** Independent review supports unreachable disarming from a fresh v1.70 game
with shipped data and normal inputs, **STRONGLY INFERRED**, not a universal proof.
The advertised possession action is inert, but save loading can restore the references.
The evidence and limits have one home: `traps.md` §11 (Q455).

**Decision.** States 204–206 are marked unreachable in `CreatureStateCoverage`, the TrapDisarm
leave hook stays not built with that scoped reason, and readiness's disarmer arm stays false.
Do not implement an invented initiator. Revisit on a binary path, a valid original save,
or an observed disarm; Q455 is not restricted to observational counterevidence.

**Consequences.** No gameplay change. Restored disarming states are outside this omission's
justified scope; their compatibility remains unresolved. Q451 remains conditional on reaching
the attempt. The 2026-10-02 review supersedes the unqualified unreachable wording.

## ADR-0317 — The keeper's training moves
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0244 and ADR-0284 · Research: `computer-keeper-management.md` §2; Q509

**Context.** Step 9 of the keeper's tick (`0x00500C20`) drew its 50% roll and asked readiness,
then counted a move it did not make. `0x004FF5C0` was re-read whole, with its slot helper
`0x004E8210`: a not-ready army's non-workers go by experience and level to a Combat Pit or a
Training Room floor slot, through the same hand calls the retreat uses.

**Decision.**
1. `KeeperTrainingStep` runs at step 9 with the retreat's prepared set and the tick's
   readiness; the allowance it returns is the tick's. The branches, their order and
   strictness, the predicates and the allowance are the research table's, unchanged.
2. Deviations, the retreat's (ADR-0284): the pick-up and drop are commands for the next tick,
   the drop issued only when the hand is predicted to take the creature; the drop is at the
   slot's tile, without DK2's `+0x900`; rooms and slots are drawn from the keeper's own stream
   (ADR-0244), in DK2's order (Training room, Pit room, then per move).
3. Same-tick predictions where DK2 acts at once: a creature the retreat lifted and dropped is
   read as landing (76), one the hand refused as prepared (75); a creature readiness levelled
   is read at its new level, its health carried by the level-up's 12-bit share.
4. Observation schema 15: each creature's experience and dropped-to-do job, each room's
   floor slots (`AutoFurnitureRules.FloorSlotSet`) in slab-chain order.

**Consequences.**
- No simulation state changes: `HashVersion` stays 149.
- Stock Level 17's Harkan lifts its three Black Knights into its Training Room from input
  tick 3; Level 10's Asmodeus lifts its creatures into its own. A Pit fighter at or above the
  skill level is taken out again by the retreat's fifth branch, so at a low skill level the
  two steps alternate, as the binary's order predicts.
- The retreat's stock-map scenario moves to Level 17's player 5, which owns no Training Room:
  on Harkan's map the training move takes the wounded knight first, as DK2's order would.
- Not compared with the original (Q509). Room list order stays the capture's (ADR-0298).

## ADR-0319 — The Combat category's leave and enter hooks run in SetState
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `combat-category-hooks.md`; Q511

**Context.** DK2 runs the Combat category's leave hook `0x0047A980` on every move out of
category 22 and its enter hook `0x0047A810` on every move in. Ours ran neither: a fighter let
go of its engagement only where the code called `CombatRules.Disengage`. A census of every
move out of 22 found seven routes that never call it, among them the collapse, the hand
pick-up and a heal shot (`combat-category-hooks.md` §4). Read whole, the leave hook's routine
`0x0045ADC0` also drops the forced target and releases every attacker, with the victory
nibble only for a creature dead at health 0 or below, which a collapse is not (§5).

**Decision.** Built in two commits, so that a moved hash names its causes.
1. The leave hook is dispatched. In the first commit it acted on the `Disengage` route alone,
   doing what `Disengage` did inline; the hash did not move.
2. It now runs on every route out: `0x0045ADC0` (`CombatRules.LeaveFight`), then the walk
   speed, which also ends a hero party's shared pace. "Dead" is ours at zero health with no
   dying state, because ours keeps health at 0 while dying where DK2 holds the countdown.
3. The enter hook stops the creature and ends a running action: the swing, the idle and
   flourish actions and the tunnel's dig.
4. A fight re-selects inside 199, as `spFighting` does (§6): an invalid target, out of reach
   and cannot cast unlink in place, and only a failed re-selection ends the state. The alarm
   and the withdraw route again after entering 199, since DK2 enters before it routes.
5. The route helpers' own `0x0045ADC0`, for a walk from 22 to an errand outside it, is in
   `BeginTravel`.

**Consequences.**
- `HashVersion` and `FormatVersion` go to 151. The first commit kept 149 with all 40
  scenarios and both rigs identical to `2c6ea95`.
- Seven of 40 scenarios' state moves (five event logs), all keeper or Call to Arms fights. Each
  of decisions 2 (attacker release, other routes), 3 and 4 alone moves them; switched off
  together they restore all 40.
- Measured on `2c6ea95`, seeds 1–20, before → after. Level 1 wins 19/20 → 20/20, ticks
  1764–2016 → 1760–2036 (DK2 1791–1902). Level 2 wins 9/20 → 8/20: seeds 6 and 18 lost,
  15 gained.
- Three tests pinned our round trip or a held withdraw and now follow DK2: the alarm walk,
  the outnumbered imp, and the chase limit, whose runner must stay on its walk.
- Not modelled: `ReportingTo` and the four other words of §3. Our victory at the collapse
  stays as it is (Q511).
## ADR-0318 — A door met is a door fought, and a dead door leaves that turn
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · `HashVersion` 152 · Q453, Q454, Q510 ·
Research: `door-blocking.md`

**Context.** ADR-0141, ADR-0159 and ADR-0250 built a door's placement, opening, locking and
route costs, and left the door's physical side to Q453: the contact in the mover, the forced
fight it starts, the reach and sight a door changes, its health and its death. The blocking
reads are now done (`door-blocking.md` §1–7); the owner confirmed two observable consequences.

**Decision.**
- A door has an `Id` from 1, never reused, with `Health` and `RecoveryDeadline` (DK2's `+0x40`,
  `+0x11A`); traps get an `Id` too. A blueprint names an id, not a list index.
- A creature's forced target gains a kind beside `AttackingId`, and a fight target kind
  `Door`. `RebelActive` is creature state, set by job 16 and cleared by state 89 and category 26's leave.
- The mover's contact (`0x0048A2EB`) forces the door and skips the step; `SelectAVictim`'s forced
  arm engages it as read; the swing, a shot (the heart's Q363 stand-in, ours) and the approach's
  neighbour fallback have door arms; the approach routes with option word 2, as read.
- `WorldSight` asks the door thing open or shut, and a door on the target's tile switches door
  blocking off.
- `DoorHealthSystem` after movement: recovery, the owner kill and the support kill;
  `DoorRemovalSystem` after the shots removes the dead that turn. Their order against shots is ours.

**Consequences.** `HashVersion`/`FormatVersion` 152, pin `0xE459726930E9CA06`. Levels 1 and 2
hold no door and fire no door event: L1 20/20 and L2 7/20, every seed identical to master
`fe5e19e`. The shipped sweep: 940 doors on 46 levels, none unsupported, one killed by the owner
test on its first turn, Level 4's hero Wooden Door at (24,9) (a prediction, Q453). Not built:
the push-out, the secret-door reveal, the adjacent-door finder `0x00481400`, area damage on
doors, the linked objects and effects. The pit's forced creature arm keeps ours (Q510).

### ADR-0318 amendment — a door gone from water leaves floor (2026-10-15, Q600)
The removal's `0x004A66F0(0)` writes navigation byte 0 over any byte carrying a door owner,
whatever the terrain, and only the next `Tile_SetTerrain` (`0x0044FC40`, which writes on every call)
puts the terrain's byte back. Level 4's capture and dump are consistent with the predicted owner kill
of its hero door on (24,9): no door from tick 2, and 0 on that water at tick 500.
A removal on water or lava adds a `WorldState.NavStamps` entry (tile, terrain id, 0); the navigation
bytes read it while the terrain id is unchanged, and `DoorRemovalSystem` drops it once the id
changes. Deviations: a `Tile_SetTerrain` that keeps the id ends DK2's floor, not ours, and a change
and revert of the id within one tick keeps ours. DK2 skips the
write for a door that never wrote its byte (placed in play, still under construction) and for an
owner number of 0; neither stands off floor in shipped data, so ours stamps every door off floor.
`HashVersion`/`FormatVersion` 256, pin `0x766C3AB62E635E07`.

## ADR-0320 — A collapsed gate is ruined, not removed, and a hero steps off its gate as read
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · `HashVersion` 153 · Q427 ·
Research: `hero-parties-and-effect-generators.md`

**Context.** ADR-0299 made a gate convertible only once ruined and left the ruin unbuilt: trigger
action 32's handler and the creature-maker's gate step-off `0x00519B20` (Q427) were unchecked or
unbuilt. Both are now read whole, and the owner confirms a collapsed gate stays and is claimable.

**Decision.**
- Action 32 (`0x005196BB`) ruins the room on its one-based tile through `0x004E9130`, which acts on
  Hero Gate types 18, 20 and 23. The ruin is `TileState.RoomRuined` on each of the room's tiles,
  ours since rooms here are derived from tiles; no terrain is written, as read.
- `ConvertRoom` accepts a non-Attackable room once ruined (`0x00454040`'s second arm).
- `HeroPartyRules.StepOff` for every Good creature made by actions 1 and 14: a 2x2 gate's
  first slab plus a tile, a 3x1's next chain tile, a Tile gate's side through DK2's mismatched
  table, refusing when none is open.
- Declined, named: action 32 on a heart, the Tile gate's walk, the 2x2 ruin's object destruction.

**Consequences.** `HashVersion`/`FormatVersion` 153. Shipped data: 67 records on 17 levels name
64 gate tiles and Level 7's Reinforced Wall (inert); every party raised on a gate already stands
where the step-off puts it. Rigs (L1 20/20, L2 7/20) are seed-for-seed identical to master
`fe5e19e`: neither level runs action 32, and their gate spawns do not move.

## ADR-0322 — The Casino, Torture and Manufacture leave hooks, and a stored maker count
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · `HashVersion` 155 · Q514 ·
Research: `leave-hook-bodies.md`

**Context.** Four slots of `CategoryHooks` only released or were not built, on readings from
2026-09-23 that called fields UNKNOWN and put the Workshop's count on a room. All four bodies
and their helpers are now read instruction by instruction.

**Decision.**
- Casino leave: a `CasinoGamblingFearless` creature loses the flag and gets `FearlessUntil` =
  now + variable 19 × variable 203 (203 as read, not 204); the update's countdown `+0x4F4`
  (seeded at construction, never reset) sets the flag; the fear counter and the withdraw
  test treat `now < FearlessUntil` as fearless.
- Torture leave: `DroppedToDoJob` cleared unless `TortureVoluntary`, which 127's walk onto a
  device sets; the device's draw bit and the chair's spark bit are not modelled.
- Sleeping leave stays NotBuilt: it only sets two draw bits, and ours keeps no draw state.
- Manufacture: player `+0x8A`, `NumberOfManufacturingCreatures`, stored on the keeper owning
  the maker's tile, raised by enter before its claim, lowered by leave with no floor; the
  decay reads it. It replaces the count derived from `UpdatingCategory` (ADR-0203).

**Prediction, written before measuring.** Entering a walk runs no hook, so a maker walking from
the Workshop to eat or sleep keeps DK2's count up until it arrives; ours dropped it the turn the
walk began. Workshop points should now decay less while makers are away. Levels 1 and 2 build
no Workshop, Casino or Torture Chamber, so both rigs should be seed-for-seed unchanged.

**Consequences.** `HashVersion`/`FormatVersion` 155, pin `0x72C7236DC18B69AF`. The prediction
holds for a walk to bed only: hunger sets 91 from the job's state, which leaves category 5 at
once in DK2 as in ours. On a fixture Workshop with two makers and a Lair, the stored count saved
5 points over 5 walking seconds (1,467 decayed against 1,472 in 30 minutes); a hunger run decays
the same on both. No scenario or rig level has a Workshop, Casino or Torture Chamber: all 41
scenarios' event logs and world dumps are byte-identical to `1ec9fa5` (their hash series move
from tick 0 by composition), and L1 20/20 and L2 7/20 match seed for seed. Not built: the
jackpot, the Crypt handovers, the presentation bits, the `ThreatThing` reader of
`FearlessUntil`, the other readers of `TortureVoluntary`, and the death bookkeeping's
`SetState(1)` (`0x00476C80`), so a maker that dies outright keeps the count raised.
## ADR-0321 — Traps fire when their shot is built, and the target's answer walks only to a trap
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `traps.md`

**Context.** ADR-0251 built readiness and charge and held firing back on Q450's reads: the
Trigger's countdown and propagation, its count lifecycle, the tile chain's order, the shot's
immediate hit, height and collision, and the threat distribution. All of them are now read
(`traps.md` §2–§10, 50 function records). The read of `0x0045AA20`, which a trap's firing calls,
shows its walk-to-the-attacker arm runs only for a trap (class 3) and its fighting arm only
for anything else; `FightRules.Retaliate` walked a creature toward a creature attacker.

**Decision.** `TrapSystem` runs the update `0x004A84E0` after the shots, newest trap first, and
`TrapRemovalSystem` removes the dead before the doors. A trap fires only when its shot's damage
type, process and chained shots have a handler (`TrapRules.FiringBuilt`): Sentry, Fireburst,
Lightning, Freeze, Trigger, Magic Door and Hero Sentry; every other trap still loses its owner
and recovers. The tile chain is a per-creature link order noticed once a turn (ours: DK2 links
at the move). The threat goes into `TempFear` without the owner discount or `ThreatThing`, as
`FearRules` holds neither (Q375). The sine table is built from its formula and pinned against
the binary's entries. `Retaliate`'s not-fighting arm becomes `AnswerTrap`.

Ours, at their sites: players walked by id
and each one's creatures newest first in the sight finder; a held creature is off the threat's
lists; only `0x0048ED40`'s `CanFly` arm; trap shots carry caster 0.

**Consequences.** `HashVersion`/`FormatVersion` 156 (154 was this branch's; master took 155 first). Shipped data: 959 traps on 39 levels, 649
fire here; Level 20's hero Boulder at (12,5) dies on its first update (a prediction). The
Level 18 Inferno and Chicken scenario moved its creatures off a Nemesis Freeze Trap. The
constructor's zeroed sight cache holds a sight trap's fire on turn 0, as DK2's does (review). Rigs keep
L1 20/20 and L2 7/20 but move per seed; baseline `1ec9fa5` with only the `Retaliate` fix
reproduces this branch's every line, and neither level has a trap. Left: the Guard Post,
disarming (Q455), the reveal, the upkeep (Q59), effects and sounds, the unread shots, heights.

## ADR-0324 — The StealGold arm's route test carries its own word, and routes through a foreign door
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `steal-gold.md` §1; `door-blocking.md`, *Route planning*

**Context.** After ADR-0323, Level 3's final party spawns at 3168 and both Thieves stand at
their gate for 400 turns: the standing job enters, the StealGold arm fails, state 4 waits
twelve turns, and the loop repeats until another hero breaks the corridor door at 3565. By
then our Workshop had put doors on the corridor at (26,26) and (26,31). The arm's route test
in ours was the fight's `CombatTargetRules.CanReach`, whose word is 0x80 for everyone but an
Imp, and 0x80 refuses a foreign door (`door-blocking.md`). DK2's arm tests the route with
`0x00471740(room, 3)` (`steal-gold.md` §1, CONFIRMED): no 0x80, so a keeper's closed, untagged
door is routed through (a door whose tile carries tag bit 2 is refused whatever the word), and
the Thief fights it when it meets it (ADR-0318). DK2's Thieves took their job the turn after
spawning. That the doors were our stall's cause is a diagnosis consistent with the result, not
a reading: whether DK2 had built the same doors by then is not known, as the capture's object
map ends at slot 1719, around turn 1920.

**Decision.** `CanReach` gains an overload taking the route word; `StealGoldRules.Arm` passes
its own, 3. The fight's callers keep the Imp's 0 and everyone else's 0x80.

**Consequences.** No state changes. `StealGoldTests` gains the door case and its rock-wall
control. The other hero arms still use the fight's word; their own words are unread. Measured
on 7b66fd7 with ADR-0323, seeds 1–20: Level 1 20/20 and Level 2 7/20, seed-for-seed identical
to ADR-0323's. Level 3 against seed 01: both Thieves take their job the turn after spawning,
as DK2's do, and fall at 3344 and 3388 (DK2 3330 and about 3390). The win is still not reached:
it needs the Lord of the Land killed, and ours walks into the heart at 3663 with 3,144 health
where DK2's dies at 3683 under three Warlocks' 500-point shots and their stun.
## ADR-0327 — Room messages 41–43 are retained, and the keeper builds or expands to them
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · `HashVersion` 160 · schema 16 · Q518, Q519 ·
Research: `computer-keeper-messages.md` §1–§3, `computer-keeper-management.md` §10

**Context.** The keeper's walk acknowledged 41 and 42 without acting, nothing posted them,
and the planner had no expansion. Re-reading the arms, producers and planner showed the
existing note on 42's untag wrong: its failure needs a refused untag on Impenetrable
terrain, and the action table never refuses one.

**Decision.**
- `PlayerMessageQueue` retains 41, 42 and 43 with their shipped subtype rows. A type the
  rows do not list, and 41 for a Graveyard (unmodelled `+0xF4E` suppression), are refused.
- `TileState.RoomSizeChangedTick` is `room+0x9F`, stamped on every room tile by
  `SlabChain` whenever a rebuild relinks the room. The full-Lair 42 waits on it.
- `RoomNeedRules` posts from the gold carrier's store chooser (41 at availability 3, 42,
  43), a sold tile's refund no store takes (41/42 unless availability is 1) and the Lair
  finder (41, 43 by an ignore-doors route, 42 after four seconds), each by its own gates.
- `KeeperRoomRequests` runs both arms in queue order, acknowledging only what DK2 marks
  handled; 42 emits the gold-dig untag once per tick and treats it as accepted, as the
  action table does. `PlanRoom` takes a request as `0x004FC690` does, leaving Portal
  behind it, and an `0x80` request runs `RoomExpansion` before any new site.
- `KeeperRoomView.ChainOrder` carries the slab chain for the expansion's corner ties.

**Deviations, ours.** The pending build/sale gate has nothing to test: our waves complete
in their command's tick. Untag, build and acknowledgment land a tick later (ADR-0244), so
a request is predicted from the captured state; the untag result is taken as DK2's always
is. The messages test reach with DK2's own route checks (`0x00471630`, `0x00471740`), while
our finders choose with their existing routes, so a choice ours fails where DK2's route test
passes posts nothing, and the reverse; the target-tile check `0x004B35C0` is not repeated.
Hero and neutral creatures' Lair searches post 41 to players 1 and 2 (Q519).

**Consequences.** Hash/format 160, pin `0xA846A4DFE0257674`; observation schema 16. Taking
a request now leaves the Portal placeholder, adding the neutral-portal pass DK2 runs
between rooms; every existing keeper scenario keeps its expectations. Level 17 Harkan,
with its stores filled and a floor pile, posts 42 at tick 10, grows its Treasury by
(12..15, 4) from tick 505 and later stores gold there: a modern-run result (Q518).
Unbuilt: the other finders' producers (the Hatchery's: ADR-0335), the claim failure, the rescue selector,
`0x004BA420`'s other callers, mood messages and the rest of the suppression words.

## ADR-0325 — A Support creature surveys its attack spell while it recharges

**Context.** On Level 3 our Warlocks threw one Fireball, then walked into the Thieves'
melee for the 14 ticks the spell needed, fled at fear 60 and withdrew at a tenth of their
health; two hurt Warlocks met the Lord of the Land, who survived to 3704 with 3,144 health
where DK2's seed01 kills him at 3683. In the capture three Warlocks engage Thief 426 from
3310 and it loses nothing to melee. `combat-acquisition.md` §6 read the survey's slot test
as "castable, and for a Support also `0x00460C50`"; the decompile at `0x0045CCB2` reads
`(FightStyle == 4 && 0x00460C50() == 0) || 0x0048C800() != 0`.

**Decision.** `SpellRules.SurveyAttack(whileRecharging)` waives the recharge gate when
`CombatTargetRules.SpellWhileRecharging` holds: a Support creature that `FearRules.Cornered`
finds an escape tile for. All three survey callers pass it. The caster then keeps nibble 0
and the spell's range² between casts, and the in-reach tick's cannot-cast path (§9–§10)
has it stand or step back rather than close to melee. A cornered Support, and every other
fight style, still needs the spell ready. Docs: `combat-acquisition.md` §6 corrected,
`combat-spells.md` §5 extended; KB `0045CB00`, `00460C50` (new), `0048C800` (new).

**Consequences.** Test `AWarlockWhoseFireballIsRechargingKeepsTheSpellAndStandsOff…`. The
rule is RNG-free; the hash pin is unchanged. Level 3 seed01: the Warlocks now cast 17
times for 12 shots with 33 step-backs and two withdrawals (six, three and five before), but
the Lord still stands at 3704 with 5,001 health: ours hits him with traps and Imps while
DK2's Trolls land 500 a blow and he is stunned — the next lead. Rigs: L1 20/20 unchanged,
L2 6/20 (7/20; different seeds win). The waiver precedes the slot's flag read, so in DK2 it
covers a thing-targeting slot too (not built); the friendly arm re-tests the recharge and is
not waived. Unread: whether the fight-starter's melee retry for a Support (`0x0045A550`)
ever reaches a Warlock in play.

## ADR-0328 — The idle decision tries for a lair before any job, as state 89 does

**Context.** Level 3 seed01: our Goblins (arrivals 1667, 1899) trained bedless from the
tick they landed, carried `AngerNoLair` to its limit and left through the portal at 3272
and 3572, their anger log naming Lair as the only term; in the capture
(`reverse-engineering/dk2runs/level3-live1/seed01/level3.dk2cap`, a capture reading) the
Goblins 431 and 433 go idle after their first fight, pass through state 89 and walk to
the Lair before any job (431: idle 1756, 89 at 1757, travel 1758), stay, reach 2,250
health, and stand beside the Lord of the Land as he dies at 3683. State 89 (`0x004778E0`,
`idle-fallback.md` §1, CONFIRMED) runs the lair attempt `0x0046F390` as its step 5, before
the dropped job, the remembered job and the happy chooser. Ours made that attempt only in
`CreatureSleepSystem`, on a 12-tick retry timer and only while idle; a creature that turned
idle between that system and `CreatureJobSystem` — out of a hand drop's stun, or a fight —
rolled a job first, and the unhappy chooser's attempt sat inside its five-second gate.

**Decision.** `CreatureJobSystem.Choose` makes the attempt first, for every mood and
outside the gate, immediately after the Call to Arms arm; the unhappy chooser's duplicate
is removed. The sleep system's tired-and-bedless attempt stays. Docs:
`lair-acquisition.md` §7; KB `004778E0`.

**Consequences.** Two tests in `LairAcquisitionTests` (content; unhappy inside its gate).
RNG-free and stateless, no `HashVersion` change; a success skips that tick's roll, so every
replay with a bedless idle creature shifts. Level 3 seed01: no Goblin leaves, the Lord is
fought in the corridor at (24,22)–(26,25) from 3564 as DK2's is, and stands at 3704 with
2,656 health (5,001 before; DK2 kills him at 3683) — then, with the replay's entity map
corrected (its party rule had shadowed the placed Lord from turn 2, so the player's six
Thunderbolts on him were refused as a missing creature), **Level 3 seed01 is won at 3680**,
DK2's 3683; five of the player's later Thunderbolts are still refused for mana (6,000 each)
that DK2's keeper had. Rigs: L1 20/20 with every win tick
moved (1764–1984), L2 6/20 (seeds 7, 9, 10, 15, 18, 19; 6/20 before on other seeds).

## ADR-0334 — A room built over claimed floor keeps the floor's mana, as DK2's rate word does
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `mana.md`, KB `004559D0`, `00455B90`; Q521

**Context.** Level 3 seed01 after ADR-0328: the player's Thunderbolts from 3559 are refused for
mana (6,000 each) while DK2 casts fourteen. The capture's player record reads the keeper's
mana (`+0x82`): 81,002 at 3490 against our 51,000. Its rate word `+0x10E2` fits the capture's
own tiles exactly, at every sample from tick 4 to 3490: `word + imp and trap upkeep = claimed
path + reinforced wall + every room tile the keeper built`, with the heart's 25 and the
portal's 9 counting 0. Ours paid nothing for room tiles — a `ManaGain` of 0 on all 26 room
terrains, read as "building costs income" since ADR-0017. The binary says why the data
disagrees: the word is a running sum. `Tile_SetOwner` (`0x004559D0`) moves the tile's current
terrain's `ManaGain` (and its `MaxManaGain` into the cap word `+0x10DE`) between owners, and
`Tile_SetTerrain`'s adjustment (`0x00455B90`) swaps the old terrain's gain for the new one's
only when neither is a Room; a bridge laid adds 1 to the tile's tag of the moment — the neutral
player's, over water or lava — and a bridge removed takes 1 from its builder. So a room over
claimed floor keeps the floor's 1, a room the map laid pays 0, a captured room hands its
captor 0 and leaves the old owner paying. The word also carries the upkeep (the imp and trap
registrations take it off), which is why the payment `0x004C10E0` adds the upkeep back before
the cap and removes it after: `min(cap, gross + 30) − upkeep`, as `ManaRules.ApplyOneSecond`
already paid. An earlier reading of that payment as "the upkeep cancels" was withdrawn by the
same fit.

**Decision.** `TileState.KeptManaGain`: `RoomRules.Place` records the covered floor's
`ManaGain` when the builder owned the tile (a room over a room keeps the earlier value), and every
owner change clears it (`TileWorkRules`' conversion, the room-convert spread, defeat).
`ManaRules.GainPerSecond` adds it on room tiles; `GainPerSecondByPlayerIndex` raises the cap by
the owned tiles' `MaxManaGain`. Setup rooms and the tests' map hearts keep 0. Not mirrored (Q521): the
old owner's leftover for a lost room tile, a map-laid or captured room's 0 once sold, a rival's
room over foreign floor, the bridge's neutral 1, and the cap bonus following the current terrain
rather than the owner-change; the kept value is a byte (a vault's 100 fits). Docs:
`mana.md`, `terrain-room-dump.md`, `hash-versions.md`; KB `004559D0` and `00455B90` (new),
`0044FC40`, `004C10E0`.

**Consequences.** HashVersion and FormatVersion 165 (163 and 164 are branch m7/close's), pin `0x3112DA3F61990DB7`. Tests:
`ARoomBuiltOnClaimedFloorKeepsTheFloorsIncome…`, `ARoomTileTakenByARivalPaysTheRivalNothing`,
the vault cap in `IncomeIsCappedAtMaximumManaGainPerSecond`; the scenario
`land_pays_a_keeper` reads 38/s before and after its treasury. Measured: Level 3 seed01's keeper now holds 9,547 mana at 800 (DK2 9,405), 12,771 at 1200 (10,662),
70,662 at 2800 (32,553) and 96,675 at 3490 (81,002) — the mid-game surplus is territory, ours
claiming and building faster between 2000 and 2400 (gross 316 against 241 a second) and slower after
3200 (395 against 421); all six Create Imps and thirteen Thunderbolts are paid, and the level is won
at 3648 (DK2 3683). Rigs: L1 20/20 with every tick identical; L2 7/20 (seed 3 joins at 3616; the
other six within 20 ticks of before).

## ADR-0335 — The Hatchery finder posts 41–43, and a coop does not stock a hatchery
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · `HashVersion` 166 · Q522 ·
Research: `computer-keeper-messages.md` §2, `hatchery.md` §3, record `0x004DED00`

**Context.** ADR-0327 left the Hatchery finder's messages unbuilt. Re-reading `0x004DED00`
showed its stocked test is the room's `ObjectList` (`+0x0C`), where coops are not (they are
on `+0x0E`), and that 42 also needs `ChickensGenerated` (`+0x51`), which nothing modelled.
`EatingRules.HoldsAnyObject` counted coops, so a birdless hatchery was walked to and 42
could not fire for any hatchery of six tiles or more.

**Decision.**
- `EatingRules.HoldsAChicken` is the stocked test, for the walk and the messages alike.
- `TileState.ChickensGenerated` is `room+0x51` on the lowest tile, as `HatchTicks` is:
  `HatcheryRules` counts each egg, and `SlabChain.Changed` drops it from a changed tile.
- `CreatureEatSystem` runs its finder before the already-inside shortcut, as
  `Hunger_TryToEat` does, and a failure calls `RoomNeedRules.NoHatcheryFor` (41, 43 by an
  ignore-doors route, 42 for an empty reached room that has laid, past four seconds).
  `KeeperRoomRequests` answers 41 and 42 as for any room.

**Deviations, ours.** As ADR-0327: no pending-wave gate, and DK2's route tests beside our
finder's own choice, which measures to the room's centre where DK2 measures to its first
slab. The count lives on the lowest tile, so growth past that tile or a merge loses it (Q522).

**Consequences.** Hash/format 166, pin `0x32B476C1ECE5CC30`. A hungry creature no longer
walks to, or waits in, a hatchery holding only coops and eggs. In a test world a keeper
answers a hungry creature's 41 with a Hatchery, and policy 0 answers an empty one's 42 by growing it.

## ADR-0336 — A room has one health, and a conversion beats the whole of it down
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · amends ADR-0044 · Research: `room-health.md`; Q500, Q92

**Context.** DK2 keeps one health word per room (room `+0x35`) and changes it only through
`0x004E5300`; ours beat the worked tile's health, 13 applications for any room. Read and
checked against room `+0x35` in three full-state captures: a built room grows 10000 a tile, the
Level 1 portal (90000) falls 4000 a tick and changes hands at 90000 after 23 applications. The
conversion's neutral arm reads variable 136, `ConvertNeutralRoomHealth`, not `Unknown_17`.

**Decision.**
1. A room's health is a deficit below StartingHealth × Size kept on its tiles
   (`TileState.RoomHealthLost`, summed). An untouched room reads full however it was laid
   down, and a tile added or a merge writes nothing: DK2's clamped sums equal the summed deficit
   while StartingHealth ≤ MaxHealth, which every shipped room terrain meets with equality
   (`RoomHealthOnRealDataTests`). A tile leaving gives each piece the old room's whole-percent
   share of its own cap, at least 1 (`0x004ED440`).
2. `RoomHealthRules.Apply` is the applier: below 1 the room passes whole to the worker's keeper
   and resets to StartingHealth × Size; a positive delta clamps at MaxHealth × Size.
   `RoomHealthSystem` adds `HealthGain`, which is 0 in every shipped room.
3. `ConvertRoom` works the room's health, never a tile's, at the rival or the neutral rate by
   the worked tile's owner. The whole-room takeover stays. The gate is the world-aware one, so
   a ruined heart is convertible through the system (ADR-0162), not only by `Applies`.
4. Not built, both inert on shipped data: the level-start pass for Neutral's rooms
   (`0x0050B966`) and the map loader's percentage for a pre-placed room (`0x005215BA`).

**Predictions, written before building 3.** One worker at 80%: a rival's room takes 13
applications for one tile, 25 for two, 113 for a 3×3; a neutral room 3, 5 and 23; a ruined
heart 313 (13 before). The Level 1 and Level 2 rigs convert exactly one room per seed, the
neutral portal at (21,28) and (13,38), 17 or 18 ticks after the first work today; it now takes
23 applications, about 10 ticks later in every seed, so arrivals and everything after can move.
The scenarios that take a portal move and the rest stay identical.

**Consequences.** Part 1 alone (`HashVersion` 167) changes the pin and nothing else: all 42
scenarios' events and worlds and both rigs' per-seed event logs are identical to 51b13a4's.
Part 3 moves no state's shape and not the pin, so no further bump. As predicted, every seed of
both rigs is identical up to the portal's takeover, which now lands 27 or 28 ticks after the
first work against 17 or 18 (DK2's capture: 24). Level 1 stays 20/20 with its win ticks moved;
Level 2 goes from 7/20 (3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 16, 18) to 3/20 (7, 9, 19), each change downstream of
that takeover. Nine scenarios move, each first at a portal's or a bridge's conversion; Level
11A's call lands in another drawn diagonal off the heart, and its pin follows.
Re-measured after merging master cb72d01 (`HashVersion` 169, against cb72d01 itself): every rig
seed and all nine moved scenarios still diverge first at that conversion; Level 1 is 19/20 (seed
13 reaches turn 2044 still fighting the Lord, who dies at 1940 on master) and Level 2 goes from
7/20 (3, 7, 9, 10, 15, 18, 19) to 4/20 (1, 7, 10, 18).

## ADR-0342 — Heroes knock rooms down tile by tile; repair is built and never started
**Date:** 2026-10-02 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0336 · Research: `room-health.md` §4–7; Q500, Q523, Q525

**Context.** `AttackRoomHealth` has one reader, action 11 (`0x00497DF0`). It hits the tile's own
health, not the room's, through the tile applier, which unmakes a fallen room tile as a sale with
no refund. A Good-player creature applies −3750 a blow with no rate; anyone else −1500 / 4 × its
rate. Only states 180, 181 and 267 start it. 267 comes from the creature update, when a Good
creature with `DestroysRooms` steps onto a keeper's buildable land room; 179–181 come from job 11.
Action 12 (`RepairRoomHealth`) has no starter at all.

**Decision.**
1. `TileWorkKind.AttackRoom` is action 11's application: gated on a `Buildable` room, ×10 with
   no rate for the Good player, through the tile path, so the tile falls to its destroyed
   terrain (a bridge to its water or lava), its gold spills and the rest of the room keeps its
   share of health (ADR-0336).
2. `RoomAttackRules` is the creature update's arm and state 267: on stepping onto such a tile the
   hero walks to its centre and strikes once a turn until it is no room, then idles. Not an imp
   task, so it has no place in the imp's order.
3. Job 11's states 179–181 are not built: the target keeper and room choosers `0x0050EA20` and
   `0x004C60E0` are unread (Q523). Messages 0x22, 0x24 and 0x25 are not built.
4. `TileWorkKind.RepairRoom` is action 12's application, gated by `0x004E6C00` and clamped at the
   cap. Nothing queues it, as nothing in DK2 starts it.

**Predictions, written before measuring 2.** DK2's Level 1 and Level 2 captures lose no room tile,
so both rigs stay identical per seed if our heroes stay out of the keeper's rooms as DK2's do.
Scenarios where a hero walks onto a keeper's room move; the rest stay identical.

**Consequences.** No new field and the pin holds, so no version bump. Level 1 and all 42 scenarios
are identical to ADR-0336's. Level 2 is not: in ten seeds party 1's Dwarves (`Flags2` bit 0, the
only `DestroysRooms` heroes on the level) step into the keeper's Hatchery and Lair from about tick
2307 and knock tiles down, the first difference in each seed; wins go from 3/20 (7, 9, 19) to 5/20
(1, 9, 16, 18, 19). DK2's own run of that packet never puts a `DestroysRooms` hero on a keeper's
room (`level2-live2/seed01`, every frame): its party 1 stays by its gate until about 3170. The
prediction failed upstream of this mechanic, in that party's walk (Q525).

## ADR-0339 — The grid search cuts a corner only past an open side, as the route query does
**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Status:** accepted · amends ADR-0025 · Research: `imp-task-priority.md` §2.2; `steering-behaviours.md` §7; `navigation-and-steering.md`; Q28

**Context.** ADR-0025 let `GridPathfinder` step diagonally between two solid tiles, from the owner's
observation of a creature crossing such a corner (Q28). The route layer never allows it: DK2's
pre-check `0x004C9400` compares region ids, and the fill that assigns them (`0x004C91A0`, read
2026-10-03) walks only a triangle's three edge neighbours, so two floors touching at one vertex never
share a region; our mesh router, built on the original's algorithm (ADR-0157), has no route through
one either. The grid survives
behind `TryFindNearest`, which chooses an imp's work and tests a dig side's reachability
(`0x00469AF0` via `0x00471630`). The Level 2 capture (l2live2 seed01, 3063-3082) shows the cost: a
tagged wall's one reachable side held three diggers, its other sides lay behind a corner-only gap,
and six DK2 imps passed it for the next wall, consistent with that refusal; our chooser, put in that
world, took the gap each time (decision checker: six of the 31 non-lost mismatches).
**Decision.** A diagonal step is refused when both of its orthogonal neighbours are unwalkable; one
open side admits it, as the mesh does. Q28's observed crossing was not a route; whether it was
steering's (the mover commits a step by the tile it lands in) stays the open half of Q28.
**Consequences.**
- `GridPathfinder.CornerOnly` in both searches; `PathfindingTests` pins the gap refused and one open
  side restored, `MeshRouterTests` pins the mesh's agreement.
- The Level 2 decision checker: 768 -> 776 of 799 the same (the six dig sides and two kind verdicts
  at 3083 and 3103 that followed from them). Rigs on the same build: L1 20/20 (unchanged), L3 seed01
  won at 3676 (identical run), L2 6/20 against 7: seeds 1, 3, 9, 15 and 19 are tick-identical, and 7,
  10 and 18 first differ at 2168-2179 where an imp's stand for the dig at (12,15) moves off the hideout
  side it could only reach through the corner; seed 7's later fight then goes the other way. DK2's own
  seeded replays of this packet reach the party in one of three distinct seeds, so the count is
  within that variance, not a verdict on the rule.
- Routes elsewhere are unchanged unless they squeezed through a corner, which the walk could not
  follow anyway: such a target was skipped by the mover (ADR-0157), so an imp now never takes it.

## ADR-0340 — A creature with nobody to fight attacks an enemy's revealed trap (scan D)
**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0338, ADR-0163 · Research: `traps.md` §10–§11; `combat-acquisition.md` §6; Q362

**Context.** `SelectAVictim` (`0x0045CB00`) runs, after the fight-type arm, a route check on the arm's
creature (`0x0045D74A`) and then, with no target left and not a Turncoat, scan D: each hostile
player's trap list, newest linked first, passing over a hidden or unbuilt trap and trap 16, keeping the
nearest strictly within sight (inclusive) and seen; a worker only under `0x800`. A trap target skips
the heart scan. The commit gates it on a third of the distance, picks melee within a tile unless a
Support or with no spell, and sets the reach by the target's class (`+0x12`): a trap (3) adds `0x400` to
`MeleeRange`, a door (4) `0x800` or `0xC00`, any other class `0x800`. The swing's trap arm (`0x0049916D`)
lands the blow flat, as the door's. The NonFighter arm (`0x0045BDF0`, the Imp's) falls through to these
scans unless it returned `0xEA60`. The approach's door fallback is class 4 only (`0x00471D68`).

**Decision.** `CombatTargetRules.Choose` runs DK2's order: the arm (NonFighter included), the route
check, `ScanTraps`, E, F, then the commit; `EngageTrap` commits on `FightTargetKind.Trap` (4).
`FightRules` validates, positions, swings at and casts at a trap; its blow goes through
`TrapRules.Damage` and the dead trap through the existing removal. Three corrections ride with it: the
heart's melee reach is `MeleeRange + 0x800` (the Arch Pillar is class 2; ours had the trap's `0x400`)
and its commit takes the class-blind melee rule (`0x0045DE6E`: within a tile, not a Support),
and the creature route check keeps an attack spell's seen target with no distance test, as the binary has
none. Not modelled: the Turncoat skip (`+0x453`), the game's player order (a tie between two players'
traps takes the lower id), the impact pair (presentation).

**Consequences.** No new state field and no version bump: `FightTargetKind` is a byte already saved.
An Imp attacks a revealed enemy trap within about 0.7 of a tile, and a melee creature must step onto
the trap's tile to reach it (a Goblin's reach is 0.6 of a tile), where a tile-selector trap fires at it.
Prediction, written before measuring: Levels 1 and 2 hold no traps a keeper creature can see revealed,
so trap fights add nothing there; the heart reach can move seeds where a hero reaches a heart.
Measured, seeds 1–20 (base 05d3ab6; the route-word fix 1d7d105 reverted on it changes nothing):
L1 20/20 → 20/20, eleven win ticks moved; L2 7/20 → 8/20 (seeds 1 and 6 join, 18 drops). With the
heart reach alone reverted the rigs are seed-for-seed the base's, and every changed seed's first
divergence is a hero Dwarf's heart engagement (reach² 1730 → 3317): the heart reach is the whole rig
effect. The reach is CONFIRMED; its effect on win ticks is not, as it is measured to our ring-tile
stand-in for the pillar (Q363), and the two should be checked together. The heart's melee rule leaves the rigs unchanged. Scenarios: Levels 8 and 11A move by the heart reach,
11A also by the melee rule (a Salamander within a tile of the heart melees instead of casting); Level 17's five by the route check (a
Wizard keeps a seen target at t0); Level 18 by the trap fight (a Salamander, then a Troll, take on a
rival's Sentry). None compared against an original capture.

## ADR-0341 — M7 leaves shot heights to M9 and the Boulder's slap to object slapping
**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Status:** accepted · scopes the plan's M7 row · Research: `shots.md` §4a, §6, §10; `boulder.md` §3; Q398, Q520

**Context.** M7's definition of done is combat resolution, hero parties, hero gates, traps and doors.
Its row also listed shot heights (Q398). No thing in the simulation has a vertical coordinate:
creatures, objects, traps and shots are planar. Height is the moving-thing stepper's (`0x004B2030`)
gravity for a shot with mass (the Grenade alone of the creature shots), the lobbed launch, the aim's
half-height and the overlap box's height test (`0x004B5590`) — one physics layer shared by every
thing class. The Boulder's slap arm of `Object_ReactToSlap` (`0x0049C4ED`) is read: it rolls the boulder
along the slap's angle and costs it 400. Ours slaps creatures (`SlapCreatureCommand`) and the Call to Arms
flag (action 63) only; no command slaps any other object, and none carries the angle slap action 6
(`0x004C0FE0`) passes, whose source is unread. The dispatcher's knockback and Hero Lair arms are unbuilt too.

**Decision.** Shot height is not M7 work: it moves to M9 (Fidelity) as a named approximation of the
flight, with Q398 its row; M7's combat is resolved in the plane, as every built shot already flies.
The Boulder's slap waits for object slapping — the angle's source and the dispatcher's other arms
(M8's hand and object work); nothing is built for it now. Disarming stays deferred under ADR-0329.

**Consequences.** M7's row loses shot heights and keeps the owner's observations (Q513, Q520, Q524)
as its open item; a flat shot may hit a thing whose box the height test would refuse, and the
Grenade's lob is a straight line. Revisit when a vertical coordinate is introduced for any
thing.

## ADR-0343 — An aimed gold fetch is the ring scan too, so a pile in water is passed over
**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `imp-task-priority.md` §2.2 and its kinds table; `functions/00468520.md`, `functions/0046B6D0.md`; Q144

**Context.** DK2's per-kind search `0x00468520` runs kind 7 through the ring scan `0x00468D10`
with the gold handler `0x0046B6D0`, as it runs kinds 3, 6, 8 and 16; the scan visits a tile only
when its byte `+0xB` bit `0x20` is clear, which a water tile never is. Ours ran that arm, the
same-kind retry of a worker the hand aimed at gold, as a nearest-by-route search gated only by the
handler's own-or-water test, so it waded to piles DK2's scan never reaches. Level 2 seed01: imp 430,
aimed at gold, chooses at 2283 and 2301 with the 273 at (9,24) in water nearer than any other pile,
and both times DK2 takes a pile on its own floor; our chooser in that world took the water pile
(two of the decision checker's 23 non-lost mismatches).
**Decision.** `TryTakeFloorGold` is the dispatcher's kind-7 arm: `DiamondRings` from the worker on
our fixed north side (`UnchosenStartSide`), the own tile unfiltered, every ring tile through
`RingScanVisits` and `CanFetchFrom`, the first tile with a route winning. Water gold is fetched
only from underfoot.
**Consequences.**
- The review re-read `0x00468D10`: it draws `rand(4)` (`0x005558D0` on `world+0x15A0`) into the
  side slot at `0x00468D54`/`0x00468D60` on every call, and a chooser overwrites it, so DK2's
  chooserless side is random and ADR-0294's "stale stack" reading was wrong (its status line says
  so). The water result holds on every side; whether to reinstate the draw is Q526.
- `ImpFetchesGoldTests`: an aimed imp passes a water pile two tiles off for one on its floor three
  off, where the nearest-by-route search waded.
- Checker 776 -> 778 of 799. Rigs: L1 20 seeds tick-identical (19 of 20, seed 13 as before); L3
  seed01 identical (won 3660, DK2 3683); L2 3 of 20 as before, seed 3's fetch at 2493 moving to
  the ring-nearer pile and its win from 3484 to 3476. HashVersion unchanged: no state shape moved,
  and the pin's run has no aimed fetch.
- Tier B's sweep already carried the filter; only the retry changes, and its "nearest" is now
  Manhattan rings, as DK2's, not route steps.

## ADR-0344 — A placed hero takes its record's Objective as its standing job
**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Status:** accepted · extends ADR-0216 · Research: `verification-2026-09-26.md` §6, `hero-parties-and-effect-generators.md`, `placed-things.md` §6; Q275

**Context.** The level loader calls `0x0048BE20` at `0x0052077C` for every placed Good creature
with the record's `Objective` (`+0x4F`), the tag of player index `ObjectiveTargetPlayerId − 1`
(`+0x4E`; 0 when the byte is zero) and the action point (`+0x44`): the triple
the party spawn writes for a member and action 15 writes by script. Ours copied it for members
(ADR-0216) and for action 15 but not at placement, so a placed hero's `GoodJob` stayed `None` and
the 1,025 shipped placed Good creatures (296 KillPlayer, 600 SendToActionPoint, 127 Wait, 2
KillCreatures) idled until a script gave them one. The owner saw placed
heroes act with no trigger on Level 20 (Q275).

**Decision.** `ThingProjection` sets `GoodJob`, `GoodJobPlayerId` and `GoodJobActionPointId` on a
placed Good creature from its record, as `HeroPartyRules` sets them on a member; `HeroSystem` runs
the standing job as it runs a member's, through the job rules already built. A job those rules
lack leaves the hero idle, as before. The three arguments are CONFIRMED in the disassembly; that
DK2's player tag is our player id is inferred, as `HeroJobRules` records.

**Predictions, written before measuring.** Levels 1 and 3 place no Good creature, so their replays
are identical. Level 2 places eight (four Wait, four SendToActionPoint), so its replay moves from
the first turn one of them is idle; whether DK2's own capture shows them walking is unmeasured.

**Consequences.** No new field, and the determinism pin (a fixture world, not a level) holds, so no
version bump. All 3,466 tests
pass, the capture comparisons among them; `PlacedHeroObjectiveOnRealDataTests` pins Level 2's
eight and the empty Levels 1 and 3. The Level 2 20-seed rig was not re-run in this session:
re-measure it before reading its win count against ADR-0342's 5/20. Predicted, not measured: from
Level 6a on, placed KillPlayer heroes walk to a keeper's heart from the start.

## ADR-0345 — A stunned creature gets up for its type's ticks, then stands fifty turns from getting up
**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `hand-drop-landing.md` §3–§4; `creature-status-effects.md` §2; `functions/00481200.md`, `functions/00481CF0.md`, `functions/004E8DA0.md`; Q527

**Context.** Level 1 seed 13 was the one Level 1 seed that lost. The packet drops six Goblins at
(15,14) at 1700–1703 as the Lord arrives; in DK2's seven captures each lies 76 × 1, 255 × 4,
257 × 11, then stands in 250 until the Lord comes into sight at 1728–1730, all six engage, the
threat is shared six ways, nobody flees for more than a few ticks, and the Lord dies about 1780.
Ours skipped 257's hold and entered 250 with a stale `StateDeadlineTick`: three Goblins idled at
once and wandered off, one engaged alone, fled for 90 ticks with the Lord chasing, and the Lord's
KillPlayer walk was re-issued at 1830 and 1995. Re-read by disassembly: 257 (`0x00481200`)
returns 1 while an action is current (`0x00496D00`), the get-up action 53; and `0x004E8DA0`
writes now into `creature+0x2CC`, the state record's `+0x7E` (`0x24E + 0x7E`), just before
`KickToState(250)`, so 250's `+0x7E + 50 > now` is fifty turns from getting up.
hand-drop-landing.md §4's "`SetState` does not write `+0x7E`" was wrong, and ours inherited it.
**Decision.** At the stun's end `CreatureStatusSystem` enters 257 and holds it on
`ActionUntilTick` for `DropLandingRules.GetUpTicks`, a per-type table read off the Level 1–3
captures (Warlock 8, Goblin 11, Troll 5, Firefly 13, the Lord of the Land (29) 4, type 14 (the Dwarf) 4; an unmeasured
type 8, a guess, Q527), then runs the room drop. `AfterGettingUp` stamps `StateDeadlineTick` with
now on its way into 250. 257's step along the facing and `0x00481400`'s victim-or-door pick stay
unbuilt.
**Consequences.**
- L1: 20 of 20 (seed 13 wins at 1800, the Lord dead at 1776; DK2 about 1780). Over the 20 seeds
  the Lord's death moved from 1742–2006 to 1749–1801, the six seeds past 1890 falling to
  1753–1801; seed 13's flee events 26 → 7.
- L2: 4 of 20 (seeds 1, 10, 18, 19; 3 of 20 before: 1, 3, 7), the DK2-like variance of ADR-0339.
- L3 seed01: won at 3564 (3660 before; DK2 3683); the run diverges at the first drop's get-up
  (1731). The Lord's own fight is a separate gap: DK2's Lord fights from 3510 to 3680 and is
  stunned four times on the way; ours dies 27 ticks after his KillPlayer walk is issued.
- Tests: `DropLandingTests` no longer pre-stamps the word (that hid the gap); the stun tests
  count 257 as the stunned family, damage doubled. HashVersion unchanged: no new field, and the
  pin's run has no stun.

## ADR-0346 — KWD writers preserve source images and require explicit templates
**Date:** 2026-10-03 — **Status:** accepted

**Context.** The level editor needs byte-exact output before it can edit records.
Reader projections alone cannot recover unknown header words, timestamps or tails.

**Decision.** Keep parsed container words and write over retained record images.
Unedited files reproduce their source bytes, including LEVEL's understated size.
New chunks require a parsed header template: copy its unknown words, checkTwo and
timestamps, then calculate lengths and counts. This selects observed bytes rather
than guessing a clock encoding or choosing undocumented zero values. Copying old
timestamps for a new chunk is an editor policy, not a claim about DK2's editor.
Corpus evidence is in `research/kwd-container.md` §Writer header evidence.
No simulation state or hash version changes.
Retained typed models support immutable copies; copying never rewrites their
source image. Only an explicit overlay writer encodes typed changes.

**Consequences.** New records require explicit images. Split/Join validates
counts, strides and tagged lengths; every typed reader has an overlay writer.
The shared dispatcher audits every shipped record through typed writes.
`kwd rewrite` and its install-gated test share `KwdRewriteAudit`, including
per-file identity and first-difference diagnostics from decoded properties.
Rewrite refuses linked paths and existing destination files, and creates
outputs exclusively so aliases cannot overwrite source files.
Unknown bytes, unchanged padding and the embedded CREATURES tail survive.
Filtered CREATURES list-count changes and raw PLAYERS AI block edits are refused.
Trigger views share reader layouts; conflicting aliases and type changes are
refused. GLOBALS is supported only as a LEVEL path discriminator (Q220).
The unshipped dead-body layout remains a hypothesis (Q221).
Q528's base-creature aliases share one value.
The DK2.Data editing surface owns a level's manifest and referenced file images,
applies transactional typed edits, and saves relative paths under an output root.
Generic edits freeze trigger references and the file manifest.
THINGS insertion/removal retains source images and updates container counts
and lengths; new trigger roots must resolve uniquely in a complete level set.
Trigger insertion is limited to fresh detached nodes, and deletion to uniquely
identified nodes without incoming tree links or roots. Complete manifest context
is required; generic/action counts are updated separately. Existing trees remain
unchanged, with no graph-rewiring API. Map resizing retains overlapping
coordinates and requires an explicit fill image for new tiles.
No editor UI or playability validation is built. New-header synthesis is Q529.

## ADR-0347 — A worker flees any attacker that is not an Imp, and the approach state's flight keeps its back-off
**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `combat-fear.md` §3.3–§3.4; `functions/0045EC80.md`, `functions/0045EC10.md`, `functions/00470E30.md`; Q530, Q531

**Context.** Level 3 seed01 releases the Lord's party when the last gold in an action point's
rectangle is mined (condition 42, terrain 6, flags 29–35 → flag 8). DK2 finished the (26,18)
seam at 3356, ours at 3311, and our Lord fought 130 ticks early. In DK2 hero Thieves picked the
imps at the seam one by one and each imp fled within a tick (state 203); ours never fled. The
fear counter `0x0045EC80` sets itself to 3 for a `NonFighter` when `0x0045EC10` is true, and
`0x0045EC10` is true for a live attacker whose type is **not** the Imp. `combat-fear.md` §3.3
said "an Imp among its attackers", and ours built that, so our imps fled only other keepers'
Imps. Separately, the approach state's flight (`0x00470E30`) zeroes the back-off only for
`AlwaysFlee` (`def+0x686` bit 3), where ours reused the fight state's rule.
**Decision.** `FearRules.OverThreat` tests `NonImpAmongAttackers`. `EnterFlee` takes
`fromApproach`: from state 8 only an `AlwaysFlee` definition gets a zero back-off.
**Consequences.**
- Our imps flee 27 times in the Level 3 run instead of 5; an Imp near its heart still takes a
  hostile within a tile, and flees once a non-Imp strikes back. Two Imps now fight.
- L1 20/20 (seed 15 wins later, 1972). L2 5/20 (seeds 4, 8, 11, 15, 17), party, early group and
  Lord counts unchanged. L3 seed01 won 3588 (3564 before; DK2 3683).
- The release is still early (flag 8 at 3307): in this run no Thief reaches the seam while it is
  mined. The Thief pair from (26,5) spawned at 3144 and at 3244 in our two runs, DK2 at 3198, and
  not from the timer loop, whose counters match DK2 to the tick (Q530).
- Level 11A's scenario: Drako's Imp now fights Morgana's at tick 65 instead of both fleeing, and the
  call is cast at tick 100 two tiles off the heart at (64,34), the other point of the drawn diagonal,
  where it was (64,38); the expectation names both.
- The review found a second reader of `0x0045EC10`, the damage routine (`0x004B2EBA`): a stunned
  creature hit with a non-Imp among its attackers has its stun lengthened by variable 181 (Q531).
- `AlwaysFlee`'s only reader found is the approach state. The `+0x482` gate is not modelled (no
  possession). HashVersion unchanged: no new field.

## ADR-0348 — The get-up lasts the Getup animation, and a hit lengthens a stun
**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `hand-drop-landing.md` §3; `creature-status-effects.md` §2; `functions/00481200.md`, `functions/00481360.md`, `functions/0045EC10.md`; Q527, Q531

**Context.** ADR-0345 held state 257 for a per-type table measured in the captures, with a guess
of 8 ticks for every type no capture stunned (Q527). The action table's filler `0x004950C0` puts
animation block 27 in action 53's record (`0x006E47AD` = 27), and every creature's block 27 is
its Getup animation, at 30 frames a second. The ADR-0347 review found the fear helper's second
caller, the damage routine (`0x004B2EBA`, calling `0x00481360` at `0x004B2EC9`): a stunned creature hit with a live non-Imp among its
attackers runs `0x00481360`, which lengthens the stun by variable 181 (Q531). Ours parsed
variable 181 and read it nowhere.
**Decision.** `CreatureDef` carries the Getup block's frames and rate, parsed and written at
record offsets `0x940` and `0x944`. `DropLandingRules.GetUpTicks` is `ceil(frames × 4 / rate) + 1`,
the +1 the tick the handler sees the action end, as for the Entrance animation; a fit to six
captures (STRONGLY INFERRED), as is `+20` naming the block. The table and its guess are gone. `StatusEffectRules.Hurt` lengthens the stun left in 255 or 256 by variable
181 percent of itself, capped at `StunDuration`.
**Consequences.**
- The formula gives every captured length: Warlock 8, Goblin 11, Troll 5, Firefly 13, Dwarf 4,
  Lord of the Land 4; an install-gated test pins all six. A Knight now gets up in 4, not 8.
- L1 20/20, tick-identical. L2 6/20 (seeds 4, 7, 8, 11, 15, 17; 17 seeds tick-identical, seed 7
  now wins). L3 seed01 won 3588, as before; it first differs at 3510, a Knight's get-up.
- 257's and 209's handlers do not read the moved start turn, so ours lengthens only 255 and 256.
  The fixture's Goblin carries the shipped Getup art and variable 181 its shipped 25.
  HashVersion unchanged: `CreatureDef` is data, and no state field changed.

## ADR-0349 — A miner whose strike lands on an emptied seam is not full, and reaches the seam's end
**Date:** 2026-10-04 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `functions/00465870.md`, `imp-claim-path.md` §5; Q526

**Context.** Q526's start-side draw (parked) loses Level 1 seeds 1 and 2 because the Hatchery
block is never claimed while it is dug. DK2 claims it in every seed. In DK2's seed 2 capture,
imp 452 alone mines (14,24); its own strike brings the seam down and leaves it holding 818,
not full. It reaches state 10 at 158, digs on, walks to the store full at 194, claims (14,24)
on the way (`0x00464170`, state 15 at 200) and from then on claims the corridor and the block.
State 26 (`0x00465870`, CONFIRMED by disassembly) asks the hands test, which reads only the
purse, after the strike has landed. A miner that is not full whose tile is no longer a seam
falls through to the seam's end (`0x00465A6F`), which raises kind 14. In our seed 1 three
miners shared that seam, and the one at 818 left for the store on the fall tick. ADR-0296's
