second check counts the strike just queued as held, but an earlier imp's strike that tick had
brought the seam down, so this strike freed nothing. No capture shows DK2 in that simultaneous
case; the rule above decides it.
**Decision.** That check predicts the yield on the tile as the queued strike will find it: this
tick's earlier orders on the tile are applied in queue order to a copy, as `TileWorkSystem`
will apply them. A strike that frees nothing does not fill the hands. The miner then reaches
the seam's end and raises kind 14, as in DK2.
**Consequences.**
- Level 1 seed 1 raises kind 14 at (14,24) at 171, and imp 2 claims it on its way to the store at
  214 holding 1,090. That is the same pattern as DK2's seed 2 capture (200, 1,091); the seed
  numbers name different games. L1 20/20; seeds 1, 12 and 17 change.
- L2 5/20 (seed 4, first different at 2215 on this case, now loses; seed 3 also changes). DK2's own
  seeds win 4 of 18. L3 seed01 is tick-identical (3588). HashVersion unchanged: no state field.

## ADR-0350 — Build keeper spells only after their complete effect paths are read
**Date:** 2026-10-03 · **Status:** accepted (2026-10-04)

**Context.** Seven keeper spells remained outside the simulation's cast boundary.
The task required staged binary research, implementation and independent review.

**Decision.** Extend the existing command/shot boundary one spell at a time.
Keep unread effects explicitly unbuilt; ask the owner about observable gaps.
Every stage carries its evidence, function records, tests and snapshot/hash
changes, and passes the complete gate before a fresh verifier reviews its commit.
Possession covers simulation and engine-neutral actions; its view is out of scope.

**Prediction, and how it held.** No scenario casts the seven spells and keeper AI
expansion is outside the task, so each stage should keep every scenario's events
and world, changing hash series only through new hashed state. It held at every
stage: all 42 scenarios kept `events.log`/`world.txt`; the series moved only at
the hash bumps 170–177. Base `d3abf248`, HashVersion 169
(`plans/2026-10-03-keeper-spells-baseline.md`); Level 1/2 seed rigs are absent
from the isolated worktree and were not measured.

**Stages** (evidence and limits in each `research/keeper-spell-*.md`).
1. Create Gold: the shot/landing boundary makes neutral floor gold; AI path unbuilt.
2. Tremor: world slots, wall effects, creature reaction/recovery, integer action clock.
3. Turncoat: temporary combat allegiance; actual ownership kept; reversion built.
4–5. Summon Horny and OneShotReaper: creation, arrival, upkeep, departure; the
   one-use variant's LEVEL level, timer and player flag. Idle controllers unbuilt.
6. Sight of Evil: presentation only, unbuilt (Q194, Q534).
7. Possession: lifecycle and modifiers, movement (hash 176), action-26 melee and
   spells over a mixed-class tile link order (hash 177; unbuilt arms Q535/Q536),
   the binary upkeep rule the owner chose (Q58), recharge modifiers (Q393).
8. Research upgrades: ADR-0247's grant already covers every spell with a bonus
   shot, and the casts already take the bonus data, so nothing new was built and
   nothing hashed changed (no bump). `KeeperSpellUpgradeTests` reaches each
   upgrade by research; Horny and OneShotReaper have no bonus shot. The upgrade
   table is `research/keeper-spell-casting.md` §5. The third cast path
   `0x004BC290` is unbuilt (Q537); Q152's held-creature part stays open.

**Consequences.** 12 of the 13 keeper spells cast in the simulation.

## ADR-0351 — Every ring scan draws its start side
**Date:** 2026-10-04 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `functions/00468D10.md`, `functions/00468520.md`, `imp-claim-path.md` §2; Q526

**Context.** `0x00468D10` calls the game's draw `0x005558D0(4, world+0x15A0, …)` at `0x00468D54`
and stores the result in the side slot (`0x00468D60`), which a chooser then overwrites
(`0x00468DEB`). So every ring scan call draws once, and the kinds 6, 7, 8 and 16 scans, which
pass no chooser, start on a random side. ADR-0294 had dropped the draw on a wrong reading of that
slot. Built on 2026-10-03, the draw lost Level 1 seeds 1 and 2: the Hatchery block got one imp
and nothing on it was claimed by the 466 order. ADR-0349 supplies the second claimer DK2 has.
**Decision.** Ours draws `rand(4)` on every ring scan call, chooser or not. The chooserless arms
start on the drawn side; the claim scans draw and then use their chooser's side.
**Consequences.**
- L1 19/20: seed 1 wins again; seed 2 builds a 3-tile Hatchery at 466 and loses, a known
  residual. Observed in the replay: its second claimer appears at 294, claims the corridor north
  (14,23)–(14,18), already dug by then, and reaches the block at 394. Observed in DK2's seed 2
  capture: (14,21) is still gold at 249 and the claimer turns to the block. Unverified: that the
  residual is our faster digging north rather than a claim rule.
- L2 3/20 (DK2's own seeds: 4 of 18). L3 seed01 won 3608 (DK2 3683; ours was 3588).
- The fetch scenario's seed no longer fetches its pile (the rest goes in passing), so its
  expectation is dropped; a test asserts both sides of two equal piles occur over seeds. The
  kind-8 arm draws before the objects handler's refusals, as in DK2 (no change in the rigs). HashVersion unchanged: no state field.

## ADR-0352 — The computer keeper casts Create Gold and Sight of Evil where DK2's does
**Date:** 2026-10-04 · **Status:** accepted (2026-10-04)

**Context.** ADR-0350 put twelve keeper spells in the simulation; our keeper cast six.
A census of every cast call the tick reaches (`KEEPER_AI.md` §5.10,
`research/computer-keeper-spell-sites.md`) finds two unbuilt sites: the gold step's
Create Gold and step 14's Sight of Evil. The battle scan's flag words exclude every
spell ADR-0350 added, in shipped and level data; the third cast path is never reached (Q537).

**Decision.**
1. **Create Gold.** The gold step follows `0x004FD590` and the list it reads: every
   step rescans, `CurrentGoldArea` stays 0, a stored deposit is copied into
   `DigRoomAt` for tasks 5 and 6, and with none stored the keeper casts spell 13 at the
   heart's centre plus (1, 1) when it is at availability 3. No allowance is spent and
   the cast is issued whenever DK2 calls it: the simulation's own location check
   refuses it on a 5 × 5 Heart (Q540).
2. **Sight of Evil.** The simulation casts spell 1 with an empty effect: permission,
   payment, one-shot mana and both clocks, no shot and no region (ADR-0350 stage 6).
   The keeper's step draws the position and its mode roll in DK2's order, tests the
   tile's owner in mode 2 and availability, and spends one allowance on a cast its
   captured permission predicts will pass.
3. The battle step is unchanged.

**Prediction.** No non-keeper scenario casts spell 1 or 13, so 32 stay exact in both
stages. Stage 1: Levels 17 and 18 (spell 13 at 3) issue Create Gold only below
`TendancyMoney` (2,000 / 3,000), every cast refused, so the cast moves no world; the
rescan-every-step list can move gold routing wherever the gold step runs. Stage 2:
Harkan (mode 1), Level 17's player 5 (mode 1) and Nemesis (mode 2) pay 5,000 mana per
cast once they hold it, so the five Level 17 and three Level 18 keeper scenarios may
move through later mana-gated casts; Drako (mode 0) and Asmodeus (spells at 2) do not.
Stage 1 measured: all 42 identical. The prediction missed that no keeper scenario enters
the gold step (a probe saw none); a short keeper's cost arm finds a seam first, so the
cast needs a map without reachable gold. Unit runs cover it.
Stage 2 measured (hash 178 moves every series): 32 scenarios and Drako keep events and
world; the eight Level 17/18 runs move as predicted (0–30 Sight casts each, refused ones
when mana is short). Asmodeus also moves, which the prediction missed: research makes
spell 1 available at t1961 and he casts 14 times; before that the position draws alone,
taken before the availability test as DK2 takes them, shift his stream.

**Deviations.** The keeper's own stream (ADR-0244) keeps DK2's draw order, not its
values. The prisoner step before Sight (`0x005006D0`) is unbuilt: in DK2 a keeper with a
Prison draws its rolls and may spend the last allowance there first. The gold gate tests
our task state, not the task pool's kind-2 count; the cost arm with nothing stored takes
the fresh scan's first deposit (Q539). Sight's shot (process 25, 64 updates, no
collision) and the thing slot it would take are not created.

## ADR-0353 — The keeper's remaining messages: mood, room ownership, threat and room producers
**Date:** 2026-10-04 · **Status:** accepted 2026-10-05 after two verifier passes

**Context.** The keeper's walk (`0x004FA400`) reads types 1, 6, 12, 17, 18, 32–35, 41, 42
and 47; ours consumed 1, 6, 41 and 42. A census of all 151 insert calls
(`computer-keeper-messages.md` §2, §4) lists each producer of a type the walk reads, and the arms.

**Decision.** Build what is read, in stages, producers in the simulation and reactions
as ordinary commands, messages retained with explicit acknowledgement:
1. Mood: the anger wrapper posts 17/18 on an upward band change with its selector as
   Data1; the sweep frees one whose creature has left the band.
2. Make happy by the current largest bucket: pay (a partial withdrawal from the
   Treasuries and Heart, minted as gold dropped on the creature), a Hatchery chicken,
   the Lair or a job room; failure is handled below three event tasks.
3. Dispose: a Temple floor slot when `AngryDisposalMethod` is 1, else a Temple, a
   Portal or a Hero Portal; none leaves it for retry.
4. Room ownership: 32/33 and 35 from the room transfer, and both arms. 5. The other
   room producers our simulation has events for.
6. Threat: 12 from the tile-work applier, 34 from the hero's room blow and its room
   reader, and 47 (the Alarm, already posted) to the position reader.
7. Documents and the same-map comparison protocol.

**Prediction** (outcomes; HashVersion moves every hash series). Stage 1: 17s reach
Harkan on Level 17 treasury-full (four creatures, t651–679) and Asmodeus on Level 10
(five), so those two runs gain acknowledgements; no keeper creature turns angry in any
run, and other scenarios keep events and world. Stage 2: Harkan's first 17 has Lair as
its largest bucket, so he lifts the creature into a Lair if he owns one; Asmodeus's
`UnhappyCreaturesHappy` is clear. Stage 3: inert, no keeper 18. Stage 4: every transfer
in the corpus takes a neutral Portal, so it posts 33 (acknowledged) and a 35 to the
neutral player; both arms are unreachable. Stage 5: keeper runs whose creatures want a
missing or full room move; which ones is measured. Stage 6: inert; no scenario destroys
another player's solid wall, wrecks a room or fires an Alarm.

**Measured.** Stage 1 (hash 179): worlds unchanged in all 42; events differ only in the
message ids room-message events print, since 17s now take ids (nine runs); Asmodeus and
Harkan (treasury-full) gain one acknowledgement each, at t620 and t652, as predicted.
Stage 2 (hash 180, schema 18): only treasury-full moves. At t652 Harkan lifts Troll 47,
its Lair bucket largest, into his Lair at (13, 13); the Lair draw then shifts his stream,
so later keeper choices differ, as any added draw does (ADR-0244). Stage 3: all 42
unchanged, as predicted. Stage 4 (hash 181): worlds unchanged; message ids shift; the keepers
that take a neutral Portal acknowledge its 33 (four Level 17 runs). Missed: Asmodeus takes
one at t23, but Level 10 posts no message of any kind before t479, so the 33 is refused.
Stage 5, the claim's 42 (hash 182): only treasury-full's world moves; Harkan's Training Room
fills at t737 and, under policy 0, he lays two more Training tiles at t817 and t820.
The finders (hash 183): only treasury-full's world moves; a creature that wants to pray at
t803 brings Harkan a 41 Temple that takes his planner's next slot, so his Torture Chamber
(t2805 before) is not laid. Elsewhere the new 41s add events and acknowledgements only.
Stage 6 (hash 184): all 42 unchanged, as predicted.
Unbuilt, for want of a read field or state: rescue (Q542), finder gates (Q543), Graveyard (Q544).

## ADR-0354 — No carry to a full Prison; a refused body goes to the room point
**Date:** 2026-10-05 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0148 Decision 2

**Context.** ADR-0148 sent an imp to a full Prison's rim, reading the owner's 2026-09-13
note as "capacity is checked only at the door". The owner has since said (2026-10-05) that
the rim answer is for a Prison that fills while the imp carries, and that they never saw an
imp carry a body when the Prison was already full. The rescue selector `0x0046D810` agrees:
with no Prison holding a place it raises no task (result 3). State 47 (`0x00468270`) puts a
refused body down on the room point `0x004E8430`: a uniform draw from the world stream
among the room's tiles, in slab-chain order, that are neither a floor slot (`0x00454110`)
nor a wall slot (`0x00454230`).

**Decision.** `CarryRules.TryDestinationFor` takes an enemy body only to a free cell
(`PrisonRules.FreeTileIn`); with none, nobody sets off. The door check stays (ADR-0148).
A refused body is set on `PrisonRules.RefusedBodyPoint`, our 47's walk elided as 44's is.
ADR-0148's guard against re-carrying a refused body is removed: with every Prison full
there is no destination, and once a cell frees the body is carried in, as DK2's selector
would. Not built: the selector's 41/42/43 (Q542) and state 44's retry of another Prison.

**Prediction.** Only runs with a `not_admitted` drop move: the chicken-in-a-prison run.
**Measured** (hash 185): only that run moved. Its body refused at t215 (its cell taken by
a wandering prisoner) lies at rim tile (7, 5), not (5, 4), and is imprisoned at t225, not
t218; every expectation holds.

## ADR-0355 — The gold carrier's store tile, and the draws a store pile takes
**Date:** 2026-10-05 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0243 and ADR-0285

**Context.** The 2026-10-05 verification audit re-read the store chooser `0x00464400` and the
deposits `0x004F3C60` and `0x004F4090` blind (`build/verification/2026-10-05/blind/`). Ours
differed in four ways:

1. The chooser takes the first chain tile with **no object on it**, or whose store pile holds
   less than the **Treasury** tile cap (3000, on a Heart too), not the first with space. Back
   at its random start tile it fails, and no other room is tried.
2. It walks the carrier to one of eight points of that tile, `0x00698C20[rand(8)]` (line
   `0x2FC`), not to the tile's centre.
3. Each store pile a deposit creates draws rand(0x800) on the world stream (lines `0x14F` and
   `0x207`). Ours keeps store gold as tile state and drew nothing.
4. The sweep `0x004F47E0` deposits each loose pile and **destroys it**, so a leftover goes back
   down as a new pile at one of eight points (rand(8)); and the Treasury sweeps only while not
   full (`0x004F39A0`). Ours kept the pile and swept a full Treasury.

**Decision.** `GoldStore.DepositTileAlongChain` tests DK2's acceptance; a tile holding gold is
a tile with a pile, because `0x004F4510` deletes a pile its last gold leaves.
The Heart builder's objects (`0x004DB700`: Arch Pillars on chain tiles 7, 16 and 18, the heart
and its obstacle on 12), which ours does not keep as objects, make those tiles refuse a carrier.
`TryRouteToSomewhereItFits` tries only the nearest reachable room, draws the walk point and
fails without a message when the tile or the walk fails. `GoldStore.PutOn` draws for each
new pile; `GoldStore.DepositFrom` is the whole of `0x004F3C60`, shared by state 29 and the
sweep. `StoreSweepSystem` walks each store's chain, gates the Treasury on its tally and
destroys each swept pile. The starting gold paid at load (ADR-0270) draws nothing: when
DK2's world stream is seeded relative to the THINGS load is unread. Not modelled: the room
effect `0x004F3C60` plays before the draw when the room definition's `+0x425` is set, and
whether that effect draws.

**Prediction.** Every run with a gold carrier or a store sweep moves from its first new
store pile on. The Level 1 and 2 rigs move by stream shift; neither should change its
outcome distribution beyond seed variance.

## ADR-0356 — A failed aimed claim retry searches for a claim twice
**Date:** 2026-10-05 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0351

**Context.** State 10 (`0x00463DF0`) runs the aimed retry and, when it fails, clears the aim
at `0x00463EEC` and falls straight into the per-kind record at `0x00463EF3`. For a claim,
column 5 runs the claim search again, and its ring scan draws a second rand(4)
(`0x00468D54`, ADR-0351). Ours used `else if`, so it searched once.

**Decision.** `TryTakeJob` falls through. A dig or mine repeat draws nothing; a claim repeat
draws one rand(4) more after every failed aimed claim retry.

## ADR-0357 — Mana above the ceiling is clamped, not drained
**Date:** 2026-10-05 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q545. `0x004C10E0` adds the second's net to the player's mana; a net that is not
negative then cuts it to the ceiling `+0x10EA` in one step (`0x004C11DD`–`0x004C11E7`), and a
negative net only floors it at zero (`0x004C11CB`–`0x004C11D1`).
`ExcessManaDecreaseRatePerSecond` has no absolute-address reader but its loader (a
table-relative reader is not excluded). Ours drained the excess at
that variable's 5 a second, an inference never read.

**Decision.** `ManaRules.ApplyOneSecond` adds the net and clamps as DK2 does;
`ExcessDrainPerSecond` is removed.

## ADR-0358 — A portal creature's death lowers its portal's tally
**Date:** 2026-10-05 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0271

**Context.** Q508. `Portal_CreateArrival` (`0x004DC9A0`) stamps the portal room's tag into the
creature's `+0x4EB`, and `Creature_DeathBookkeeping` (`0x00487C70`, `0x00488150`–`0x00488170`)
decrements that room's tally when it is above zero, with no test that the room is still a
portal. Level 3 seed 01 shows it: the tally fell 6 → 5 as the portal-born Firefly died.

**Decision.** `CreatureState.PortalEntranceTile` holds the portal's centre tile, which holds
our tally; `CreatureHealthSystem.Die` calls `PortalRules.ArrivalDied`. Deviates: DK2 stamps a
room tag, so a portal rebuilt on the same tile is a new room there and the same one here.

## ADR-0359 — A carried body's clocks stand still
**Date:** 2026-10-05 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q164. The corpse lifetime counts down in `0x004B12D0` only while the body's
carried flag `+0x138` is clear (take-hold `0x0048B4A0` sets it, the drop `0x0048B500` clears
it). The dying handler `0x004599D0` skips the rescue countdown while BeingDragged `+0x3C7` is
set (`0x00459BE8`). Ours ran both clocks while carried.

**Decision.** `CreatureHealthSystem.Dying` and `Rotting` count nothing while the body is
carried.

## ADR-0360 — The heart's start is its room record's percentage
**Date:** 2026-10-05 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q129. `DungeonHeart_Build` (`0x004DB700`) raises the new heart to variable 174
and takes off `trunc(health × (100 − pct) / 100)` through `0x004DA200`, `pct` being the heart
room record's percentage. A percentage of 0 ruins the room (`0x004E9130(1)`) and skips the
whole heart block, the starting-gold payment included. Ours ignored the percentage.

**Decision.** `ThingProjection.BuildHeart` applies it. Level 7's rival heart starts at 1000
and Level 8's is a ruin with no heart and no starting gold paid. STRONGLY INFERRED for the
damage, which assumes the heart is `Damageable` at load and `player+0x76` bit 4 clear.

## ADR-0361 — Creature trigger roots run before action points, newest first
**Date:** 2026-10-05 · **Status:** accepted · Corrects Q246

**Context.** Q330. The frame's entity pass `0x004B7830` walks list 0 (creatures) to its end
before list 5 (action points), and the linker `0x004B4A10` puts each new thing at a list's
head, so each class runs newest first and the points in reverse THINGS order. A corpse is a
dead body in list 6, with no tree. Ours walked the points first, oldest first.

**Decision.** `TriggerExecutor.Run` walks creatures newest first, skipping corpses, then the
points newest first. Deviates: DK2 walks a creature's tree inside that creature's update
(`0x00488930` → `0x0048A480`), interleaved with the creature's own work; ours keeps one
trigger pass before the systems.

**Measured, ADR-0355 to ADR-0361 together** (hash 186), against master `82b128fe`: Level 1
packet rig 20/20 wins (master 19/20), Level 2 4/20 (master 3/20; seeds 3, 13, 14, 17), Level 3
seed 01 won at 3572 (master 3608, DK2 3683). Every scenario's expectations hold. One
modern-run assertion went: Level 17's Harkan no longer carries gold into its new Treasury row
within the run, because a Heart rim tile now takes a carrier and the Heart absorbs every
later load (`Level17TreasuryNeedScenarioTests`). The Sulk state's only simulation coverage
was a chance entry in the busy-dungeon test; it has its own test now.

## ADR-0362 — Ground nobody can own belongs to the neutral player
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0043 and ADR-0045

**Context.** Q514. `Tile_SetTerrain` (`0x0044FC40`) passes its owner only when the new terrain
is `Ownable` (`+0x17B` mask 4, bit 2) and otherwise the neutral player `[0x006F2548]`
(`0x0044FDBF`), and the map loader `0x0051EC60` sets every tile through it. Ours kept the
authored owner of 3,629 shipped non-ownable tiles (1 or 3), and the room sale, the defeat's
fall and trigger action 22 wrote 0, where TileWork already wrote the neutral player.

**Decision.** `WorldState.FromMap`, `RoomRules.Unmake`, `DefeatRules`, action 22 and the bridge
burn give a non-ownable terrain to `PlayerIds.Neutral` (the burn STRONGLY INFERRED: its writer
is unread). The presentation view still shows such ground as unowned. ADR-0043's "unowned ground carries 0" is
replaced; 0 stays the owner of nothing on the map.

## ADR-0363 — Trigger action 22 sells a room tile and builds one
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0136

**Context.** Q301 (`trigger-action-arms.md`). The arm `0x00519425` sells a room on the tile
through its owner with no refund (`0x004C5DB0(x, y, 0)`); a plain terrain is then written
through `Tile_SetTerrain`; a room terrain lays water first for a room placeable on water,
else lava for one placeable on lava, both neutral, then builds the room tile free and
untested (`0x004C5C30(…, 1, 1, 8)`). Ours declined every room tile and room terrain. The
campaign uses the room path: Wooden Bridges on Siege (over water) and Secret3 (over lava,
which becomes water first, so the bridge spans water).

**Decision.** `TriggerExecutor.AlterTerrain` sells (`RoomRules.Unmake`, the displaced gold a
floor pile) and builds (`RoomRules.Place`, `SlabChain.Changed`). Deviates: for a room that is
neither placeable on water nor lava DK2 first writes the room's terrain through `Tile_SetTerrain`
with the player (`0x005195A2`), whose navigation, mana and bridge side effects ours skips; effect `0x146`,
the map refresh brackets and a Combat Pit's reset are not modelled.

## ADR-0364 — A collapsing victim gives no victory
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q511 (`combat-category-hooks.md` §5). A collapsed victim stays the target until
step 5 of `spFighting`, where `IsAttackable` fails on its `CreatureDying` bit (`0x0045F2DB`)
and the attacker unlinks with no nibble. Only `0x0045E4A0` (from the death bookkeeping), the
victim's fight-leave and the invisibility drop set the nibble, each at health ≤ 0 while the
attacker holds the victim: an outright death. Ours celebrated at a collapse outside 22.

**Decision.** `CombatSystem` gives `VictoryRules.TargetDied` only for an outright death (a
corpse, or a creature with no dying state; STRONGLY INFERRED, since the destroy path from
`0x0048B770` to the death bookkeeping is untraced and `HasDyingState` stands in for it); a collapsing victim is let go through
`VictoryRules.TargetDown`, with no nibble, and the attacker looks for another target.

## ADR-0365 — A forced creature target gets the spell, not melee
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q510. `0x0045CB00` jumps from `0x0045CF05` past scan A and the fight-style arms
for a forced target, so the running best stays `0x7FFFFFFF` and the within-a-tile melee rule
never applies: a surveyed attack spell, status ones included, is cast. Ours applied that rule
only to a forced door.

**Decision.** `CombatTargetRules.Engage` takes `forced`, which skips the melee shortcut. Not
built: scans D, E and F for a forced creature target.

## ADR-0366 — Fighting earns combat experience
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** The Combat category's update `0x0047A870` (read 2026-10-06): in state 199 or 200,
a creature whose definition is not a worker (`+0x686` bit 0) or is Good (bit 8), and whose
fight target `+0x502` is a live creature (class 0), gains `ExpPerSecond` (`+0x6B7`, per tick
from the loader); above level 1 scaled by stat 15 and kept within 0 to 0xFFFE. The owner saw
a hero Dwarf gain levels in a fight (2026-10-05). Ours left the hook unbuilt.

**Decision.** `CreatureExperienceSystem.CombatExperiencePerOriginalTick`, granted with work
experience on DK2's tick.

**Amendment (2026-10-15, hash 252).** The walk to a fight target is DK2's state 8
(`0x00470E30`, group 9, category 2), whose state word fails the hook's 199/200 test; ours
models it as a flag on 199 (`Approaching`) and paid experience on the walk. Level 4 seed 1's
hero Dwarves went up a level within 120 turns of arriving and up to level 6 by 3595; DK2's
two never levelled and were down within about 130 turns. Now the walk earns nothing. Seeds 1–20 on
master 1aed4de2 against the change: Level 1 20 → 19 (seed 6's Lord dies at 2028, a win not
recorded before the replay's 2044 turns), Level 2 1 → 6, Level 3
17 → 18, Level 4 0 → 3; hero level-ups on Level 4 fall from 425 to 163. Other readers of the
state word that the flag hides (`ActivityRules`, `CombatMessageRules`) are not changed.

## ADR-0367 — Shots are updated newest first
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q398. Shots are list 1 of the frame's entity pass `0x004B7830`, and the linker
`0x004B4A10` adds at a list's head, so they update newest first. Ours walked them oldest
first.

**Decision.** `ShotSystem` walks its snapshot from the newest shot.

## ADR-0368 — The victory pause is one play of the creature's clip
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q376 (`combat-approach-and-victory.md` §7). Action 55 plays art slot 35 once, or
slot 8 when 35 is absent; `0x00494880` falls back when the slot's runtime bit 0 is clear, and
the loader `0x00504D80` sets it for any non-zero type and copies the file flags only for
types 1 to 8, so a slot is present exactly when its type is non-zero. By the action clock that is 1 to 22
turns (Thief 22, Bile Demon 19, Vampire 15, Imp 5, Dwarf 4, Stone Knight 1). Ours paused 8
turns for everyone, and tested slot presence by the file flag alone (Reaper, knockdown and
get-up too, ADR-0348).

**Decision.** `AnimationTimingRules.SlotOrFallback` (type non-zero) for every slot with a
fallback, which changes nothing on shipped data for knockdown, get-up or the Reaper; `VictoryRules.PauseTicks` is `VictoryHoldTicks`. STRONGLY INFERRED for
the lengths, which rest on Tremor's clock.

## ADR-0369 — A Flanker aims behind the heading; the victor turns to face the body
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q400 (`combat-approach-and-victory.md` §3, §6). The Flanker's refreshed point
(`0x00470E30`) is d behind the target's heading through the 16.16 sine tables
(`0x006C1488`/`0x006C1C88`), moving or not. State 259 turns toward the body by the turn rate
(`0x004B2AE0`) and starts the pause once it faces it. Ours used the target's velocity (a
standing target gave its own position) and celebrated on arrival without turning.

**Decision.** `ApproachRules.Destination` uses `TrapRules.Sine`/`Cosine` of the target's
heading; `VictoryRules.GoingToBody` turns, then celebrates. Deviates: the walk to the body
counts as over within half a tile (`BodyStandSquared`), because ours keeps a corpse as a
creature and the walk to its exact point does not finish; DK2 has no distance test.

Q259 rides on the same hash: the three effect-generator fields the loader `0x00521380` never
reads (`+0x08`, `+0x0C`, the six bytes at `+0x1E`) are no longer hashed.

**Measured, ADR-0362 to ADR-0369 together** (hash 187), against batch one (`efabd303`): Level 1
packet rig 20/20 (20/20), Level 2 4/20 (4/20; seeds 1, 3, 10, 17), Level 3 seed 01 won at 3564
(3572; DK2 3683). Every scenario's expectations hold. Tests that celebrated over a collapsed
Goblin now kill it outright, since only an outright death gives the victory.

## ADR-0370 — The Graveyard's burial, gate and Vampire as DK2 has them
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0151

**Context.** Q318–Q321 (`graveyard.md` §2). The burial `0x004DD470` adds the corpse's
`DecomposeValue`, above level 1 scaled by stat 19 and kept within 0 to 0xFFFE, before any
test. The gate `0x004DDCA0` passes while the owner's living `CanBeResurrected` creatures
number fewer than the summed capacity of its Graveyards, and posts 42 for the Graveyard when
it fails and one exists; `Room_ComputeTotalCapacity` (`0x004E3ED0`, type 14) makes that
capacity the room's floor slots. When the gate passes and the tally has reached the
threshold, the tally is zeroed (the excess lost) and `0x004DD820` raises one creature: on the
room's last Graveyard Crypt (object 75) after a draw, else at a random tile drawn along the
chain (`0x004E4D90`). No shipped level places a crypt. Any sale rebuilds the room with its
tally at 0. Ours subtracted 1000, had no gate, raised on the last burial tile and kept the
tally of a part-sold room. The shipped stat-19 row is 100% at every level, so only the 0xFFFE
clamp changes a shipped burial.

**Decision.** `GraveyardRules.Bury` takes the corpse and its level, `HasRoomForAnother` is
the gate (`AutoFurnitureRules.FloorSlotCount`), `Forget` drops a tally when a Graveyard tile is
sold (the sale command and trigger action 22; other tile-removal routes and a merge keeping the
survivor's tally were not checked). Not modelled: effect `0x138`, state 198 (not
built) and message 72 on the new creature; the crypt branch, which no level reaches.

## ADR-0371 — A Vampire reincarnates at a Graveyard
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Closes Q111's build

**Context.** Q329 (`creature-death.md` §2.3). The health routine's death block calls
`0x0048FFC0` for a `CanBeResurrected` creature. Its guards, in order: not on an interior
Temple cell; the owner's Graveyard gate passes; `Player_RandomRoomOfType(14)` draws a
Graveyard; a level above 1; the Monk's mark (`+0x3EA` bit 2) clear. It then moves the creature
to that Graveyard's position words and gives it its current level's maximum health. The
decrement `0x0048AFA0` indexes the old level for both maxima, so that health stays above the
new level's maximum, and it zeroes the experience `+0x3FF`. Then the Combat Pit mark is cleared
and the creature enters state 1.

**Decision.** `CreatureDeathRules.TryReincarnate`, tried by `CreatureHealthSystem` where it
books a run-out health, before the collapse or the death. Not built: the Monk's mark, which
ours never sets, so a Monk's kill does not yet make a Vampire's death permanent; the room draw's
skip of a Graveyard with `+0x9A` bit 0 (meaning unread). Differences kept: the position words
are our STRONGLY INFERRED `CentreFieldX/Y` (Q515); DK2 tries this on every health write that
kills, ours once a game second, so a Vampire can stand at 0 health for up to a second and the
direct kills of `ManaRemovalSystem` and `PrisonSystem` do not reach it.

## ADR-0372 — Trigger conditions 20 and 21 count moods
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0113

**Context.** Q269. The player dispatcher `0x004C7B20` (arms 0x14 and 0x15) counts the
player's creatures, of `CreatureId` when non-zero, that are not workers and whose mood band
`+0x28A` (written by `Anger_Add`) is 0, happy, or 2, angry, and compares the count with Value.
Ours declined both.

**Decision.** `TriggerExecutor.MoodCount` on `CreatureAngerRules.MoodOf`.

## ADR-0373 — A slap is counted for the slapped creature's owner, by the slap's arm
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q278. `Hand_SlapCreature` (`0x0048B8A0`) adds one to `[thing+0x2A]+0xEE6`
(`NumberOfSlaps`) of the slapped thing's owner; condition type 71 reads it. Its arms: a Horny
goes to state 242 uncounted; states 76, 101 and 193 return at once; 209 and 255 take damage and
count without anger or bonus. Then the room the creature holds (`+0x3B9`), not the one under
it, decides: one the slapper does not own returns; a Torture Chamber takes damage only; with
no held room, states 67, 120, 132 and 197 return. Every return skips the damage, anger and bonus
as well as the count. The rest count after a state move (67, 77 or 120), unless it is refused.
Ours never counted and applied every slap in full. The trap and object writers have no
counterpart here: ours slaps only creatures.

**Decision.** `HandSystem.Slap` chooses the arm on `HeldPlace` and increments
`PlayerState.SlapCount` of the creature's owner where DK2 does. Not built: the state moves (so a
refused move is still counted), a Horny's state 242 (ours slaps it in full, uncounted).

## ADR-0374 — Flag 128 is the level score in a condition
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q229 (`trigger-state.md` §4). Condition 1 on id 128 compares `LevelScore` with
Value directly, whatever the literal bit (`0x00518270`). An indirect id of 128 reads the byte
past the flag bank. Ours read `IndirectFlagId` with the bit clear, and an indirect 128 read the
score.

**Decision.** `TriggerConditionEvaluator.EvaluateFlag` compares the score with Value for id 128
and declines an indirect 128, which no shipped level uses. Not built: the `MpdScore` adder
`+0x344`.

## ADR-0375 — Creature records of any size; signed job-table words
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q14: the chunk reader `0x0056A250` zero-fills a 5449-byte record and reads the
file's record into it, so DK2 accepts any size (LIKELY: the rest of the routine is unread, and
a record over 5449 bytes is read into a scratch buffer of unread size); ours threw on all but
5449 and 5537. Q11: the
job tables' mood and mana words are signed 16-bit (`0x00492320`); ours read them unsigned. No
reader of either word is known.

**Decision.** `KwdCreatures.Parse` copies up to 5449 bytes of each record into a zeroed buffer;
`CreatureJobPreference` and `CreatureJobAlternative` carry `short`. `KwdCreaturesWriter` still
writes only 5449- or 5537-byte templates. The loader divides both words, unsigned, by a local
that is INFERRED to be variable 19 (not traced); not built, since nothing reads them.

**Measured, ADR-0370 to ADR-0375 together** (hash 188): the Level 1 (20/20), Level 2 (4/20) and
Level 3 (won at 3564) rigs are identical to batch two, tick for tick; none of the three levels
reaches a Graveyard, a Vampire, conditions 20, 21 or 71, or flag 128.

## ADR-0376 — The keeper slaps on DK2's activity code and plans inside its record's build area
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `computer-keeper-management.md` §8,
`computer-keeper-observations.md` (*First same-map comparison*); Q546

**Context.** On Level 17 ours tunnelled to neutral Portals at (53,6) and (16,70); DK2's Harkan
never does. Two causes. `KeeperAI` planned over the whole map, while the PLAYERS record
unpacker loads `MaxBuildArea` (keeper `+0x12`) from block `0x92`, and Harkan's (1,1)-(40,64)
fails both Portals at `0x004FC690`'s first gate. And ours slapped any working creature, where
`0x00502F00` asks `0x00478A20` for 5: a worker with no task or a reinforce task, a non-worker
by its category's entry in `0x006996C4` (filled at `0x004798F0`). The slap sped our Portal
claimer to 90 %.

**Decision.** `KeeperAI` takes the record's `MaxBuildArea`. Deviates: a record with no rectangle
gives the whole map, where `0x004F8750` would store zeros; none of the 121 shipped computer
records has one. `CreatureActivityRules.Code` reproduces `0x00478A20`; the observation carries it
(schema 19) and the slap step asks for 5. The `SpeedChangeTimer` test reads our speed
effect (`0x0048CAD0`'s timer) and, because our slap does not start that timer as DK2's does,
also refuses a creature slapped within 400 ticks. Deviates: the state object's `+0x3C`
overrides are not modelled.

**Consequences.** Level 17's Harkan tags nothing outside (1,1)-(40,64) and claims his second
Portal at 159 (DK2 164, ours 149 before). He now builds the Prison at 476, centred on (12,25);
DK2's is at 855 on (16,22) (Q555). The changed slap targets change the keeper's allowance and random stream.
On Level 11A a slap takes tick 49's allowance, the tag past the bridge lands at 50, the imp that
dug it at once on master has taken another job, Morgana reinforces the tile first, and the call
moves from 104 to 247; the scenario runs 300 ticks. One AI test takes seed 2. No simulation state changes: no HashVersion bump.

## ADR-0377 — Trigger action 18 makes and breaks alliances
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `trigger-action-arms.md` (*Action 18*),
`computer-keeper-observations.md` (*Level 11A*); Q557

**Context.** In the first Level 11A comparison ours sent Drako against Raksha at tick 66, a
tunnel north with eight bridge tiles; DK2's Drako never attacks her. Level 11A's first turn
runs action 18 for 7-6, 7-4 and 7-5, and the capture shows those alliance bytes set on turn 2.
Ours left action 18 unperformed, so the attack planner (`0x004FAEF0`) saw Raksha as an enemy.

**Decision.** `TriggerExecutor` performs action 18 as `0x00519376` does: body byte 02 zero
allies the players in bytes 00 and 01, any other value breaks the alliance, both ways, and the
action succeeds. A player the level lacks is not written. HashVersion and the snapshot format
go to 189; no new field.

**Consequences.** On Level 11A ours now goes Morgana, then Belial through (48,43) and the
bridges at (47,43) and (46,43), the tiles DK2 uses. It tags Belial's first tunnel tile at 68; DK2
digs it at 443 (Q557). The `level11a_drako_attack` scenario still passes. The neutral
player's row, allied with everyone at load in the capture, is not modelled (Q558).

## ADR-0378 — The claim on the way comes before the walk-over pick-up, from a worker job only; the pick-up reads the imp's own tile
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0293, ADR-0303

**Context.** The creature update's worker arm (`0x0048904E`, record `0x00488930`) calls the claim
on the way `0x00464170` (`0x00489076`) before its gold test, on a tick the tile changed. Inside,
`0x00464170` asks for effective category 3, a worker job (`0x00478050`: the state's category, or
through a walk the state it resumes), and nothing carried (`+0x3C3`, `+0x3C5`), then its distance
and kind tests. The pick-up then walks only the imp's own tile's thing list, takes the
first neutral pile strictly within `0x555`, and stops. Ours picked up first, scanned every world
object within the box (so a pile on the next tile could be taken), and tried the claim only on
job, fetch and deposit walks, by activity.

**Decision.** `ImpTaskSystem.Update` tries `TryClaimOnTheWay` when `NeedRules.ResolvedCategory` is
`WorkerJob` and no object or creature is carried, then `PickUpGoldInPassing`, which reads the
imp's own tile. A wander walk resumes idle and never claims; in ours an idle imp takes any such
tile through the claim search first, so only a tile dug during a wander walk could tell the two
gates apart, and no test pins it. Deviates: piles are taken in our world order, not the tile's
thing list; the player byte `+0x10FC` test is not built.

## ADR-0379 — The ring scan does not filter its own tile
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0291, ADR-0292

**Context.** `0x00468D10` calls its chain on the centre at `0x00468DA0` with no `+0xB` bit `0x20`
test; only the ring loops make it (`0x00468E99`, `0x00468F71`). Ours filtered the centre in Tier
B, the drop scan and the kinds 6 and 8 scans (only the kind-7 retry exempted it), so gold under
an imp standing in water was never offered by them.

**Decision.** `RingScanVisits` takes the scan's centre and admits it untested, for every caller.

## ADR-0380 — A free reinforce side the imp cannot reach deletes the wall's task
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0291

**Context.** When the walk to a free side fails, `0x0046AEA0` deletes the wall's kind-6 entry
(`0x00508040`), whether it was just raised or found with other sides held, and tries the next
side. State 22's handler checks `0x00508070(+0x8A, 6)` at `0x004663C4` whenever no action is
playing (`0x00496D00`: no action id, or 0x15), and on a miss clears `+0x8A` and sets 10 (read
2026-10-06). So every other imp on that wall loses the task. Ours passed the side over and kept no per-wall entry.

**Decision.** `TryReinforceAt` skips a solid side, as DK2 counts only a side that is not solid
and the keeper's (ours had only the ownership test, and an owned reinforced wall beside it failed
its route quietly), and calls `ForgetReinforceTask` when a free side has no route: every other
worker whose task is that wall's reinforce goes to 10. Without the solid test the deletion fired
every tick on the shipped scenarios' corridor ends. Deviates: ours drops them at once,
where DK2 drops a reinforcer at its next check and, INFERRED (the walk states were not read), a
walker on arrival; repair (kind 16) is not a job in ours.

## ADR-0381 — A loose crate asks its blueprint before the shared latch
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0294

**Context.** In the objects handler `0x0046B9C0` a crate (flag `0x10`) calls the crate branch
`0x00468910` before the latch it shares with books is tested, and its success returns 1 at once,
with no kind-8 reach test, task or holder steal. Ours tested the latch first, so a book whose
Library search failed hid a later crate from its blueprint, and a blueprint take went through the
route check and the steal.

**Decision.** `TryObjectAt` runs `BlueprintForLooseCrate` and `CommitCrateFetch` first for a crate;
only when they fail does the latch and the Workshop search follow.

## ADR-0382 — State 27's take stops at the pile that fills the hands
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0288

**Context.** `0x00466850` takes neutral piles, each up to what the hands lack against the
level-scaled maximum, and stops after the first pile that makes `0x00464360(1)` report full (the
limit less variable 74, 340). Ours took every pile on the tile up to the full limit, so a part-full
imp could leave up to 340 heavier.

**Decision.** `TakeFromPilesOn` takes neutral piles in order and stops once `HandsFull`. Not built:
DK2 takes only piles strictly within `0x555` of the imp, which walks to the pile's own point
(`0x0046B6D0`); ours walks to the tile centre, where the box would leave a corner pile out of reach
and the imp would fetch it forever.

## ADR-0383 — The trigger fields Q227 named
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Q227 (`trigger-action-arms.md`): condition 23's byte 2 is a player slot, 0 for the
total (`0x004C7DF0`); action 24 reads only its second dword's low byte (`0x004C8688`), 0 speaking
and posting the message record, non-zero only speaking; action 35's byte is 0 vanish, 1 death fall;
39 and 40 name a door and a trap type; 41 an effect id. Ours named them `Unknown_*` and read action
24's field as a dword.

**Decision.** `KwdAdditionalRecords` names them `PlayerSlot`, `SpeakOnly` (a byte, its other three
bytes unreached), `DeathKind`, `DoorId`, `TrapId` and `EffectId`. Names only: nothing in the
simulation reads them, so no hash change.

**Measured, ADR-0378 to ADR-0382 together** (hash 190), against master `21ca5011`: the Level 1
packet rig 20/20 (20/20; seeds 4, 7, 10, 11, 13 and 19 move by 8 to 24 ticks), Level 2 5/20
(4/20; seeds 1, 3, 10, 13, 14 against 1, 3, 10, 17), Level 3 seed 01 won at 3592 (3564; DK2 3683).
Every scenario's expectations hold.

## ADR-0384 — Task 7 waits on each tagged tile and ends on DK2's route test
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `computer-keeper-tasks.md` §5,
`computer-keeper-observations.md` (*Level 11A*); Q557, Q561

**Context.** On Level 11A ours started Drako's tunnel to Belial at tick 68; DK2's digs its
first tile at 443. Task 7 (`0x004FDC50`) works on the cursor's own tile: rock is tagged and
then waited on, without stepping, until it is dug; only open ground asks `0x00452970` whether
the target routes to the cursor. Ours tagged as the walker stepped, walked on past the tag,
and ended once a flood from the heart through its own tags reached the target. A tunnel
therefore ended as soon as its last rock was tagged.

**Decision.** `KeeperAI.DigPath` follows DK2's order: rock on the cursor is tagged if it is
not already, and the pass ends; open ground ends the task when the target routes to the
cursor, with option 1 and no water, lava or portal hole; otherwise the walker steps, and the
tile it steps onto is handled next pass. Deviates: a target on a solid tile never routes. Our
search never judges the triangle a route starts in, so Level 17's gold target (19,2) routed
past walls to the Portal and Harkan stopped digging; DK2's Harkan digs to it, so its query
probably fails there (inferred from the outcome, Q561). Water
stands in for DK2's stale water flag; the 51-free-entry pool test is not modelled. No
simulation state changes: no HashVersion bump.

**Consequences.** Level 11A: Belial's first tunnel tile is dug at 281 (DK2 443), its bridges
at 297 and 299 (DK2 457, 461), the call at 308 (700), Morgana falls at 730 (1,378); the bridges
at (57,38) and (57,39) move from 164 to 871. The scenario's ticks move (tag 12, spans 89 and
90, call 279) and it runs 320 ticks. Level 17: Harkan digs to his seam one tile at a time and
mines from 85, then grows his Training Room (359-685) before his Prison (1,291); DK2 builds
the Prison at 855 first (Q555). The scenario runs 1,400 ticks.

## ADR-0385 — An imp task walk casts Imp Haste as it sets off
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `travel-state-call-sites.md` §3; Q401, Q418

**Context.** Every imp task handler walks through `0x004651A0` (45 call sites; the wander, state
87, does not). Before routing it scans the creature's ability slots 0 to 2: a slot within the
creature's level, with a spell, and ready by `0x0048C800`. A teleport slot (record flag `0x20`)
ends the scan; a speed slot (`0x40`) is cast on the spot: the slot stamped, `0x0048CAD0` with the
record's `+0x1F`/`+0x23`, refused while a speed effect runs, and the display word `+0x4DD`. The
shipped Imp carries Imp Haste (150 %, 15 s, 5 s recharge) in slot 0 at level 4 and Imp Teleport
in slot 1 at level 8, so a DK2 Imp from level 4 walks hasted after most task choices. The Imp is
the only creature with either flag. Ours never cast it.

**Decision.** `ImpTaskSystem.BeginTaskWalk` runs `CastOnTheWalk` before every task walk's
`BeginTravel` (not the wander's), through `SpellRules.CanCast` and `StatusEffectRules.ModifySpeed`.
Deviates: ours begins a walk only once a route is found, where DK2 scans before routing, so a walk
whose route fails casts in DK2 and not in ours; `+0x4DD` (display) is not kept; the teleport is not
built (Q418). The haste itself keeps ADR-0168's approximation (Q399: ours scales the cap every
tick, running included). The 45 call sites were not mapped one to one: the dig, claim and
reinforce handlers hold two to four each, read as their alternative walks (a free or a held side,
reinforce or repair), which ours starts through one `CommitJob`; if any is a second walk inside one
task, DK2 may cast there and ours does not (Q562).

**Measured** with ADR-0386, below.

## ADR-0386 — Work experience is paid once per work hit
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0083 item 6

**Context.** Measuring ADR-0385 on Level 3 showed our Imps reaching level 4 at 1357, DK2's at 2082.
`ImpExperienceGainPerSecond` (20, `0x006F295E`) has nine readers, every one a work action's
callback (dig `0x00496E00`, the mining strike `0x004971D0`, claim `0x004974C0`, attack floor
`0x00497670`, reinforce `0x00497960`, conversion `0x00497BF0`, room attack `0x00497DF0`, repair
`0x00498120` and one more), each paying the raw 20 once when its tile test passes, before the
work. All nine actions are mode 3 (`0x004950C0` writes 3 at record `+0x15`), which the runner
`0x00496AA0` calls once per action. ADR-0083 read the callbacks as running every tick and paid 20
per tick of work. The Level 3
capture's imps gain exactly 20 on 17 % of their digging ticks, 63 % of claiming and 38 % of
mining: once per work application. DK2's imps first reach levels 2, 3, 4 and 5 at 661, 1371,
2082 and 2540; ours did at 305, 670, 1357 and 2077.

**Decision.** `TileWorkSystem` pays `CreatureLevelRules.WorkExperiencePerHit` to the maker of every
work order whose outcome is not `Rejected` (`CreatureExperienceSystem.AwardWork`), worker or not
(the room attack's reader pays only a Good creature, so ours skips a non-Good `AttackRoom`); the
per-tick work pay is gone. Deviates: ours pays when the queued order resolves later in the tick,
not inside the callback, and without the per-tick loop's held, imprisoned, down and leaving gates.

**Measured, ADR-0385 and ADR-0386 together** (hash 191), against `1939bebd` (Level 1 20/20, Level
2 5/20, Level 3 seed 01 won at 3592): our Imps first reach levels 2 to 5 at 635, 1388, 2097 and
2558 (DK2 661, 1371, 2082, 2540; ours was 305, 670, 1357, 2077). Level 3 is won at 3612 (DK2
3683). Level 1 falls to 19/20 (seed 6 lost; seeds 8, 11 and 17 win near 1930) and Level 2 to 2/20
(seeds 5 and 17): the early levels had been covering residuals elsewhere. Haste alone, on the
old rate, gave Level 1 20/20, Level 2 2/20 and no Level 3 win by the capture's end. After the
merge with ADR-0384, Level 17's Harkan lays his Prison from 1,643 (1,291 before; DK2 855, Q555),
so `level17_harkan_unassisted` runs 1,800 ticks.

## ADR-0387 — Imps repair their keeper's damaged wall, and a work rate is truncated before it is scaled
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0133; answers Q219's last row

**Context.** On Level 11A our Drako dug Morgana's reinforced wall (64,38) at 229, DK2's at 387.
The capture shows why: three of Drako's imps take 2 each a tick, and from 101 one of Morgana's,
at (64,37) in states 23 and 24, puts 3 back, so the wall loses 3 a tick. The reinforce handler
`0x0046AEA0` has a second pass, kind 16, gated by `0x00453E30`: the keeper's own solid,
penetrable, goldless tile whose health is not its maximum, touching the keeper's floor. Ours had
`TileWorkKind.RepairWall` and its action but no job reached it. And `RepairWallHealth` 22 gave 4
an application where DK2 gives 3: the loader divides every rate by variable 19 with `IDIV`
(`0x0051CBA0`), so 22 is stored as 5, and the action (`0x00497AC0`) floors 5 × 0.8.

**Decision.** The reinforce priority takes `RepairWall` when `Reinforce` does not apply, on the
same stance and own-floor test, recorded as task kind 6 since both resume through one handler.
`RepairWall` applies to `0x00453E30`'s tile. `SimulationTiming.WorkApplication` replaces the
shift of fourteen: truncate the tabled value over four, then floor it times the rate. They differ
only where four does not divide the value: repair, and claiming (825) and own-wall digging
(−130) with both bonuses. Deviates: DK2 records kind 16; the own wall below half health that
`0x00453E90` gives kind 6 (reinforce, rate 50) is repaired at 22 in ours (Q564); the own-floor test omits `0x00453B30`'s Ownable bit, as the reinforce path always has; the divisor is the constant four, not live variable 19.

**Measured** (hash 192), Level 11A with keepers 4 to 7 running, as DK2 runs them (the comparison
had run Drako's AI alone): Morgana repairs from 92 (DK2 101), the wall falls at 362 (387), the
Belial tunnel's first tile at 433 (443), its bridges at 446/448 (457/461), the call at 544 (700),
Morgana at 1,004 (1,378). The scenario now runs those keepers on the record's gold. Q563 holds the
rest.

## ADR-0388 — A rival's imp holds no task of this keeper's, and the fight approach walks within a tile
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Advances Q563; supersedes the every-player count of ADR-0026 and ADR-0030

**Context.** With ADR-0387 the Level 11A wall falls at 362, DK2's at 387, but Drako claimed the
hole 13 ticks later where DK2's imps fight in it until 638. Two faults. At 364 Drako's imp stole
Morgana's imp's claim of the hole (`task_stolen: imp=11 from=18`): DK2's task pool is the keeper's
own (`player+0x1105`), so a rival's imp can neither hold, crowd nor lose a slot of it, while ours
compared any worker on the tile. Then the two imps, 0.58 tile apart on one tile and out of reach,
looped in state 8 without moving: our route request gives a creature on its target's tile a
finished route, where DK2's gate walk `0x004CF490` returns a one-point route, the target itself
(`0x004D0320`, `0x004D0240` have no shortcut either).

**Decision.** Every holder scan (`MiningSlots.Holder`, `ImpCrowding.FaceIsFull`, the claim and
reinforce steals, `ForgetReinforceTask`, the object and crate holders) counts only the asker's
keeper's workers (`TaskStealing.SharesTaskPool`). The approach's three route requests use
`TryRouteToStance`, which loads the one point on the same tile. Deviates: `TryRouteTo` keeps the
finished route for every other caller; removing it there fails eleven simulation tests and a scenario that pin a creature
already in its room taking the job without a walk, which DK2 may check in its callers (Q565).

**Measured** (hash 193), Level 11A with keepers 4 to 7: the imps fight in the hole from 368
(DK2 389) and Drako claims it at 399 (DK2 638; 375 before); Morgana's keeper lifts her wounded imp
out by hand at 391, where DK2's wounded imps show state 77, the slap reaction, and fight on. The call is at 540 (700),
the bridge at (64,46) at 832 (1,155), Morgana falls at 887 (1,378; 1,004 before). Levels 1 and 2
on the seed rig, against 885ec6d8: Level 1 19/20 both (seed 6 lost before, 8 now), Level 2 2/20
(1/20 before). Level 3 was not run.

## ADR-0389 — The gold fetch walks to the pile's point and takes within its box
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Completes ADR-0382 · Research: `gold-on-the-floor.md` §8, §12

**Context.** The gold handler `0x0046B6D0` walks an imp to the pile's own position (`0x0046B90A`:
the pile's `+0x1A`, word `0xE8`, resume 27), and state 27 (`0x00466850`) runs when that walk
(state 6, which tests no pile or task) ends, taking only the piles strictly within `0x555` of the
imp on both axes. Ours walked to the tile centre, took on stepping onto the tile, took every pile
on it, and abandoned the walk when the tile's gold went. Five captures (Level 1, Level 2 seeds 1
to 3, Level 3) hold 34 walks that ended in 27, all on a bare tile: in 22 the imp's gold rose that
tick, 4 to 15 units from the pile and 1 to 7 ticks after entering the tile, taken by the walk-over
pick-up (`0x0048904E`, STRONGLY INFERRED: 27's own handler had not run yet); in 12 the pile was
already gone and nothing was taken. Imp 443 (Level 3) shows 27 holding 1,092 at 2343 and walks to
the store at 2344.

**Decision.** `CommitFetch` routes to the first neutral pile's point through `TryRouteToStance`
(the route request has no same-tile shortcut, `imp-walk-arrival.md`); `UpdateFetching` waits for
the route to end and has no pile test before it; `TakeFromPilesOn` takes only piles inside the box.
Deviates: a pile's point is its third-of-a-tile cell centre (`ObjectState` has no position), so
two piles in neighbouring cells are never both in the box; the first pile is in world order, not
the first whose task is free (per-pile tasks are not built, Q155); ours runs 27 in the tick the
walk ends, DK2 on the next; 27 takes on the target tile and abandons an imp that ended elsewhere,
where DK2 takes around wherever it stands; 27's task check (`0x00508070`) is not read, so whether
it fails on an emptied tile is unknown (with empty hands the outcome is the same); the wrapper's
teleport for a walk over two tiles is not built (Q418).

**Measured** (hash 193, before the merge with ADR-0388) against master `885ec6d8` (Level 1 19/20, Level 2 1/20, Level 3 seed 01
won at 3604): Level 1 18/20 (seeds 8 and 16 lost, seed 6 now won), Level 2 4/20 (seeds 3, 5, 10
and 13), Level 3 won at 3556, further from DK2's 3683.

## ADR-0390 — A KMF clip is interpolated between its keys and timed by its descriptor
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Presentation only · Research: `kmf-animation-playback.md`; Q442

**Context.** The byte after each `GEOM` position is the frame, within its 128-frame block, at
which that entry is exact; DK2's evaluator `0x0057E5B0` puts a frame between two keys on the
straight line from entry g to g + 1, and the drawer `0x00577F10` evaluates a continuous frame
f = (frames − 1)·time, its integer part clamped to frames − 2. A creature clip's pass lasts the
descriptor's frame count (`+0x44`) over its FPS (`+0x48`) in seconds by the type-6 clock
(`0x004B41E0`); that this clock drives the drawn time is STRONGLY INFERRED. `KmfReader` dropped
the byte, so every frame that is not a key held the previous key's pose (12.05 M of 28.4 M vertex
lookups over the shipped KMFs), and `GlbWriter` wrote `STEP` keys at an assumed 30 fps.

**Decision.** `KmfReader` keeps the key bytes and evaluates each integer frame as `0x0057E5B0`
does, the last through frame − 1's lookup as the drawer clamps it; `Dk2ArtResource` carries a
type-6 resource's frame count and FPS, and `GlbWriter` writes `LINEAR` morph weights with one
pass, frame 0 to the last, over count/FPS seconds. Keys fall on integer frames, so a viewer's
linear blend between the sampled frames is DK2's pose. The descriptor's count is not the KMF's in
300 of 906 creature clips (mostly one less; Imp_Happy 20 against 14), and the pass follows the
descriptor. Deviates: equal keys hold entry g exactly (the reciprocal table's entry 0 is unset);
a backwards key and a last entry with no g + 1 also hold g, which matches DK2 only because, in
every shipped KMF, they fall on the key's own frame, where DK2 multiplies a zero numerator by a
float read outside its table, assumed finite; a KMF with no descriptor (objects, rooms) keeps 30
fps; the link from the animation phase to the drawn time is unread (Q442).

## ADR-0391 — Wall torches are a stateful presentation layer
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Presentation only · Amends ADR-0036 · Research: `wall-torches.md`; Q445, Q446

**Context.** DK2's wall torches are engine lights the simulation never reads, placed by CBridge
slot `+0xB8` (`0x00439B90`): a Torch-flagged wall that is not a door lights each floor face, N, E,
S, W, that is not solid or a door, passes the parity (x odd for N/S, y even for E/W) and holds no
torch yet, so the first wall refreshed takes a floor two walls share. The terrain setter
(`0x0044FC40`) refreshes the tile and the qualifying walls beside it and two steps away; the
room-change closers recolour (command 16, `0x00448710`, colour only). Colour, intensity, radius
(clamped to `0x2780`), height and art come from the floor's room (`Rooms.kwd` `0x36E`..`0x3C7`,
flags 9 to 11 adding 255) or the balance defaults. Ours had no torches.

**Decision.** `RoomDef.Torch` reads the room's torch; `TorchLayout` (`DK2.Presentation`) keeps the
torches, laying a level out once and then repeating the setter's refreshes for each tile whose
terrain changed, and recolouring the tile and its neighbours when its room changed;
`ScenePresenter` pushes them after the tiles through three new `IRenderTarget` methods
(`CreateTorch`, `UpdateTorch`, `RemoveTorch`), and the Unity scene draws a point light with the
mesh. The meshes are catalogued per art name (`room.torch.mesh.<art>`); a room has torch art
when its torch art name is non-empty, the loader's own test. State rather than a `WorldView`
method, because a floor's winner depends on refresh order. Deviates: the level start runs the
setter's neighbour refreshes in row order with every tile already loaded and no refresh of the
tile itself (its command 3 is dropped at the closed gate), where DK2 refreshes during the load
(HYPOTHESIS, Q446); in a running game the tile's own refresh is assumed posted, after its
neighbours'; changes are found by terrain id once per frame and replayed in tile order, not in
the order the setter ran, and a setter call that changes no id is missed; a floor's room is read
from its terrain, where DK2 reads the tile's room word, which may still be empty while a level
loads (unread); the two-step refresh's world gate (vt `+0x1FC`) is taken for a bounds test; the
Torture Chamber's and Casino's furniture phase is not kept, so they use the plain parity, and so
the room-change closers' other refreshes (`0x004F0E30`, command 3) are left out as no-ops
(STRONGLY INFERRED); the terrain-art gate (inert in shipped data) is not tested; a door's own
refreshes (command 17) are not followed; the Unity light's colour over 255 and intensity over 128
are a renderer's choice.

## ADR-0392 — A room tile carries the wall pieces DK2's chooser picks for its sides
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Presentation only · Research: `wall-pieces.md`; Q71

**Context.** DK2's room loader (`0x004EACC0`) builds a room's floor and wall pieces by name, art
2's name plus a number, and its wall chooser (`0x00444F10`, read in the disassembly) gives each
side of a room tile whose outside neighbour is visible and AllowRoomWalls (Impenetrable Rock,
Reinforced Wall, Edge of Map, or a closed secret door) a whole piece, 7 or 8 at the furniture
phase, where the room runs on both ways along that wall, else two halves: 4 or 6, and 5 or 6. Ours
drew one mesh per room and per solid terrain (`AssetCatalogue`).

**Decision.** `TileView.Walls` (`RoomWalls`, four bits a side) carries the chooser's answer for the
Normal and DoubleQuad rooms, worked out by `WorldView` from the tile and its eight neighbours,
and the presenter pushes a tile again when it changes. The catalogue lists each such room's
`wall4`..`wall8` meshes and the converter makes them from `<art 2 name><k>`, as the loader names
them. Deviates: "the same room" is the same room terrain, not the tile's room word; a closed
secret door is not drawn as wall, as the neighbour or as the diagonal that continues a wall; the
diagonal's test is the terrain's Solid flag where DK2 asks the world (vt `+0x208`); a neighbour
is visible when the viewer has discovered it, where DK2 also takes Sight's view; an off-map
neighbour takes no wall; no furniture phase is kept, so a whole side is always piece 7;
the hero gates' own arms (types 0x12, 0x17) are not built; DK2's highlight of a dig-tagged wall
is not carried; the Unity scene does not draw the pieces yet, having no mesh loader; floors and
plain terrain (`floor-and-terrain-pieces.md`) stay one asset each.

## ADR-0393 — A creature at the training cap leaves the Training Room through states 108 and 110
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Answers Q509

**Context.** Q509 asked whether DK2's Harkan lifts his level-7 Black Knights into the Training
Room early, as `0x004FF5C0` reads. The Level 17 idle capture (2026-10-05) shows it: the three are
lifted at ticks 6, 7 and 11 onto (12,20) and (13,20), and each then runs 76, 255, 257, 108, 110,
1 and is lifted again, about every 27 ticks, to 220, and again at 586-597 and 888-899. Ours lifted
them at 5, 6 and 7 onto the same cells and then left them in state 108 until 676: the state
handlers that eject a creature at the cap were not built, and the drop skips the job choice that
refuses one. State 108 (`0x00485310`) sends a creature at or above
`TrainingRoomMaxExperienceLevel` to 110 after starting action 0x2C, and 110 (`0x00485580`)
returns 0 for it, which idles it.

**Decision.** After the training category hook, a creature at the cap in 108 goes to 110
(`training_refused`), and in 110 stops its job and idles. Deviates: action 0x2C is not played, nor 108's return to idle when it or the move to 110 fails,
and 111 and 112, which test the cap too, are not built.

**Measured** (hash 195), Level 17 with Harkan's AI, 950 ticks: our knights are refused at 26-28
and lifted again onto the same two cells, about every 25 ticks. Each knight's first re-lift comes
45, 57 and 73 ticks after its refusal; later ones mostly 4 to 6, as DK2's every one is 4 (108 at
29, lifted at 33). The first gap is ours to explain (Q509).

## ADR-0394 — The room planner searches from a room's stored position, in DK2's direction order
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Advances Q555 and Q563

**Context.** Level 11A's capture holds Morgana's task pool: she tags (62,36), (59,36) and a Lair
at (56-58, 35-37). Ours tagged every one a row north. The site search (`0x005012A0`) and its
direction table match ours; its origin did not. `0x004FC690` starts from a room's stored position
(`+0x27`, `KeeperView.PositionOf`), which for a heart is its first slab plus three, (66,36) for
Morgana, where ours took the bounding-box middle (65,35). `0x004FCE70` also tries the preferred
direction, then +1, -1 and +2, and only then, on `random(100) > 4`, restores the preferred
direction and reseeds from `0x004C63D0`'s one draw over all rooms (a bridge yields none); ours
stepped +1 four times and reseeded from any room's middle. The neutral-room branch reads `+0x27`
for its target and for the nearest own room, its origin, and measures a portal's range from the
portal's first slab; the retreat's Lair drop is `+0x27` too (`0x004FF260`).

**Decision.** `RoomPlanner.Origin`, `RoomPlanner.NextSearchDirection`, `KeeperAI.FindSite`'s
reseed, `RoomPlanner.ClaimableNeutralRoom` and `KeeperRetreatStep.Destination` follow those reads;
`KeeperView.RandomNonBridgeRoom` and `NearestOwnRoomByPosition` serve them, walking the room list
newest first as DK2's does. Deviates: the neutral candidate ranking (`0x004C61C0`) keeps the
middle, as do the planner's readers whose field is unread; the Lair drop lands on the tile, not
DK2's `+0x900` (as ADR-0317's drops). No hash change: the keeper AI issues commands and holds no
simulation state.

**Measured.** Level 11A: Morgana tags (56-58, 35-37) at 6 and (62,36) at 8, (59,36) at 100 (DK2
202, 8, 106: ours tags the rectangle before the path, Q566). Level 17 with keepers 4 and 5: Harkan
lays his Prison first, 616-713 on (16,18)-(20,22), DK2's 855-922 on the same 25 tiles (before:
1,336, second). Level 11A over ten seeds is not closer: call 472-608, Morgana falls 808-1,052
(DK2 700, 1,378; Q563); the scenario's seed 12345, outside those ten, calls at 613.

## ADR-0395 — A searched room site gets its joining path first, and task 3 builds at its cursor
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Answers Q566 and Q555, advances Q563

**Context.** Both captures dig a new room's path before its rectangle: Morgana's path at 8 and 106
and her Lair at 202 (Level 11A), Harkan's path tile at 381 and his Prison at 500 (Level 17). Ours
tagged the rectangle first and dug a path only when a flood from the heart could not reach it. On
success the site search (`0x005012A0`) stores its origin at `+0x86`, where its walk stopped at
`+0x82` (`side/2` along the near edge) and a zero cursor; Task 2 (`0x004FD030`) answers the zero cursor with task 7 from the
first to the second, continuation 2, spending nothing and testing nothing, then tags in walking
order. Task 3 (`0x004FD2B0`) builds only at its cursor, from the square's unflipped corner, holding
on a solid or unowned tile; ours built any ready tile, so DK2 waited 355 ticks for its first
Prison tile where ours waited about 40.

**Decision.** `SiteFinder.Search` returns the join point, corner and steps; `KeeperAI` keeps them
(`JoinPathStart/End`, `JoinPathPending`, `RectangleStart`, `RectangleStepX/Y`), digs the path first,
tags and builds in walking order with task 3's cursor, and drops the reach flood. A failed walk now
takes `NextTask`, as `0x004FDFA3` does; ADR-0304 abandoned only because task 2 would have detoured
again. Deviates: one build a tick, our build landing a tick later; the dig pool's 20-free gate is
not modelled; task 2 tags only taggable tiles not yet tagged, where DK2 dispatches on every tile and
retries a zero result (the handler's result is unread); task 3 tags a held tile not tagged by this
keeper, where DK2 tests kind 1/2 by anyone. An expansion skips the path as DK2's does once a
searched site has set `+0x82`; whether one can come first is unread. No hash change: the keeper AI holds no simulation state.

**Measured.** Ten seeds each. Level 11A: Morgana's path at 7 and 100-104, her Lair at 111-196;
the call at 455-696 (was 472-608, DK2 700), on DK2's (64,38) in 8 (was 1); Morgana falls
858-1,093 (808-1,052, DK2 1,378). Level 17: the Prison's site is a draw over Harkan's rooms, DK2's
in 6 (3 on master); there it is laid from (16,22) as DK2's, first tile 557-868 (DK2 855).

## ADR-0396 — A gambler moves among the Casino's furniture, and a jackpot starts a party and a collection
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Completes ADR-0187, ADR-0313 · Raises Q572 · Research: `casino.md`

**Context.** A gambler stood in state 145 while the Casino's hook charged it; 146–153 and the jackpot
were unread. Read whole: 145 (`0x00456160`) chooses a party, a free table, a free alcove or a bare
tile and walks there; 146–151 face the object, play an action and return; the hook's roll calls
`0x004D6AA0`, which kicks the room's other gamblers into 153, counts a party on the keeper
(`+0xF4A`, which lifts the purse tests) and sends the winner through 152 and 155–157 to a Treasury;
the room update ends the party after 90 seconds, and a missed deadline angers the keeper's creatures.

**Decision.** `CasinoStep` runs 145–151 and 153, `CasinoJackpotRules` the jackpot, the party and
152, 155–157, with `CasinoJackpotSystem` for the drunk timer and the deadline. Action lengths come
from the creature's art: `CreatureDef.ArtSlots` holds every block and `AnimationTimingRules`
resolves a missing slot by DK2's switch; a counted action plays count + 1 times (LIKELY, as the
prison's flourish). DK2's literals stay literals: 25 % and 45 seconds drunk (the shipped drink
variables have no reader), 90 seconds of party, 10 of celebration. Deviates: a kicked creature's
new state runs from the next turn; sounds, the wheel's spin (its draw kept), the drunk walk and
effects are not kept; DK2's room object order breaks a finder tie, ours the world's; the party
branch's finder messages are not built. A drinker stands 45°–135° from its alcove whatever its
wall, so a south wall's alcove refuses the walk (Q572).

**Measured** (hash 196) against master `95daa5f6`, both sides run: Level 1 20/20 and 20/20, Level
2 2/20 and 2/20 (seeds 14 and 17), Level 3 seed 01 won at 3560 and 3560 (DK2 3683). No shipped
level of the three has a Casino, so every run is identical.

## ADR-0397 — A researcher moves among the Library's shelves, and an intruder disturbs a long read
**Date:** 2026-10-06 · **Status:** accepted · Completes Q438's Library half · Research: `library-states.md`

**Context.** A researcher stood in state 53 while the Research hook credited it; 54–59 were unread
or unbuilt, and idle-fallback.md §6's disturbed-room rule waited for them. Read whole: 53
(`0x00475A20`) walks to the nearest free Book Case or Library Book, or a random free bare tile
(`0x004E1ED0`); 54 faces it and reads, action 29, long at a slot (56) or short on a bare tile (57);
the reads return to 53, or leave a Library holding a creature the reader objects to when another has
a place; an intruder on a Library tile sends a worried long reader into 59, which watches it and
hurries it out. 55 and 58 share the stub that returns 0, and nothing enters them.

**Decision.** `ResearchStep` runs 53, 54, 56, 57 and 59; the contact test runs the Library arm of
`0x004E8660`; `RoomCapacityRules.FindRoomWithPlace` mirrors `0x004C6AE0` returning the room.
55 and 58 are unreachable by Q415's method. The object's position (`+0x1A`) moves `0x700` toward
its wall for a Library Book as for the Casino's alcove (`AutoFurnitureRules.FurniturePosition`).
Deviates: a state entered this turn runs from the next; `0x004C6AE0` measures to the room's

`0x004E1AC0` inside the capacity test is not built for any caller. Two corrections land with it: a
