## ADR-0398 — The modern Imp looks like the approved concepts and moves like the shipped mesh
**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** accepted (owner) · Presentation only · Amends ADR-0242 for the Imp

**Context.** ADR-0242 makes the originals authoritative. The Imp has three sources. The shipped
mesh and texture (`Imp_Idle1`, `impfrnt`/`impback`): tan-orange skin, dark eyes, no separate ears,
187 triangles, a large sack, the pick in the right hand (Q568). A DK2 portrait the owner supplied
(445×280, SHA-256 `35d7d318…`, `dk2_portrait.png`, not yet located in the install): olive skin,
huge dark-red eyes, pointed ears, teeth. And two AI-generated concept renders made from that
portrait (`portrait.png` `0c03e77e…`, `front_side_back.png` `41a3fe06…`, 2026-10-07), which the
owner approved as the modern appearance target. The renders are not game assets and not evidence
of any DK2 detail. All under `build/modern/creature/imp/reference/`.

**Decision.** The approved concepts guide the modern **appearance**: face, anatomy, clothing and
materials. The original DK2 resources guide **scale, movement and gameplay compatibility**: height
0.36 tiles, every clip's motion and timing, and the pick in the right hand by default. Skin
colour is one adjustable base colour (`skin_color` on `IMP_skin`); eyes, teeth, clothing and
equipment never take it. Olive, gray, earthy brown and muted red are previews, not a runtime
system. The converted originals stay the classic look (Goal 11), unchanged.

**Deliberate departures from the original**, each the owner's choice:
- skin colour (olive, not the texture's tan-orange); ears, teeth, riveted braces and a buckled
  belt, which the mesh does not show; ankle wraps and leather foot straps, which the DK2 portrait
  shows and the in-game mesh's bare feet do not (`docs/plans/2026-10-07-imp-footwear.md`);
- the concept's **smaller, higher sack** by default; the original's large sack is kept as a
  possible equipment variant;
- an optional **left-handed** variant (ADR-0399).

The concepts' egg-shaped **belly plate** is part of the harness. The braces end under its upper
rim and the belt crosses its lower part, as in `portrait.png`. It replaces the planned skull
ornament (owner, 2026-10-08). Nose and ear
piercings are optional separate accessories; the base creature has no jewellery. Inputs, hashes,
regions and the intended split into parts: `art/manifests/creature/imp.yaml`.

**Consequences.** Under `ART_DIRECTION.md` §3 these departures would be level D. Here they are
owner decisions recorded per item, so this ADR is the one place that admits them for the Imp. A
concept detail is never cited as a DK2 fact. The base-colour ΔE check against the shipped
texture (`ASSET_PIPELINE.md` §7) does not apply to the skin; the owner's review against the
concepts replaces it. The silhouette check against the original mesh remains a diagnostic, except
for the listed departures. Blockout state and open details: `docs/plans/2026-10-07-imp-blockout.md`.

**History.** First accepted on 2026-10-07 with the DK2 portrait as the appearance source and the
shipped mesh for proportions, pick and sack. The same day the owner approved the AI concept
renders made from that portrait as the target instead. With them came the smaller sack, the
left-handed variant, the rejection of the belly plate, and piercings as accessories. On
2026-10-08 the owner asked for the front to match the portrait. The belly plate was restored and
replaced the planned chest skull ornament, which had never been built.

## ADR-0399 — The Imp is right-handed; a left-handed variant shares its mesh and rig
**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** accepted (owner) · Presentation only · Refines ADR-0398

**Context.** DK2's Imp holds its pick in its right hand: the owner's play and the converted mesh
agree (Q568). The approved AI concept renders (ADR-0398: `portrait.png`, `front_side_back.png`)
show it in the left.

**Decision.** Right-handed is the default, as DK2's. A left-handed appearance and animation
variant is optional, and both variants use the **same base mesh and rig**: the pick is a separate
object, each hand gets a pickaxe attachment point, and handedness is an appearance setting stored
apart from skin colour and accessory choices. The whole model is never mirrored: face, costume
and sack are asymmetric and would flip with it. A left-handed clip is made at rigging time by
mirroring suitable skeletal poses and then adjusting the working clips (dig, claim and the like)
so that the grip, the pick's trajectory and body and sack clearance stay correct. The concept's
left-hand placement is a reference for that variant only; it does not change the default.

**Consequences.** The modelling milestone keeps the pick separate and models both hands able to
hold it. The left-handed variant is a documented departure from DK2, chosen per Imp in
presentation; the simulation never sees it, so no hash or schema changes. Animation work for it
waits for the rig (`ASSET_PIPELINE.md` §5).

## ADR-0400 — The first eight category 0 states: a neutral idle, the Heart's drop, the tunneller's wander, the evicted holders' way back, the gold cheer
**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `refused-states.md`, `temple-states.md` §8

**Context.** Eight states the original files under category 0 were unbuilt: 5, 69, 71, 86, 113,
126, 135, 211. Read, with every entry, by a call scan and a raw byte scan: 5 is the idle every
neutral creature in state 1 takes (ours sent only a fleeing one); 69 is entered and left within
68's one call; 71 is the Heart's drop state, which pays a non-worker its wages and gives a worker
on the Heart's inner 3×3 back for Create Imp's mana; 86 is a tunneller's wander when its planner
gives up, on 186's fields as they stand; 113 and 126 are where a rebuilt Training Room's and
Prison's holders wait a turn before going back in, as the Temple's 107; 135 is the kick a willing
torturee takes before answering a Call to Arms; 211 is the gold celebration. Reading 5 found that
a Bile Demon's idle action makes a shot one time in ten, not a sound. The owner answered Q570 (a
creature cheers when gold lands on it) and corrected the Temple: an offering is made only in the
pool.

**Decision.** Built: 5 (every neutral creature, sharing state 3's body, which now draws the Bile
Demon's roll and makes shot `0x35`, the Heal Instant Shot, whose data words are 0: it dies on its
first turn and its death shot heals by 0), 71 (`DropLandingRules.HeartDrop`, and a worker getting
up on a Heart goes there instead of idle), 86 (`TunnelRules.Wander`, the mixed units as read), 113
and 126 (`RoomEvictRules`, which the Temple's 107 now uses too), 135 (`CallToArmsRules.Recruit`,
kicked before the route test), 211 (`DropDeliveryRules.Celebrate` at the Hand's gold delivery to a
creature holding no place). 69 is unreachable. The Temple's offering is made only on a pool tile,
one the Temple surrounds: by the Hand's drop (creature or object) and by 101 (`TempleStep.Sacrifice`).
Deviates: a rebuilt room is seen at the holder's next turn by its size stamp, and a freed room or
new owner is left to the job's room test or the Prison's release; the neighbour-terrain trigger
`0x004E44E0` and 76's worker arm are not built; 71 runs in the turn it is entered; the Heart object
is a living Heart; 126's neutral owner change and the Heart's responder kick to 135 are not built;
the Hand offers a creature in the pool at the drop, where DK2 offers it in 101 after the drop's stun.

**Measured** (hash 200) against the branch at `5e504d86` (M-D), both sides run: Level 1 20/20 and

## ADR-0401 — The slap's state moves: 67, 77 and 120 and their reaction
**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `slap-states.md`

**Context.** The slap `0x0048B8A0` moves a creature before it does anything else to it: to 67 when
it holds a place in its slapper's Workshop, to 120 in its slapper's Prison, otherwise to 77; when
`SetState` refuses the move the slap returns with no damage, anger, speed or count. All three run
the reaction `0x0046F1F0`: action 19, then back to the room's state or idle. Ours made none of the
moves (ADR-0373), so every slap landed in full and a slapped creature carried on. The owner asked
for them to be built (Q569).

**Decision.** `SlapRules.Move` in `HandSystem.Slap`'s main path, a refusal being the slap ignored;
`SlapRules.React` in `CreatureStatusSystem` for every creature in 67, 77 or 120 (a new activity,
`Slapped`): action 19 at the first turn (art slot 4, its length the counted clip, LIKELY), held while
it runs, then 63, 115 or 130 by the held room, a worker 10, anyone else idle. The transition table
refuses 10 from 77, so a slapped worker idles and goes to 10 from 1. Deviates: the knock-back's
velocity and its stop at a rival's or a locked door's tile are not modelled; a Horny is not
slappable in ours, so 242 and 238 are not reached. The owner confirmed from play (2026-10-07) that a
slapped Imp flinches, then digs on faster.

Level 11A's keeper scenario changes outcome: Drako's slapped imps lose Morgana's hole, the front
goes west and the call stands on (37,37) with no attack on Morgana's heart inside 700 ticks, where
DK2's call stands two tiles off her heart. Re-pinned with the owner's consent; a divergence to
watch (Q574).

**Measured** (hash 203; built on ADR-0402's 202, so 201 is unused) against the branch at
`c1142b9b` (M-F), both sides run: Level 1 20/20 and 20/20, Level 2 2/20 and 2/20 (seeds 3, 13),
Level 3 seed 01 won at 3676 and 3676 (DK2 3683).

## ADR-0403 — A worshipper moves about the Temple, and every job walk ends where DK2's room walk does
**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `temple-states.md` · Numbered ADR-0398 on its branch, renumbered at the merge

**Context.** A worshipper stood in state 101 while the Temple's hook prayed for it; 102–107 were
unread. Read whole: 101 takes a creature on its own Temple to 103 (in the pool it is the offering);
103 picks its own tile or a free neighbour and walks to a point a quarter tile out from the room's
centre; 104 faces the centre and prays, action 27 two or three more plays; 105 waits it out, steps
its definition's vector 1 ahead and chooses again. 106 is the creature a sacrifice makes, walked off
the pool; 107 takes a holder back in after its Temple is freed, rebuilt or changes owner
(`0x004F15D0`, the Temple's room-type slots +0x05, +0x09, +0x0D). 102 is `SetState(101)` and
nothing enters it. Building them showed that ours walked every job to its room's centre, which in a
Temple is the pool; DK2's room walk ends at `0x004E4C10`'s point, never a furniture slot.

**Decision.** `TempleStep` runs 101 and 103–107; 102 is unreachable by Q415's method. The sacrifice
reward kicks its creature to 106 (`HandSystem`). `CreatureDef.PrayerStepX/Y` reads file `0x127B`
(the definition's vector 1). `RoomWalkRules.ArrivalTile` is `0x004E4C10`, and `CreatureJobSystem`
uses it for every job room, entering the state at once when the creature is already in the room.
Deviates: a state entered this turn runs from the next; 107 is seen at the holder's next turn by
the Temple's size stamp against `CreatureState.HeldPlaceStamp` (set at the claim), not inside the
rebuild; 101's offering stays the Hand's (ADR-0149), which sacrifices on any Temple tile where DK2
sacrifices only in the pool; ours ends a walk within the creature's own tile at once, so 103's
quarter-tile point is reached only from another tile; 103's refused walk goes idle rather than to
another Temple; the job walk draws the room point for each candidate before routing, where DK2 draws once for the room its finder settled.

**Measured** (hash 198) against the branch at `71d1a0dc` (M-B), both sides run: Level 1 20/20 and
20/20, Level 2 2/20 (seeds 5, 13) and 5/20 (seeds 3, 5, 10, 13, 14), Level 3 seed 01 won at 3560
and 3608 (DK2 3683). None of the three replays builds a Temple (their room-build events): the move is the room walk's point,
which every job takes. The owner accepted Level 2's move past one seed (2026-10-07).

## ADR-0405 — The keeper slaps on the last task kind; a repair is kind 16
**Date:** 2026-10-08 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `computer-keeper-management.md` §8; Q574

**Context.** Since the slap's reaction (ADR-0401) Level 11A's scenario seed lost Morgana's hole and
its front turned west. Over ten seeds the change was not one seed's: before ADR-0401 Drako attacked
Morgana first in 10 of 10, after it in 6. The slap step's worker test `0x00478A20` reads the state
object's `+0x98`, the last task kind, which each task handler writes as it takes the task and state
10 zeroes before it chooses again (`0x00464010`). Ours tested a held reinforce target, so an imp
drawn from a reinforce into a fight was never slapped, and ours recorded a repair as kind 6 where
`0x0046AEA0` writes 16. DK2's Level 11A capture slaps Morgana's imps fighting in the hole (state
199, kind 6) and slaps its keepers' eligible imps at 0.82 % a tick (53 of 6,429), consistent with
the 1-in-100 roll if the step runs every tick (unread).

**Decision.** `CreatureActivityRules.Code` gives a worker 5 for `WorkerIdle` or `LastTaskKind` 6.
`ImpTaskKind.Fix` (16) is recorded for a repair, searched by the reinforce arm as `0x00468520`
searches 6 and 16 alike. No new field.

**Consequences.** The remaining spread on Level 11A is the roll itself: when Morgana's keeper slaps
the imp reinforcing (64,38) before it finishes, the tile stays rock and falls at 72-88; when her
repairer has moved west, it falls at 241-294; otherwise near DK2's 387. Over seeds 1-10 Drako
attacks Morgana first in 6. DK2's one capture fits a draw from that spread (its Morgana slaps once
in her first 200 ticks against 2.8 expected at that rate), so it cannot separate the two; more DK2 seeds of
Level 11A would. The scenario's seed 12345 attacks Morgana again (call (64,34) at 364). Level 17's
seed 12345 builds no Prison inside 3,000 ticks, one seed of 31; seeds 1-30 build it at 548-875
(master 548-851), so the scenario moves to seed 13.

**Measured** (hash 204) against master `acfe743a`, both sides run: Level 1 20/20 and 20/20, Level 2
2/20 and 2/20 (seeds 3, 13), Level 3 seed 01 won at 3676 and 3676 (DK2 3683): every seed's result
unchanged.

## ADR-0406 — A room's holders are kicked when it is freed, taken, or a neighbouring tile changes
**Date:** 2026-10-08 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `room-return-states.md` §1; Q575

**Context.** Besides a rebuild, DK2 kicks a room's place-holders to its return state from the type's
slots `+0x05` (freed) and `+0x0D` (owner changed, from `Room_TransferOwnership`), each of which
reaches every holder, from `+0x11` (a load; the Library's only) and from `0x004E44E0`.
`Tile_SetTerrain` calls `0x004E44E0` for each N/E/S/W neighbour that is a room tile; for a
definition with `SpecialWalls` it kicks a Library's holder to 62, a Training Room's to 113, a
Workshop's to 70, a Torture Chamber's to 136 and a Casino's to 154 (the Prison has the flag and no
arm). It kicks one holder a call: the loop follows the kicked creature's own link, which the kick's
release zeroes, so only the list's head, the latest claimant, goes. The Torture Chamber's `+0x05` and
`+0x0D` are `0x004F1FB0` and its `+0x09` (`0x004F1F10`) kicks to 136 first. Ours kicked only on a
rebuild; a freed or taken room ended the job at the next game second.

**Decision.** A claim records a serial (`HeldPlaceSerial`, from `WorldState.NextPlaceClaim`).
`SlabChain.KickNeighbours`, run on a terrain change from `SlabChain.Changed`, the defeat's fallen
tiles and the trigger's terrain action, marks the highest-serial unmarked holder of each qualifying
neighbour room (`HeldPlaceStamp` = `KickedMark`). An ownership change, by conversion or defeat,
stamps the room (`RoomKickedTick`), which a holder's claim stamp (`SlabChain.HoldersStamp`) then
differs from. `RoomEvictRules.Evict` takes the job's room type and kicks on either, or when the held
tile is no longer that type (freed). A Torture Chamber's victim so kicked goes through 136 as for a
lost device. Deviates: the kick lands at the holder's next turn; a head whose kick the transition
table refuses is not passed over for the next; the Library's load slot is not built, so a saved game
plays on as an unsaved one would; the Library's books, the Workshop's crates and the Casino's effect
on a freed or taken room are not moved.

**Consequences.** A wall dug, reinforced or claimed beside a Library, Training Room, Workshop,
Torture Chamber or Casino sends its latest occupant out of its state and back in. A sold room's
holder passes through its return state before it idles.

**Measured** (hash 205) against `9bbfdfed` (ADR-0405), both sides run: Level 1 20/20 and 20/20, every seed
unchanged; Level 2 2/20 and 2/20 (seeds 3 and 13 before, 10 and 13 after); Level 3 seed 01 won at
3676 and 3584 (DK2 3683). Level 11A seeds 1-10 unchanged but one heart strike; Level 17 seeds 1-10
build the same Prisons at the same ticks, later rooms shift.

## ADR-0407 — A Dungeon Heart sends its owner's creatures to an intruder
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `combat-alarm.md` §7; Q563, Q574

**Context.** In DK2's Level 11A seeds whose wall at (64,38) falls before 100, Drako buys two or
three imps and then spends 5,000 mana every 70 ticks or so; ours bought five and seldom cast.
DK2's Drako has a creature fighting on 348-403 of the first 500 ticks there, because the moment
the wall opens Morgana's nearby imps walk to Drako's digger, resuming 254, and fight it in the
hole; the fight flag puts the keeper's battle step in place of imp buying. Ours had no such
walk, so the imps parted. The sender is the tail of the heart's room update `0x004D9690`: every
fourth turn, an attackable enemy within `DungeonHeartReportingDistanceTiles` (4) of the heart
sends every owner's creature within `DungeonHeartCreatureGatheringDistanceTiles` (7) that may go,
workers included, running to it. Neither variable was read.

**Decision.** `HeartDefenceSystem`, after the store sweep, does that dispatch with DK2's
refusals (Horny, Call to Arms, Combat category, `0x0045A6D0`, a quarter of health, group tag 3,
a dropped job, already walking to 254), its Imp route flag and its run, into the alarm's state
254 (ADR-0166). A table without the two variables has no dispatch. Deviates: DK2's phase is the
heart room's id, `(turn + room+4) & 3`; ours has none and gives every heart Morgana's, 1100 (the
other Level 11A hearts are 1097, 1101, 1105 and 1107); the ruin gate is the player's, not the
room's; a willing torturee is not kicked to 135 first.

**Consequences.** A breached wall within four tiles of a heart is defended by everyone near it.
`level11a_drako_attack.yaml` moves to seed 7, whose wall falls at 369 (DK2's idle capture 387)
and whose call stays on Morgana; seed 12345 now calls west, after Belial's tunnel opens (Q574).

**Measured** (hash 206) against `9adc142a`, both sides run. Level 11A seeds 1-10: Morgana first in
8 (6 before: seeds 2, 3, 8 and 9 turned to her, 4 and 5 west); the early-fall seeds 2-4 buy 3-4
imps before 700 (5, 5, 3) and Heal 3-5 times (0-2); in seed 7 11 imps engage in the fight, 5 of
Drako's and 6 of Morgana's (3 and 3; DK2's capture 6 of Drako's and 5 of hers). Level 1 20/20 both, median win 1792 both;
Level 2 4/20 (seeds 10, 13, 14, 17; before 10 and 13); Level 3 seed 01 won at 3660 (3584; DK2
3683); Level 17 seeds 1-10 unchanged.

## ADR-0408 — The classic look is read from the player's install, and both looks render through URP
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted (owner) · Presentation only · Refines ADR-0034, ADR-0242 · Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-09-classic-look.md`

**Context.** `GOAL_ALIGNMENT.md` gap 5: the Unity scene draws boxes. `DK2.Convert` decodes every KMF
and engine texture and writes GLB and PNG, but `DungeonScene.Instantiate` has no loader, Unity
ships no runtime glTF importer, and `DK2.Convert` builds for net10.0 only, so Unity cannot call it.
`ASSET_PIPELINE.md` §11 left two owner decisions open: the render pipeline, and how Unity receives
assets.

**Decision.**
1. **The classic look is read from the player's own install at run time.** `KmfReader`, the
   engine-texture decoder and what they need build for netstandard2.1 (`UnityBound.props`), as
   `DK2.Convert` or as a reader assembly split from its writers, and join `sync-assemblies.ps1`.
   They decode into engine-neutral mesh and image data; only the Unity adapter makes `Mesh`,
   `Texture2D` and materials. No glTF package is added and a player runs no conversion step.
2. **ADR-0034's converted tier may resolve a key to an entry in the install**, not only to a file
   under a converter's output. The chain order `replacement → converted → placeholder` and the
   total placeholder are unchanged. `GlbWriter` and `dk2tools convert` stay, for the asset
   workstation and the replacement tier (ADR-0242).
3. **The project moves to the Universal Render Pipeline (URP)** before anything depends on the
   built-in one. The classic and modern looks are two material and lighting sets over one scene
   and one view, selected as data.
4. **Which piece, rotation and texture a tile shows is decided in `DK2.Presentation`** and tested
   headlessly, as `RoomWalls` is (ADR-0392); Unity places what the view lists and decides nothing.
5. **The classic look is judged against DK2**: each plan step ends with a screenshot beside DK2's at
   the same place and camera, and the owner accepts it.

**Why.**
- The player owns the files and nothing derived from them leaves the install, which is what
  AGENTS.md's no-redistribution rule allows. One reader serves the converter, the tests and the
  game, so a format fact has one home.
- A runtime glTF importer would re-read what `KmfReader` already decodes, and would add a package
  and a conversion step the classic look does not need.
- URP carries both looks: unlit or vertex-lit materials for the classic one; physically based
  materials, shadows and post-processing for the modern one; and the hardware range a creature
  crowd needs. HDRP narrows the hardware and makes the classic look harder; the built-in pipeline
  would need every modern feature added later. Only placeholder boxes depend on the pipeline
  today, so the switch costs least now.

**Consequences.**
- `ASSET_PIPELINE.md` §11 items 1 and 2 are decided for the classic look; the modern tier's
  interchange format stays PoC step 7's choice.
- An engine-neutrality test asserts the newly Unity-bound assembly targets netstandard2.1, as
  `AssetArchitectureTests` and the `EngineNeutralityTests` do for theirs.
- ADR-0034's one mesh per solid terrain ends with the plan's terrain and room steps; the variant
  list comes from `floor-and-terrain-pieces.md` and `wall-pieces.md`.
- Unread facts block later steps, not the first: water and lava beds (Q71), which clip a state
  plays, Q442's remaining link, and DK2's camera and lighting.

## ADR-0409 — An unaffordable room routes to the stored gold slot, and a neutral room is ranked by its first slab
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `computer-keeper-observations.md` (*The opening*), `computer-keeper-spell-sites.md` §2; Q539

**Context.** On Level 17 DK2's Harkan tags (4,8) at tick 12 toward the neutral Portal at
(1..3,6..8), then the path to his seam at 65 ((19,4)) and the seam from 134; ours tagged (19,4)
at 4 and, at 105, the own wall (8,4)
toward the other Portal, which DK2 never digs. Three reads of the room planner explain it. The
cost arm (`0x004FC9AE`) copies the stored gold slot whatever its amount and starts nothing while
a seam is tagged (`0x004FC9A1`); ours took the fresh scan's deposit when none was stored. The
neutral search (`0x004FC799` → `0x004C61C0`) ranks the neutral player's rooms, newest first, by
first slab from the heart position; ours ranked by bounding-box middle in tile order. Task 5
(`0x004FD660`, read whole) digs from the stored position of the own room nearest the target;
ours from the bounding-box middle of the nearest by middle.

**Decision.** `KeeperAI.CostArm` is the cost arm: no task while the pool's kind-2 count is
nonzero, else `DigRoomAt` is the stored slot's tile or (0,0), the rescan, task 5. Deviates: the
count is read as this keeper's tags on gold rock; what makes a kind-2 entry is unread. `RoomPlanner.ClaimableNeutralRoom` walks the rooms newest first by first
slab. `RouteToGold` takes `NearestOwnRoomByPosition` and its `PositionOf`. Deviates: the walker's
search for the far side of undiggable rock (`0x00502230`) has no bound in DK2; a target inside the
map's border with nothing open beyond it (task 5 toward (0,0) on an all-rock map) would step
across it and back for ever, and `LineWalker` now stops after width + height steps and fails the
walk, as its wall hug already does.

**Consequences.** Harkan's opening is DK2's: (4,8) first, the seam after a Portal pass. Where the
two Portals tie (37 from the heart position (7,7)) he goes to (1..3,6..8) as DK2 does. No
HashVersion: the keeper is outside the simulation (`KeeperAI`'s remarks) and no rule changed. (8,4) is still tagged in four of ten seeds,
while the second Portal is being claimed.

**Measured** against `8b355528`, both sides run. Level 17 seeds 1-10: Prison first in all ten, first
tile 708-879 (663-865; DK2 855); a Training Room at 1049-1307 in nine (1028-2337 in six; DK2 grows
its own at about 1,200); a Torture Chamber in one (seven; DK2 none); (8,4) tagged in four (ten).
Level 11A seeds 1-30: Morgana first in 22 (22).

## ADR-0410 — The nine lobby personalities load as DK2's setter loads them
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `KEEPER_AI.md` §3.2; `functions/004F8C60.md`

**Context.** A skirmish or multiplayer slot gets its keeper from the personality setter
`0x004F8C60`, not from a PLAYERS record (KEEPER_AI.md §1.2). Ours had only the record path, so no
keeper could play skirmish.

**Decision.** `KeeperAIPersonality.Parameters` is the setter: the level-name remap (`0x006A30A0`,
case-sensitive), then row p of the seven tables, every column decoded from the bytes, the skill
level capped at variable 192, the room list of the first fifteen Buildable rooms or Portals in
id order, the whole map less its edge as the build area, and every feature flag on. It returns
the same `KeeperAIParameters` the record path does. The harness takes it per keeper through the
scenario key `keeper_personalities`.

**Consequences.** All nine personalities run. On Level 17, Harkan's slot given each in turn (1,500
ticks) lays his Prison under every one; Psychotic, whose neutral range is 40, tags 387 tiles where
the others tag 16-30. Deviates: `RawBlock` is empty; with fewer than fifteen qualifying room
definitions DK2 faults (`+0x98` finds none past the end) where ours fills with 0; the shipped
rooms never reach it. The setter also adds 100 mana (misc +8, `0x004C19C0`), as the PLAYERS path
does; the harness keeps the level's mana, which that path already added. No HashVersion: the keeper is outside the simulation.

## ADR-0411 — The renderer frame is X east, Y up, Z north, and the map is no longer mirrored
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted; the unmirrored layout CONFIRMED for Level 1 by the owner's
comparison with DK2's on 2026-10-09 (plan, step 0 gate) · Presentation only · Step 0 of ADR-0408's plan

**Context.** DK2's frame is X east, Y south, Z down: right-handed, since the editor shows a map
from above with X right and Y down. Unity's is left-handed. `DungeonScene` put tile Y on Unity's
+Z, so every level was drawn as its mirror image, and a KMF placed with the same numbers would
have been mirrored too. No test could see it; only a picture beside DK2's can.

**Decision.** The renderer frame is X east, Y up, Z north, one unit a tile. A DK2 point maps as
`(x, -z, -y)` (`RenderMesh.ToRenderFrame`, `DungeonScene.Ground`), every mesh keeps DK2's own
triangle order, and the picker's ray is mapped back to DK2's plane. A torch's yaw keeps its
old formula: the sign and zero of DK2's yaw are unread (plan, step 2).

**Why.** A reflection in numbers is what draws a right-handed world unmirrored in a left-handed
engine, and it flips the winding once, as the engine's handedness does, so the stored order
stands. The glTF writer's rotation `(x, -z, y)` with reversed triangles (Q568) is right for
glTF's right-handed frame and is unchanged.

**Consequences.** `RenderMeshTests` pins the mapping, that a wall piece at DK2 Y = -0.5 lands on a
tile's north edge, and that triangle order agrees with the KMF's stored normals. The opening
camera now faces north. That DK2's Y runs south, and so that the old layout was a mirror, rested on
the editor's view; the owner's comparison of the Level 1 picture with DK2's confirmed it: the same
layout, only the camera angle differs. The floor is drawn at DK2's 0x1000, one tile
(`0x004545C0`, read), so a wall's KMF (1 to 2) stands one tile above it: that the KMF's heights
share the floor's frame is STRONGLY INFERRED, and the owner judged the proportions right by eye.

## ADR-0412 — The rescue selector posts its room messages, and a Prison's Activation is on from its first tile
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `computer-keeper-messages.md` §2; `functions/0046D810.md`, `004E2B30.md`

**Context.** The rescue selector `0x0046D810` settles a Lair and a Prison result once per scan and
posts 41, 43 or 42 for each body it meets whose room is missing, unreachable or full. Its routed
search `0x004C6610` needs a Prison's `Activation` (`+0x59`). Ours posted nothing, carried an enemy
to any Prison with a free cell, and started every Prison with `Activation` off (Q542).

**Decision.** `RoomNeedRules.RescueResult` is the selector's test: the count of the type
(`0x004C5FD0`; none is result 1 at availability 3), a room with a place (`0x004C6510`; none is 3),
then one whose position (`+0x2B`, the tile nearest the centroid that `0x00454110` rejects) the
`0x80` route reaches and, for a Prison, whose `Activation` is on (none is 2). `ImpTaskSystem`'s body
search asks it the first time a casualty needs it and posts through `RoomNeedRules.ForRescue`: an
enemy's Prison result, or a bedless own creature's Lair result. Like the selector, it meets only
bodies on tiles the worker's keeper owns (the cell's owner word), so it neither posts nor carries
for a body lying elsewhere. An
enemy is carried only on result 4, and `PrisonRules.FreeTileIn` skips a Prison whose `Activation`
is off. `Activation` is set where `0x004E2B30` sets it, at one tile: `SlabChain` keeps the byte on
the room's lowest tile, a growing room keeps the joined room's byte, a sale gives each piece the
old byte (`0x004ED440`), and `RoomRules.Place` and `WorldState.FromMap` set it for a Prison tile
laid or loaded (a new level's loader inserts its tiles one by one, `0x0051EC60` → `0x004C5C30`).

**Consequences.** Levels 1-3 replays are unchanged (20/20, 4/20, Level 3 seed 1 at 3660): no
rescue message fires on them. Deviates: DK2 carries a bedless own creature to a Lair with a place
(result 4); ours leaves it. DK2 settles its two results once per state update, ours once per
body search; the `+0x2B` spiral's order is not read (ours takes the nearest tile). A sealed Prison now refuses a body that ours used to carry in.

## ADR-0413 — The job-room finders post their remaining messages, and a Temple or Combat Pit holds one per rim tile
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `computer-keeper-messages.md` §2; `functions/004E2500.md`, `004D8870.md`, `004E3ED0.md`

**Context.** The finders' message branches stopped at 41 for the Library and the Workshop, the
Casino's party branch and the Mistress's 99 were not carried, the Temple had no capacity, so its
44 could not arise, and neither Combat Pit finder posted anything (Q543).

**Decision.** `RoomNeedRules.NoJobRoomFor` gates the Workshop's 43/42/44 on its queue
(`+0xA1C`), restricts the Casino's first loop to Casinos with a party on while `+0xF4A` is set,
and posts 99 (`RoomWanted`) for a Mistress's missing Torture Chamber. `NoLibraryFor` mirrors
`0x004E2500`: a shelf draw (`0x004E1AC0`) per reachable Library, then 41, the research-target
return, 43 (another draw each), 45 (`RoomStorageFull`), 42 and 44. `NoSpectatorPitFor`
(`0x004D8510`) runs when job 26 finds no pit; `NoFightingPitFor` (`0x004D8870`) runs from the
Training job for a creature between the two level caps, as `Job_StartTrain` calls it, with a
floor-slot draw (`0x004E8210`) and the drop test `0x004D8430` (fewer creatures on the floor
slots than slots). `AutoFurnitureRules.TryTotalCapacity` gives the Temple and the Combat Pit
their rim (`0x004E3ED0`). Messages 45 and 99 take their subtables' lifetimes.

**Consequences.** Levels 1 and 2 replays are unchanged (20/20, 4/20); Level 3 over seeds 1-10
wins 7 against master's 8, the one change being seed 1, whose stream a Library draw at 2269
moves. Deviates: our Library choice has no shelf test, so DK2's first-loop draws happen only when
ours finds none. A full Temple now refuses a worshipper.

## ADR-0414 — The corpse selections ask for a Graveyard, once a level for 41
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `computer-keeper-messages.md` §1-2; `graveyard.md` §2; `functions/0046CF40.md`, `0046D3C0.md`

**Context.** DK2's corpse selections post 41 and 42 for a Graveyard, and 41 (with 99) passes the
player word `+0xF4E` only once: it is set when one is admitted and never cleared or initialised.
Ours posted neither, refused 41 Graveyard outright, and carried a corpse to any Graveyard tile
(Q544).

**Decision.** `PlayerState.GraveyardWantedPosted` is `+0xF4E`: saved and hashed, false at a new
level (DK2's heap usually holds zero; HYPOTHESIS), refusing 41/99 Graveyard while set and set by
a new record. `GraveyardRules.ForCorpse` is the selections (`0x0046D3C0` for our search,
`0x0046CF40` for the drop scan), asked at the first corpse on a tile the worker's keeper owns: no
Graveyard posts 41 at availability 3; none with a place posts 42 (the search always, the drop
scan at availability 3); either stops the carry; otherwise `0x004C6860` draws once and the corpse
goes to the nearest Graveyard with a place. A place is a floor slot (`0x004E3ED0`, type 14).

**Consequences.** Levels 1-3 replays as ADR-0413 left them. A Graveyard smaller than 3x3 takes
no corpse, as in DK2; the tests and the burial scenario now use 3x3. Deviates: DK2 lays a corpse
on its floor slot until it is destroyed there, holding the place (`0x004E6490`, `0x004B1070`);
ours buries on arrival, so a Graveyard never fills (Q578).

## ADR-0415 — A Casino's party moves with its room
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `casino.md` §9, §12; `functions/004E3800.md`, `004ED440.md`, `004D7100.md`

**Context.** DK2 keeps a Casino's party on the room (`+0x41`, music `+0x3D`, start `+0x45`). Ours
keeps it on the room's lowest tile and never moved it, so a tile joining below that tile lost the
party, and a sold tile left a stale flag behind on the floor.

**Decision.** `SlabChain` carries the party as it carries the Prison's door byte. A tile joining
a room moves the joined room's party to the new lowest tile; rooms absorbed in the same join
lose theirs (`Room_Absorb` writes no room field, and `Room_Free` drops the absorbed record). A
tile leaving clears the party from every piece and from the leaving tile: each piece is a new
room (`Room_Construct` zeroes `+0x31..+0x48`), and `Room_RemoveTile` restores only a Casino's
lever `+0x53`. The keeper's party count `+0xF4A` is not lowered: `Casino_OnFreed` only kicks
the occupants to 154.

**Consequences.** No replay level builds a Casino, so Levels 1-3 are unchanged. A Casino sold or
split during a party leaves its keeper's count raised, which lifts the purse test for the rest
of the level, as in DK2. Hash 210.

## ADR-0416 — A researcher's Library is the Library finder's
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `computer-keeper-messages.md` §2; `functions/004E2500.md`, `004759D0.md`

**Context.** `Job_TryResearch` (`0x004759D0`) takes its Library from `0x004E2500`, whose first
loop asks every reachable Library for a shelf (`0x004E1AC0`, one draw) before a place. Ours chose
the Library through the generic room search, with no shelf test, and drew only when posting the
finder's messages (ADR-0413), so the two random streams parted at the first Library search.

**Decision.** `RoomNeedRules.FindLibrary` is `0x004E2500`, all but its tie order. Each reachable Library (option
`0x80`) draws for a shelf; one with a shelf and a place is a candidate, ranked by the squared
distance from the creature to its first slab's centre (`0x0043C260`, strict less-than); the
nearest with no holder of the other alignment wins, else the nearest. With no candidate it posts
ADR-0413's messages. `CreatureJobSystem.TrySetOut` takes the one room it names for Research, and
the finder is not asked a second time for its messages.

**Consequences.** Level 1 wins 20/20 as before; Level 2 6/20 (master 4/20); Level 3 seeds 1-10
9/10 (master 7/10). Read as spread, not a measured gain: the streams moved. Deviates: ours walks
its rooms in index order, not DK2's newest-first list, so equal distances can pick a different
Library; the reroute at the end of a read (`ResearchStep`) still uses the generic search.

## ADR-0417 — A fallen creature with no bed is carried to a Lair and makes its bed there
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `lair-acquisition.md`; `functions/0046D810.md`, `0046E610.md`, `00468420.md`, `0046F4F0.md`

**Context.** The rescue selector (`0x0046D810`) raises a carry for an own creature with no bed
(`+0x3B7` zero) when a Lair has a place (result 4). Its creature update clears `+0x3B7` once the
bed is gone (`0x00488E75`), so a creature whose bed was sold counts too. Ours posted the messages
and left the body (ADR-0412).

**Decision.** The selector carries such a body on result 4. At the pick-up the casualty chooser
(`0x0046E610`, `ImpTaskSystem.RouteOwnCasualty`) takes its bed when a route reaches it, else a room
point (`0x004E8430`, a draw) in the Lair with space nearest the body (`0x004C6610`). State 45
(`0x00468420`) delivers on a Lair tile; off one, as when the bed's tile is sold during the walk,
it chooses again, and drops the body only when nothing is found (Q107). The delivery's 79
(`0x0046F4F0`) is `CreatureDeathRules.RescueIntoLair`: on its keeper's Lair, a free tile
(`0x004E0140`), `random(0x800)`, the old bed given up, the new one placed, and the creature laid
in it.

**Consequences.** Levels 1-3 replay exactly as ADR-0416 left them; no replayed body is bedless.
Deviates: ours places the bed at once, eliding 79's walk to the tile and 80-82, as `Rescue` does
for an existing bed, so it is never up at zero health; with no free tile ours leaves it dying
where DK2's 79 posts 42 and sets 1; ours carries only a creature with a lair object, which every
own creature with a dying state has (`NeedsBed`, where DK2's 79 reads only `+0x5D6`); the old bed's
destroy (`0x0049CC20`) kicks the creature to 1 a second time, which ours does not model; a stale
bed id is skipped for that pass in DK2, where ours, deriving the bed from the objects, carries the
body at once; state 42 (`0x00467D00`) offers every creature on the tile and takes the first the
chooser accepts, where ours takes the selected body; equal-distance Lairs fall to index order,
not the room list. State 45's success branch falls through into the chooser (`0x004684DF`) on the
body just put down; what that does is unread. Hash 212.

## ADR-0418 — A corpse lies in the Graveyard until its lifetime ends
**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Status:** accepted · Research: `graveyard.md` §2; `functions/004E6490.md`, `004B12D0.md`, `004B16E0.md`, `00467AA0.md`

**Context.** DK2 lays a delivered corpse on a free Graveyard floor slot (`Room_AddCorpse`), where it
holds the place until it is destroyed and buried (`0x004B1070`). Ours buried it on arrival, so a
Graveyard never filled (Q578).

**Decision.** `CreatureState.GraveyardSlot` is the dead body's room (`+0x132`), saved and hashed.
The pick-up (state 40, `0x004678A0`) takes the first of the keeper's Graveyards in room order with
a place and a free floor slot (`0x004E6A20`: a draw along the slab chain, then the first floor slot
with no dead body). State 41's arrival lays it there when the room has a place and no lying corpse
holds the slot (`0x004E6380`); otherwise it goes to the Graveyard with a place nearest the worker,
else the last in room order with one. A place is a floor slot not held by a lying corpse. The
corpse keeps its lifetime (`DeadBodyDiesAfterSeconds`), counted as on the floor (`0x004B12D0`), and
at its end `CreatureHealthSystem` buries it (`0x004B1070`) instead of letting it rot. The
selections skip a lying corpse, and a room freed by a sale or a merge lets its corpses go
(`Room_RemoveCorpse` from `Room_OnFreed`).

**Amendment (2026-10-09, hash 214; `graveyard.md` §2).** A slot takes a corpse only with a
tombstone (objects 31–34) on it (`0x004537E0` in `0x004E6380` and `Room_AddCorpse`), which the
furniture pass stands on every floor slot; `GraveyardRules.HasTombStone`. Each room change rebuilds
the furniture, the Graveyard's crypt pass first (`0x004DD5C0`, `0x004DD9B0`): a 5x5 gets one crypt
(object 75) at its centre, which is no floor slot, and the Vampire rises there (Q579). In play the
tile-change slot (`0x004DD750`) takes in the dead bodies on its tiles not yet its owner's, and
laying a body makes it the owner's, so one a sale releases is never taken back nor carried again
(new field `CreatureState.BodyOwnerPlayerId`). `PlaceCrypts` and `AdoptCorpses` run from
`AutoFurnitureSystem`. The owner confirms the 3x3's one corpse, the rot after about a minute and
the Vampire only after enough have rotted. Levels 1-3 replay unchanged.

**Consequences.** Levels 1-3 replay exactly as ADR-0416 left them. A 3x3 Graveyard holds one corpse at a time; the burial scenarios now use a 4x3
and a 7x3. Deviates: ours keeps no stone's `+0x14A`, which only a level-placed corpse sets; the
crypt's draw is made where ours rebuilds furniture, after the turn's other systems, once a turn
per changed Graveyard, where DK2 draws in each tile's change; ours adopts in creature order, DK2 tile
by tile; the first-placed crypt is our lowest object id; ours sets the corpse on the slot's centre, where
DK2 sets y to the tile's quarter; a pick-up whose walk fails tries the next Graveyard in DK2
(state 40) and abandons in ours; ours counts one place per lying corpse where states 40 and 41 read
`+0x71` and the capacity test `+0x6B` (LIKELY the same count); the order and spot draws walk our
room index, not DK2's newest-first list.

## ADR-0419 — Start placed captives in their rooms and keep walled interiors distinct
**Date:** 2026-10-10 · **Status:** accepted · Research: hand-drop-landing.md §1–§2;
room-floors-and-liquids.md §4; furniture-placement.md §3; imps-and-mana.md; combat-acquisition.md §4

**Context.** Level 8's placed captives and torture victims remained free, creatures crossed
cell bars, and Dante's ruined Heart generated imps at its ruin. Workshop wall machines had
different working and drawing positions. These discrepancies have binary evidence.

**Decision.** Project THINGS flag 0x40 into landing state 76 and resolve its room take-over
after furniture exists. Preserve starting captive health, own-versus-captive torture and
the independent non-worker/hero/neutral fallback. Torture companions are simulation devices.
Attackability excludes landing and involuntary torture. DoubleQuad floor slots carry nav
byte 4; the inner Prison delivery uses option 0xE4. Auto-placed wall furniture uses its
binary inset in both simulation and presentation. Ruined-at-load free casts use the
default corner origin and reject outside-map/solid positions, advancing the deadline.
Hash/save version 215; no new saved field.

**Consequences.** Twenty recorded seeds per level: Level 1 retains 20/20 wins and Level 2
retains 4/20, with unchanged win ticks. Level 3 changes from 15/20 to 17/20 as Workshop
positions change its random stream; this sample does not establish an improvement.
Level 11A's seed fixture uses seed 2: the correct
startup of Belial's two flagged Goblins changes seed 7's outcome; reverting only that
startup restores its old outcome. All keepers and behavioral assertions are retained.
Startup landing finishes on the first tick; remaining deviations stay in the cited research.

**Date:** 2026-10-10 · **Status:** accepted · Research: hero-parties-and-effect-generators.md

## ADR-0423 — Preserve the ordinary obstacle query's retained flags
**Date:** 2026-10-10 · **Status:** accepted · Research: structure-blocks.md §5–§6

**Context.** Dwarves still crossed the wheel. The callback's solid bit was treated
as a definition value, but the binary retains it and toggles it for soft definitions.

**Decision.** Enumerate all eligible ordinary obstacles in row-major tile order

versus 20/4/17 under 216. All event streams change with the corrected movement.

## ADR-0427 — Sort translucent terrain triangles across materials
**Date:** 2026-10-10 · **Status:** accepted · Research: kmf-materials.md §7

**Context.** Grouping portal triangles by material lets the translucent chasm
cover crystal faces, making intact pillars look fragmented.

**Decision.** Separate blended terrain from opaque chunks. Sort its triangles
globally by summed camera-facing vertex depth, preserving ties, and batch only
consecutive equal materials. Pooled renderers submit those runs in explicit order
for each camera. Keep original positions, textures, alpha and depth-write states.

**Consequences.** Camera rotation and geometry changes refresh ordering. The
modern sort uses continuous depth rather than DK2's quantised buckets. Standalone
object/liquid transparency remains outside this stream; run batching increases
draw calls and has Unity's documented 32767 ordered-run bound. No simulation change.

## ADR-0440 — A room on TotalCapacity's default arm holds its tile count
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted · Research: auto-placed-furniture.md §5

**Context.** On Level 4 the keeper cannot build a Guard Room and captures three
neutral ones; DK2's portal then sent eleven Dark Elves, attracted by the Guard
Room. Ours sent none: `TryTotalCapacity` read no capacity outside the furniture,
Temple and Combat Pit arms, so `AttractionBudget` gave a Guard Room 0.

**Decision.** `0x004E3ED0`'s jump table sends the Hatchery, Heart, bridges, Guard
Room and every type outside 3–16 to an arm that stores the slab count `+0xA7`;
`TryTotalCapacity` returns the tile count for them. The Portal (0), Prison
(`0xFFFF`, its count in `+0x4B`) and Graveyard (floor slots) stay unread there.
Hash/save version 231 (226–230 are held by the unmerged classic-look branch).

**Consequences.** A Guard Room attracts as many Dark Elves as it has tiles, and its
Guard Post claim is capped at that count. The Guard Room's extra (creatures walking
to it, `0x004E53B0`) is still unbuilt, so ours admits slightly more than DK2.
Levels 1–3 replays are unchanged (19/6/18 over seeds 1–20). Level 4's replays now
receive 6–16 Dark Elves (DK2: 11) but none wins: our dig into the hero base lags
DK2's by 200–1,400 turns by seed, and Receive Imps (special 124, at 5783) is unbuilt
(experiments/2026-10-12-level4-packet-replay/).

**Status:** accepted, 2026-10-12. Owner requested construction effects,
Prison rats and creature portal arrival playback, followed by verification
and a merge to master.

## ADR-0443 — A tile holding a closed door is never claimed
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted · Research: imp-claim-path.md §4, functions/0046AB50.md

**Context.** Level 4's hero door at (24,27) stands on hero-claimed floor next to the
keeper's. Ours offered it as an AttackTile job; the router cannot enter a closed rival
door, so the imp dropped the job as out of reach and took it again. Seed 1 logged about
5,000 such takes by seven imps between turns 2117 and 5300; DK2 never touches the tile
until the owner's army starts breaking the door at 5344.

**Decision.** The claim priority refuses a tile with a closed, completed door, as
`0x0046AB50`'s third gate does: it continues only when `+0x21C(x, y, 0)`, the door nibble
of the tile's navigation byte, is 0. Only a closed, completed door writes that nibble
(`0x004A66F0`), so an open door or one under construction does not refuse. One gate
covers claim, attack and room conversion, as the handler does. Hash/save version 234.

**Consequences.** On ADR-0441's tool Level 4 goes from 0/20 to 2/20 (seeds 19 and 13,
at 6748 and 6760; DK2 6743), Levels 1–3 unchanged (19/6/18). Merged onto master 15c2b038
it wins 3/20 (seeds 9, 11, 19, 6724–6748) where master alone wins 2/20 (11, 12); Levels
1–3 are identical with and without the gate (19/2/13, master's own change). Before the merge (set F) the winning seeds reached rows 25,
15 and 5 within 90 turns of DK2; the gate does not help every seed (seed 1 reaches row 25 at 5169, 4599
before). Flag 14, the three Guards behind the door waking, moves to DK2's 5283 in seed 1
(3430 before) but still fires early in seeds 10–12; it does not explain the wins. The other 18 still lose imps to hero fights DK2 does not have.
Still unbuilt: the handler refuses when the walk does not start (`Imp_WalkOrTeleport`
returns 0), and ours commits a job without a route (Q588).

## ADR-0444 — The simulation is profiled through markers it opens itself
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Unity stutters once every few frames. At 4 ticks a second, a frame that
runs a tick carries all of it (one in fifteen at 60 fps), so a frame drop is the worst
tick, not the mean one. The harness timed each system as a run total only, and Unity
saw the whole tick as one block, so neither showed which tick was slow or where.

**Decision.** `ISimulationProfiler` (`Begin`/`End` of a `SimulationMarker`, one
instance per name) sits on `SimulationContext.Profiler`, set by
`GameSimulation.ProfileWith`, defaulting to an empty profiler. The simulation opens the
markers: the tick, messages, triggers, each system by its `Name`, `nav.refresh`/
`nav.build`/`nav.route`, the grid pathfinder's searches and ImpTask's phases. It is
observation under the event sink's contract;
`DeterminismTests.Profiling_DoesNotAffectState` pins it. The harness's `RunClock` is a
profiler that keeps self and total time, calls and allocated bytes per marker per tick,
and reports p50/p99/max and the worst tick. Unity maps each marker to a `ProfilerMarker`.

**Consequences.** A new hot spot is found by adding a marker, not a stopwatch. The first
Release run (Level 18, nemesis attack) puts its worst tick at ~650 ms, ~430 ms of it in
405 `grid.nearest` searches allocating 118 MB, likely because ImpTask's selection runs
one search per candidate tile. The keeper scenarios run allocate 3–10 MB a tick. Only
ImpTask's pathfinder is wrapped; the other systems' grid searches count as their own
time. A span costs two interface calls when nobody is listening.

## ADR-0445 — The possessed creature recruits followers
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted · Research: possession-arms-and-inputs.md §4

**Context.** Action 26's slot 3 (key 7 in play, the owner confirmed) recruits friendly
creatures that then follow the possessed creature and take its melee target. Ours
stamped nothing and started nothing (Q535).

**Decision.** Slot 3 runs `0x00515D50`'s pick (best aim score, not nearest, within 7
tiles of the creature) and `0x00461980`'s start into state 246; the count `+0x488` rises
only on success, up to variable 223. State 246 ends the follow when the leader is no
longer possessed and otherwise walks to it, running beyond 0x5000. A possessed melee
start records `+0x4D0`/`+0x4D2`, forgotten after three seconds while possessed;
`SelectAVictim` gives it to a follower after scan A, in place of its fight-style arm. Possession set
and clear zero the count; dismissal (action 38), fear in a fight and every removal of a
follower (the death bookkeeping runs for each freed creature) lower it; state 1
re-follows first. A follower is busy to its needs and takes no lair or pay anger.
Hash/save version 235.

**Consequences.** Only a creature target is carried to followers: a trap or door struck
by the possessed creature is recorded but not handed on. The flee state's skip of its
return to 199 while following (`0x00460586`, a window read) is not built, nor is the
death bookkeeping's unread early exit (`0x00487C70`'s first call). DK2 frees a creature
with its leader field set; ours clears it so a corpse removed later does not count twice.
Scan A's own pick keeps its discounted distance as the best where
`0x0045D69D` may take the plain one; no packet decoder builds the dismissal. No computer keeper casts Possession
(computer-keeper-spell-sites.md §1), so replays cannot change.

## ADR-0446 — Sneak, hypnosis and sniper mode are possession commands
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted · Research: possession-arms-and-inputs.md §5

**Context.** Three commands set the possessed creature's inputs (Q536): sneak (0x1D),
hypnosis (0x1B) and sniper mode (39). None was represented.

**Decision.** `ToggleSneakCommand` disguises the creature as a tile's owner unless a
creature allied to that owner sees it; every combat scan (the fight-style scan, scan C,
the NonFighter and nearest-attacker scans) skips a candidate disguised as the searcher's
side; a blow or cast at a thing allied to the disguise, another keeper's hand, and
leaving possession end it. `HypnotiseCommand` takes the nearest hypnotisable enemy in
the cone and sight from the pose, keeps its owner, makes it the possessor's and starts it
following; each possessed blow at a creature forces it at that creature and counts one
order, and it drops the order once it has launched as many attacks; a second press,
leaving possession (action 21) or its death end the hold. `SetSniperModeCommand` sets
the flag: a free-aim shot then doubles its contact damage, and a Range-0 spell is capped
at 0x3000. Hash/save version 235, shared with ADR-0445 on this branch.

**Consequences.** Creeping (`+0x3E6` bit 12) and `0x00455990` in the sneak test are not
represented; an off-map sneak tile changes nothing where DK2 reads past the map; a
targetless cast does not unmask, where DK2 reads thing slot 0's owner (unknown). Leaving
possession ours always goes through action 21's release. The owner's play questions
(sniper range, the disguise pick-up, the release on leaving) stay open.

## ADR-0444 — Preserve bank heights and idle movement after failed hero jobs
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Grounded creatures crossed liquid banks at a flat height, and
Unity interpolated their horizontal position against the destination height.
Failed hero hunts waited without the original idle wrapper. Same-tile wander
and training destinations were discarded as already reached.

**Decision.** Project the native liquid-bank height and interpolate previous
and current height alongside position. Share the existing idle wrapper with
hero state 4, and retain a destination waypoint for same-tile wander and dummy
approaches. Preserve authored creature positions. Combined hash/save version 236.
Evidence: room-floors-and-liquids.md, hero-party-walk.md and training-actions.md.

**Consequences.** These fixes apply across maps. Full vertical physics remains
outside the height projection. A hero-owned Prison correctly produces no rats;
see prison-rats.md. Original-game visual comparison remains an owner check.

## ADR-0447 — Keep combat contact, facing and melee action lifetime
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Ending a combat route disabled body contact updates. Stationary
fighters struck without facing their target, and post-impact actions became
available before the authored melee animation completed.

**Decision.** Integrate route-less bodies in native fight states 199/200,
turn toward in-reach targets before attacking, and retain melee's busy hold
until its animation-completion poll. Keep fear checks ahead of that hold.
Use existing steering, turn and authored timing rules; hash/save version 237.
Evidence: combat-spacing.md, combat-fight-state.md and kmf-animation-playback.md §7.

**Consequences.** These changes apply across maps. Native separation remains
soft and does not guarantee rigid clearance. Other route-less state dispatch,
remembered-entity activation and original visual comparison remain open.
Q582 still requires the owner's original-game casualty confirmation.

## ADR-0449 — Restore claim positioning and ownership effects
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Same-tile paths let imps start claiming off centre. Tile and room
ownership changes and successful bed creation lacked their original effects.

**Decision.** Keep a centre destination even when an imp already occupies its
claim tile. Publish typed cosmetic requests at completed floor claiming,
whole-room ownership transfer and successful bed creation. Read the terrain
and room effect references from shipped data and reuse the existing effect
renderer, independent cosmetic randomness and original sprite provider.
Evidence: room-construction-effects.md §6; function records 0046AB50 and 004D0F60.
Hash/save version 238 accounts for changed claim approaches; cosmetic requests
are neither saved nor hashed.

**Consequences.** The changes apply across maps. Native arrival tolerance is
preserved. The special cycling-colour branch and bed heading fidelity remain
research boundaries; ordinary keeper colours use the confirmed palette.

**Amendment, 2026-10-13.** Decode terrain destruction effects and submit them
only when the source becomes another terrain. Type-5 effect keys reuse the
shared mesh/material cache; particle angles follow native view spin and stop
on floor bounce. This restores Rock/Gold debris across maps without changing
hash/save version240. Evidence: research/terrain-digging-debris.md.

**Presentation adjustment, 2026-10-13.** At the owner's request, Unity uses
two-thirds-size terrain mesh fragments that start across the tile's upper
area and fall with limited sideways drift. This deliberately differs from
the shipped upward velocities; the native presentation profile remains
available and is the default outside Unity. Unity also confines room capture
to the exterior boundary, with 80% scale and colour intensity; floor capture
retains native placement. Boundaries are frozen on the first emission wave. This is
the owner's requested presentation profile, not a claim of original geometry.

## ADR-0450 — Select a bed after a creature is dropped into a Lair
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Lair drops fell back to idle after getting up, retaining a bed
in another Lair. Native state 79 handles this room-directed relocation.

**Decision.** Dispatch state 79 after the landing/get-up sequence, remembering
the Sleep job. Use the existing local free-tile search. A bed in this room is
reused; a full destination keeps the old bed. Successful selection releases
the old bed before a seeded, jittered walk to state 80, which creates the new
bed with the existing effect request. Hash/save version 239; no new field.
Evidence: lair-acquisition.md §9 and the function record for 0046F4F0.

**Consequences.** Relocation frees the former tile for another creature and
applies across maps. The casualty-delivery approximation in ADR-0417 remains
separate; this change restores ordinary hand drops.

## ADR-0451 — Remove wall reinforcement when its owned floor is lost
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Capturing enemy floor left its unsupported reinforced walls
standing. Native ownership completion has a separate support callback.

**Decision.** Run that callback after hostile floor destruction and each
transferred room slab. Preserve the native in-place neighbour order and
corner exceptions. Reuse terrain conversion and slab bookkeeping.
Evidence: research/wall-support-after-claim.md. Hash/save version 240.

**Consequences.** Walls supported by another floor of their owner remain;
unsupported reinforcement becomes neutral Rock. The rule applies across maps.

## ADR-0452 — Keep the entire live Heart platform closed to walkers
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** superseded by ADR-0505, 2026-10-17

**Context.** The Level1 Goblin report exposes ADR-0439's small excluded disk:
creatures could still cross the surrounding raised platform.

**Decision.** The former square routing and movement exclusion is reverted by
ADR-0505. Its measured effect belongs to research/imp-boundary-route.md.

## ADR-0453 — A worker's reachability comes from one flood, not one search per candidate
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Job selection asked the grid pathfinder "can this worker reach
this tile" once per candidate stance, body tile and crate, each a Dijkstra
that floods the worker's whole region before it can answer no. A keeper
dropping five imps ran 404 such searches in one tick (Level 18, 0.3 s of a
0.46 s tick, 120 MB allocated), and the drop scan's one-tile searches still
flooded the map to meet their one tile.

**Decision.** `ReachableTiles` runs the same Dijkstra once from the worker
to exhaustion and answers every candidate from it: the same neighbour order,
step costs and heap order as `GridPathfinder.TryFindNearest`, so the same
reachable set and the same route to each tile. `ImpTaskSystem` floods once
per worker update, keyed on the grid instance and the start tile, and the
point questions (stances, claims, objects, crates, the drop scan's one tile)
read the flood. The body search asks only the tiles bodies lie on, in the
search's own order of route cost then tile index, which is where the
predicate could have been true. Searches with a real predicate over unknown
tiles (`CreatureAngerSystem`'s exit) keep the pathfinder. The equivalence is
pinned by tests on grids with corner-only gaps, and the Level 18 attack
scenario's hash and event log are unchanged.

**Consequences.** The flood is for one grid and one start. The grid reads
terrain live, so a terrain change between a worker's questions would be seen
by a search and not by the flood; none occurs, because dig, claim and
reinforce are queued for `TileWorkSystem` to apply after every worker has
chosen. The drop scan's blueprint search keeps the pathfinder when no tile
confines it. The `grid.flood` marker counts floods. Selection's own cost
(ring scans over the map, candidate sorting) is untouched and is the next item.

## ADR-0454 — Derived navigation state is kept while its inputs are unchanged
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** A tick allocated about 8 MB on Level 18 and spent a sixth of
its time in `nav.refresh`, called about seventeen times a tick, each call
rebuilding the structure mask and the navigation bytes from scratch. Every
room sweep allocated a visited array the size of the map, and every
`WorldPathGrid` (one per worker per tick) rebuilt the structure mask.

**Decision.** Three results are kept and revalidated against their inputs,
never trusted blindly. `WorldSteering.Refresh` returns at once while the
tile array, the doors' navigation fields, the set of ruined hearts and the
crypts' tiles (a Graveyard's floor slots) are what the last refresh saw;
the check is one byte comparison of the tile array. `StructureBlocks.For` keeps the world's last mask with the list of
structure tiles (index, terrain, owner, heart ruined) it was built from,
and recomputes when a scan finds that list changed. `RoomIndex` takes its
visited array from per-thread scratch. No tile-write counter exists, since
tiles are written through references, so each cache compares its inputs
rather than listening for changes. The Level 18 attack scenario's hashes
and event log are unchanged; allocation fell to about 2 MB a tick.

**Consequences.** Each cache's key must name every input its result reads;
the tests found `HeartRuined` missing from the mask's key, and the reviewer
found the crypts missing from the refresh's, so any new input to those
routines must join its key. The mesh rebuild itself (`nav.build`) and the remaining
per-tick lists (room-need queries, the keeper view, furniture) are untouched.

## ADR-0455 — The adapter's run-time shaders are referenced from Resources
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** The Unity adapter builds its materials at run time from
shaders found by name: URP Lit and Unlit, with the Standard and Unlit/Color
fallbacks. A player contains only the shaders and variants some asset in
the build references, so the headless probe's Development player found
none of them and logged the failure every frame; the probe worked around
it in its own build.

**Decision.** `Assets/DK2/Resources/Shaders` holds one material per shader
and keyword set the adapter uses: URP Lit opaque and blended, each with and
without emission, all with specular and reflections off; URP Unlit opaque
and additive; Standard; Unlit/Color. Resources are always built, and a
material's keyword set is what makes Unity keep that variant. The probe
keeps its own materials for builds from an older copy. Not yet verified by
a player build, which the owner's next build will show; the Unlit/Color
built-in id (10755) is from memory and unverified on disk.

**Consequences.** A new keyword on a run-time material needs a material
here that carries it, or the player draws it pink; unity/README.md says so.
`DK2/ClassicEffect` is a shader under Resources already, so every variant of
it is built.
## ADR-0456 — The presenter runs its tile pass only when the tiles' inputs changed
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** `ScenePresenter.Present` runs every frame and its tile pass
built a `TileView` for every tile to compare with the last one pushed,
about 1-2 ms a frame on Level 1, on frames where the simulation had not
ticked and nothing could have changed.

**Decision.** The tile pass runs only when its inputs differ from what it
last read: the tile array, compared byte for byte against a copy; which
hearts are ruined (a ruined platform is drawn as floor); the fog flag; the
doors' version (a door shows on its tile); the crypts' tiles (a Graveyard's
floor slots); the view's tag-preview version; and the tick, since the view's
room facts are cached per tick. The viewing player and the database are
fixed for the view's life. A tile written, a door placed or a preview moved
between two presents is still seen (tests pin those three). The other passes
(torches, objects, structures, creatures) are unchanged.

**Consequences.** Any new input the tile view reads must join the check,
as with ADR-0454's caches; the reviewer found the doors and the preview
missing from the first version. The saving is on frames without a tick,
which at 4 Hz is most of them. `WorldState.Tiles` exposes the tiles as a
read-only span for whole-map comparison.

## ADR-0457 — Terrain chunk rebuilds are spread over frames
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** `TerrainChunks.Flush` rebuilt every chunk a tile had changed
in, in one frame. A tag wave or a room drop touches many 16x16 chunks at
once, and an earlier probe run (not kept) saw frames of about 120 ms on
Level 1 from it, even with the per-tile geometry cache (commit c902b2a3).

**Decision.** A flush rebuilds dirty chunks in ascending chunk order until
`FlushBudgetMilliseconds` (4 ms by default) has passed, leaving the rest
dirty for the next frame; at least one chunk is rebuilt per flush, and a
flush that finds no chunk drawn yet (the first after a load or a `Clear`)
rebuilds everything, so a level appears whole. A chunk waiting its turn
shows its previous mesh for those frames. Zero or less turns the budget
off. The budget's clock is a stopwatch, so it follows the machine.

**Consequences.** A large change reaches the screen over a few frames at a
few milliseconds each instead of one long frame. A seam between a rebuilt
chunk and a waiting neighbour can show while the backlog drains. The probe's
full-rebuild check sets the budget to zero first. Checked by compiling the
adapter against Unity's assemblies, not by a Unity run; whether the seam
is acceptable in play is the owner's to judge.

## ADR-0458 — Ticks run on a worker thread after the frame is presented
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** `DungeonRunner.Update` ran up to twenty simulation ticks and
then presented, all on the main thread, so a frame that carried a tick
cost the tick's whole time (15 ms at the median, far more at the tail)
on top of its own, and the diagnostics recomputed the state hash on every
`OnGUI` call.

**Decision.** `Update` first joins the tick started last frame, then reads
input, presents the settled world and starts this frame's ticks on a
worker thread, where they run while Unity renders. A frame runs at most
`maxTicksPerFrame` ticks (2), so a stall is paid back over frames. The
view shows a tick one frame after it ran, so the creature interpolation
draws the frame that owes a tick complete and starts the new motion on the
next. Nothing on the main thread reads the world while a tick runs: `OnGUI`
shows strings built in `Update`, the `Simulation` property joins the tick
first, and the state hash is taken on the worker. A tick that throws stops
the game and shows the failure. `tickOnWorkerThread` turns it off, and the
probe does, to measure ticks. The simulation is Unity-free and
single-threaded per world, which is what makes a worker safe; the one
Unity call reached from a tick, the construction effects' clock, is now a
stopwatch, and the per-thread scratch of ADR-0454 is per thread.

**Consequences.** Hides cost rather than removing it: a tick longer than a
frame still stalls the next frame by the excess. Compiled against Unity's
assemblies, not run in Unity; the first play session is the real test, and
the toggle is the way back if anything misbehaves.

## ADR-0461 — The navigation mesh is edited per tile, as the original's is
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0157, ADR-0454 · Research: `docs/research/navigation-partial-rebuild.md`, Q591

**Context.** `WorldSteering.Refresh` built a new mesh from every tile whenever a
navigation byte changed: 14 ms on Level 18 for one dug tile. DK2 edits its mesh in
place around the changed tile (`0x004CE770`'s partial path): it cuts the
rectangle's sides into the mesh and marks them, empties the inside of vertices,
refills it from the bytes, coarsens by a bounded flood of flips seeded from the
corners, then unmarks the sides and removes each side point with one byte all
round, reusing freed slots last first. Its triangles after an edit depend on the
history of edits; the research had the difference in triangles STRONGLY INFERRED
and in routes a HYPOTHESIS. The owner chose the faithful edit over a faster build.

**Decision.** `NavMesh.Retriangulate` is the partial path transcribed loop for
loop: the side cuts (`0x004CDFE0`, `0x004CDF20`), the one-sided marks
(`0x004CE380`), the interior walk (`0x004CE0C0`), the fill, the flood
(`0x004CC650` seeded by `0x004CC3D0`, 996-entry cutoff, flip results ignored),
the queue and merge-back (`0x004CE410`), and the vertex removals with their degree
reduction (`0x004CB8C0`, `0x004CB170`, `0x004CC190`). The flip (`0x004C9FC0`)
moves its constraint bits before its convexity test, as the original's does. The
whole-map build uses the same flood in place of the old slot sweep and carries no
constraint bits, as the original's reset leaves none. Our triangles wind the other
way from the original's, so every walk goes through one translation (the table
is in the research doc and NavMesh.Edit.cs), so that each routine walks the same
triangles in the same order and keeps and frees the same slots. A rectangle
within one tile of a map edge rebuilds the whole map. `Refresh` builds once, then
edits each routing byte that changed since the last refresh, in tile order. The
mesh is state: `WorldSnapshot` carries it with the bytes it was last brought to, a
load takes no tile snapshot so its next refresh edits what the saved run would
have, and `StateHash` folds in every slot and both free lists. The keeper AI's
own steering (`KeeperView`) still routes on a fresh build. Hash/save version 243.

**Consequences.** Level 18: an interior single-tile edit takes 0.035 ms median
and 0.46 ms at worst, against 14 ms for a build. 1,955 single-tile edits over the
66 shipped levels each leave a valid mesh; the whole-map pins were regenerated
once (1–3 % of triangles differ from the sweep's). Routes after an edit may
differ from a fresh build's. Two reviewers confirmed the transcriptions against
the binary and found the residuals, each stated in the code: ours batches the
bytes changed since the last refresh where the original edits at each write; the
original's locate (`0x004C98B0`) walks from a 4×4 cell cache and returns the
first triangle it reaches, so at a vertex its fan triangle depends on history,
where ours takes the lowest slot (ADR-0157); that triangle starts the degree
reduction, labels the degree-4 rim and heads the flood seed's stack, so the two
edits can pick different diagonals and flips; the whole-map builder's reset
diagonal, corner order and splits predate this and are ours (Q591). Region ids
and width classes are not modelled, the shipped game reading neither. The only
check of the triangles is a DK2 mesh dump after a dig: the Level 10 capture that
held 353 is lost, so a new capture is the next step when the original can run.
## ADR-0460 — Restore drop recovery and sleeping poses
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Hand-dropped creatures used a walking clip while stunned, and
ordinary sleepers could stop beside their bed instead of aligning to it.

**Decision.** Draw the authored knockdown and get-up clips from each state
entry. Restore native sleep-entry position and heading alignment. During
the Mistress bed's entrance clip, draw the bed and hide its occupant before
switching to her sleeping clip. Treat the authored portal exit as a visual
relocation so interpolation does not replay its movement. Evidence:
research/hand-drop-landing.md, research/portal-creature-action.md,
research/lair-acquisition.md §9 and research/object-drawing.md §8.
Hash/save version 242 distinguishes the corrected resumed behaviour. Preserve
an existing departure route only when its travel resumes in state 195;
an unrelated wander route must not bypass portal selection. Evidence:
research/creature-leaving.md §1.

**Consequences.** The changes apply across maps. State 82's existing tile-level
arrival approximation and the Mistress's unbuilt wake-door sequence remain
fidelity boundaries; this change restores sleep entry, not that exit sequence.

## ADR-0459 — A tunneller's walks keep their destination within its own tile
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0222, ADR-0430 · Research: `docs/research/tunnelling.md` §5, hero-party-walk.md §1

**Context.** On Level 1 the script softens three boundary tiles to Rock and
gives the leader Dwarf `KillPlayer`; its route fails and it starts a tunnel
(state 186). The dig tile was the tile below it, so the stand point
(`0x00486680`) was the centre of its own tile. `TunnelRules.Walk` asked
`WorldSteering.TryRouteTo`, whose same-tile shortcut ends the walk at once, and
the Dwarf, more than `0x555` from that centre, re-planned the same walk every
two ticks without moving, for as long as the level ran. The 20-seed Level 1
replays had never shown it: their Dwarf stood one tile diagonal from its dig
tile and walked a real route; commit 465 shifted the level's timing and put it
on the tile above (bisected: 464 digs at tick 1240, 465 never digs). The owner
saw both Dwarves standing in Unity. tunnelling.md had recorded the loop as a
difference in ours and left "whether DK2 can loop the same way" UNKNOWN;
ADR-0430's recheck of `0x004CF490` answers it: DK2's route request retains its
destination even within one triangle, so DK2 walks to the stand point.

**Decision.** `TunnelRules.Walk` routes through `TryRouteToStance`, the
point-walk ADR-0289 built for stance points and ADR-0430 reused for waiting
heroes: off the destination's tile it is `TryRouteTo` unchanged; on it, the
creature steps to the point. Every walk the tunnel states make goes through
`0x00471890`, so the one helper covers 186's stand and target walks and 223's
trailing walk; `RouteOrTunnel`, the first stage of the same helper, asks the
same way. The reviewer re-read the chain (`0x004D0F60`, `0x004D5100`,
`0x004D0320`, `0x004CF490`, `0x004D0240`) and found no same-tile shortcut in it;
186's four calls into the helper are listed in `00471890.md`. Hash/save
version 241; no new persisted field.

**Consequences.** Level 1 seed 1 on master: the leader Dwarf digs the softened
tile at tick 1297 and is fighting the keeper's imps inside the dungeon by 1308, where
before the fix it never dug and the keeper's own imp opened the wall at 1471.
The replay still wins (tick 1796 before, 1812 after). `AWorkerOffItsStandTilesCentre_WalksToTheCentreAndDigs` pins the case and
fails against the reverted walk (run as the negative control); the
earlier tunnel tests spawned the worker on its tile centre and could not see
it. Q565's remaining generic callers are unchanged; the tunnel's walks are now
on the retained-destination side of that question.

## ADR-0462 — Keep stationary travellers on their original standing pose
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Selecting walk art when a route exists, before velocity becomes
nonzero, lets its initial rate and zero-speed reuse play cycles in place.

**Decision.** Ordinary stationary travellers select native slot 39, loaded
from the separate standing resource; absent art falls back to walk slot 1.
Movement installation uses the body's current speed cap in 12.12 instead of
the action scalar 4096. Preserve subsequent advance-before-rate-update order.

The unrepresented movement-mode-2 exception remains scoped; possessed
movement retains its existing override. No simulation/save/hash change.

**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** The healthy Heart loop omitted its health response and mana particles.

**Decision.** Compute native five-percent pulse and height stages and select

use shipped resources and view RNG. No simulation/save/hash change. The
companion effect's dynamic light remains outside this particle renderer.

No simulation/save/hash change. Unity visual comparison remains pending.

## ADR-0465 — Restore the original wall reinforcement completion effect
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Upward completion requested effects for floor claims but omitted walls.

**Decision.** Share the source-terrain effect selection across upward completion.
Preserve the native terrain-9 placement branch and completion-only trigger.

## ADR-0466 — The room sweep is kept while every tile's terrain and owner are unchanged
**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** accepted · amended 2026-10-14: a run's total allocation is not a measure under tiered compilation

**Context.** `RoomIndex.Build` swept the whole map, filling every room and its
interior rings, at each of its 66 call sites in code, and a tick makes many of them: a lair
attempt alone rebuilt it once per creature (43 times in Level 18's first tick,
19 ms and 3.5 MB of that tick's `CreatureSleep`, against 6 ms for the routes
themselves). Its doc comment ruled a cache out because one forgotten
