invalidation would give a room that disagrees with the map.

**Decision.** Keep the sweep per world and revalidate it on every call, never
invalidate it: a room is a function of each tile's terrain and owner and of the
database's terrain-to-room map, so `Build` compares those two bytes of every
tile, and the database instance, with what its last sweep read, and sweeps again
only when something differs. Nothing has to remember to invalidate it, which is
ADR-0454's pattern. `Build` now returns `IReadOnlyList<RoomInstance>`, because the
list and its rooms are shared until the next change; the change of type found
the one caller that edited the list in place (the wander room branch, which now
filters into its own list). A changed map gets a new list, so a list already
handed out never changes. The single-room fill and the filtered sweep are left
uncached. The cache is not thread-safe; it relies on ADR-0458's rule that the
presenter reads the world only while no tick runs.

**Consequences.** All 42 corpus scenarios give the same final hashes, per-tick
hashes, event logs and world pictures as master. On Level 18's attack run,
tick 0's allocation fell from 9.3 MB to 3.2 MB, the same in every run, and its
`CreatureSleep` from about 80 ms to 32 ms; times are from a shared machine and
indicative only. The run's total allocation is not evidence either way: it varies
with tiered compilation, apparently with when methods are recompiled (probably
escape analysis stack-allocating short-lived objects, which tick 0's early code
does not yet do). Master at ebf751db, which includes this change, gave 442 MB and
760 MB in consecutive runs, and the "about 960 MB to 535 MB" first written here
compared two such runs. With `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0` the same master gave
236.5 MB in two runs; compare allocations that way. Any new input to a room's fill must
join the cache's key, and the database is keyed by reference on the assumption
that a loaded `GameDatabase` and its `RoomDef`s are never changed.
`RoomInstanceTests` pins a hit, a rebuild on a terrain or an owner change, and
that an old list survives a rebuild.

## ADR-0467 — Restore the original portal pre-arrival buildup
**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Entrance animations played without the portal's preceding buildup.

**Decision.** Read the authored room buildup field and request its original
effect at the native preview threshold. Share admission checks with the due
roll while keeping preview free of gameplay mutations and random draws.
Evidence: research/portals-interval.md, Portal buildup.

**Consequences.** The existing effect consumer renders authored resources.
Arrival timing and simulation/save/hash state are unchanged. Original graphics
quality gating is replaced by the adapter's effect path. Unity visual
confirmation remains pending while the owner is away.

## ADR-0468 — A possessed creature's blow reaches objects, pillars, shots and bodies
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted · Research: possession-arms-and-inputs.md §1–2

**Context.** Action 26's melee arm stamped and did nothing on a chicken, the Training
Dummy, a Book Case, an Arch Pillar, a shot or a body (Q535).

**Decision.** A chicken is killed by a creature owing no food that is not a Bile Demon;
otherwise eaten: hunger anger grows by its bucket over the fill, the level-scaled
`HungerFill` is paid off (not a Bile Demon's), and the creature heals the lesser of its
deficit and `HpFromChicken`, with no state change and no hunger-clock restart. The
dummy enters object process 18, restarting a running spin. A Book Case, an enemy Arch
Pillar, a shot or a body takes the swing (action 17, recorded for the followers): the
pillar's blow goes to its heart, a shot's `Health` and a body's rot window shrink flat,
and the Book Case refuses it (not Damageable). The spell scan aims at enemy pillars,
the cast hitting the heart. Pillars are `HeartPillarRules`' three, last in their
tile's chain (LIKELY). A blow at a heart, possessed or from `spFighting`, no longer
takes the bearing bonus, which 0x00498E30 gives a creature target only. No new saved
field.

**Consequences.** The Horned Reaper's state 0xEF over a target its blow killed, the
sounds, the impact effects and action 26 on art 13 are not represented. What removes a
shot struck to 0 is unread: ours, the shot system's next pass.

## ADR-0469 — A possessed worker digs, mines and claims
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted · Research: possession-arms-and-inputs.md §3

**Context.** A possessed worker's melee press with no target did nothing (Q535).

**Decision.** For a worker (definition `+0x686` bit 0) the press tries the pose's tile
when it touches the worker's own floor and is not its own: an ally's tile ends it,
the neutral player's claimable path (`0x00453FC0`) starts a claim (action 4), another
keeper's claimed floor one attack (action 6, no experience; when the floor falls, traps
and doors on the worker's own tile are zeroed). Else the tile the packet yaw faces: the
neutral player's gold (`0x00453D80`; no seam is ownable) is mined (2), any other solid,
penetrable tile dug (1) under that action's own guard and owner-chosen rate. Actions 1 (an Imp's), 2 and 4 multiply the strike by the possessed
melee recharge; the claim strikes every tick until the tile turns. Action 1 by a
worker that is not an Imp, the hero tunneller's included, digs at six times
`DigOwnWallHealth` with no multiplier: slower than an Imp on rock, far faster through a
keeper's reinforced wall (the owner's observation agrees: hero Dwarves dig walls fast). A work order carries
the multiplier and the strike's flags; a creature its claim tile; hash/save version 244.

**Consequences.** The global `0x0075AE93` that stops a non-Imp's dig is taken as 0
(campaign); `0x004ECDB0` and `0x00455030` are not represented. On shipped data one
possessed strike converts a Dirt Path, so a claim runs once; ours also ends it when the
creature leaves possession, is down or is held (what DK2's action does then is unread).

## ADR-0470 — A gem face pays every strike and is never damaged
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted · Research: possession-arms-and-inputs.md §3

**Context.** Ours damaged a gem face and paid `GoldMinedFromGems` only when it
collapsed (Q587). Action 2 (`0x004971D0`) skips the strike on an Impenetrable face and
pays 25 on every strike; the owner saw gold every swing and the face never crack.

**Decision.** Mining a gem face changes no health and releases `GoldMinedFromGems` per
strike, for every miner; the gold's crediting and hand-off are unchanged.

**Consequences.** A face never reaches its destroyed type, so no gem-mining task ends
on a collapse. An imp at the base rate earns twice the gold it did there.

## ADR-0471 — A worker's take fails when its walk cannot start
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted · Research: imp-task-stealing.md §7, imp-claim-path.md §4

**Context.** Q588. DK2's handlers take their task only if the walk starts
(`0x004651A0` → `0x00471890` → `0x004D0F60`); on a free claim slot the take's result is
the walk's. Ours chose stances on a grid with no
doors, committed the job whatever the router said, and dropped it on arrival as
`out_of_reach`: 4,979 such drops over Level 4's 20 seeds after ADR-0443.

**Decision.** For tile work, `CommitJob` routes first and commits nothing when the route
fails, emitting `job_unreachable`. The claim ring tries its next tile; reinforce forgets
a free side's task and tries the next side, as `0x0046AEA0` does. A held claim or
reinforce slot is kicked only after the walk starts. The dig caller still kicks first
and then moves to its next candidate tile, where `0x0046A550` tries the next slot and
side and `0x00469AF0` gives the selection up (Q590). Gold, object and body fetches still
ignore a failed route (Q590). Teleporting walks are unbuilt
(Q418); DK2's teleport also needs the target reachable. Not modelled: DK2 raises the task
and writes its flavour (`0x005080E0`) before the walk, and a failed walk keeps both.
Hash/save version 245, with ADR-0472.

**Consequences.** Level 4's `out_of_reach` drops fall from 4,979 to 17 (other walks);
Levels 1–3 replay identically (19/2/13). Level 4 wins 2/20 (seeds 9, 11) against 3/20
before (9, 11, 19), on master 15c2b038 and again on d1e67516. In seed 19, 26 imps'
takes of the owner's dig at (16,5) are refused 139 times, likely because the dig side is
chosen on the door-blind grid where DK2 tests each side's reachability and retries the
next slot and side (Q590, not traced). (17,5) then goes unclaimed and the owner's drop there misses.

## ADR-0472 — A worker tests a dig side, object or body for reachability first
**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** accepted · Research: imp-task-stealing.md §7a

**Context.** Q590. `0x00469AF0` keeps a dig side only if `Route_IsPointReachable(point,
0x80)` (`0x00471630`, a door-respecting route query) passes; the objects handler (`0x0046B9C0`)
asks it of the object's position before raising its task, the body handler (`0x0046D810`)
after raising it and before the walk or a steal.
Ours chose sides on the door-blind grid, so ADR-0471 refused 139 dig takes at (16,5) in
Level 4 seed 19.

**Decision.** `PointReachable` asks the router with the 0x80 profile: of each dig side
(the side tile's centre, its corner for a mine), each object and each body. A failed walk
now gives the state-10 dig selection up (`0x00469AF0` returns 0) and moves the gold and
object takes on to their next thing; a body take returns false, where DK2 tries the next
creature. Not built: the drop scan's slot-and-side
retry (`0x0046A550`) and gold's held-pile test (Q590). Hash/save version 245, with ADR-0471.

**Consequences.** On master b501992f, against master alone: Level 4's `out_of_reach`
drops fall from 5,976 to 8 over 20 seeds and 67 takes are refused up front; Levels 1–3
replay identically (20/2/8); Level 4 wins 2/20 either way (seeds 9, 11 against 3, 11),
7 of 20 replay traces changing. On d1e67516 the side test brought seed 13 back to a win
(3/20); the fetch refusals and the dig give-up never fire in these 80 runs and have no test.
On master d8bc7336 Levels 1–3 replay identically (20/3/9) and Level 4 wins 3/20 against
2/20 (seeds 4, 6, 13 against 6, 13); `out_of_reach` falls from 4,813 to 13.

## ADR-0473 — A fleeing creature counts only Guard Rooms near its attacker
**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted · Research: combat-fear.md §4 step 9, combat-alarm.md

**Context.** `0x00460B50`, which the flee run (`0x004602E0`) and the hero reluctance of the
acquirer both ask, walks the owner's rooms and skips each whose type byte `+0x18` is not 9
(`0x00460BC8`); `0x004C61C0` reads the same byte as the room type. Ours tested every room.
After commit 454 let Imps react to attackers, Level 3's fleeing Imps took the head-count
branch beside their own rooms, often found no alarm to raise (90 `no_alarm` ends in
seed 1 at that commit) and went back to work beside the Dwarves: seed 1 lost 9 Imps, 7 of them between ticks 1632 and
1848, where DK2's capture loses one, at tick 3687, and 72 of its 76 Imp flights end in the withdraw's arrival (202).

**Decision.** `FearRules.NearOwnGuardRooms` counts only the owner's Guard Rooms; away from
them the creature withdraws, as DK2's do. Hash/save version 246.

**Consequences.** On master d8bc7336, seeds 1–20: Levels 1–4 win 20/2/12/4 against
20/3/9/2; Imps lost fall from 78 to 6 in Level 3, 122 to 56 in Level 2 and 783 to 434 in
Level 4, and `no_alarm` ends vanish where there is no Guard Room. With ADR-0471/0472 on
master 434a966b: 18/5/14/5 against master's 18/4/11/2 (Level 1 changes seeds). Level 4's
1,052 `no_alarm` ends have DK2's shape: 142 are non-Scouts, and 812 of the 907 Imp ends fall
while another creature's alarm run is under way (`0x004754D0`), as in DK2's capture; the
other 95 Imp ends and 3 Firefly ends are unexplained.

## ADR-0474 — The Heart's mana sparkles rise to the Arch Pillars, an owner adjustment
**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted · Research: heart-mana-effects.md §4

**Context.** The owner watched DK2: the Heart's green sparkles originate at the Heart,
rise steadily to about the Arch Pillars' top, and pale flakes drift back down. Ours rose
to the arches' apex, 2.8 tiles over the pit floor. Every link of the chain re-read
(loader, initializer, origin draw, motion helper, HP quantum, parent lifecycle) and the
shipped data agree with the 2-tile climb; what lowers DK2's rise is unread (Q594).

**Decision.** `RoomConstructionParticles` takes a `HeartSparkleStyle`. `Native` keeps the
binary's motion and stays the default; `PillarHeight`, which Unity passes, starts a
rising sparkle inside the Heart mesh (1024 over the Heart's position, where DK2 draws
3200) and scales its vertical speed to 622/1000 so the cloud peaks about 1.5 tiles over
the pit floor (ring floor plus half a tile, the pillars' top as judged from screenshots).
Flakes keep their native motion. The Heart's effect is found through the Dungeon Heart
room's `CreatedObjectEffectId`, not a literal id.

**Consequences.** Presentation only: no simulation, save or hash change. The two numbers
are a fit to the owner's eye in Unity (the origin lowered twice on 2026-10-14, the first
build having started "where the stairs end"), not a reading; when Q594 is answered the
style is to be removed and the reading built in its place.

## ADR-0475 — The Heart's opening sequence: plug, burst, arches fading in
**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted · Research: heart-intro.md

**Context.** The owner recalled the player's Heart bursting from its tiles at level start,
creating the arches, then beating. `0x004D9A60`'s first branch is that sequence: from game
turn 1 (variable 218 ships as 0) the local player's Heart asks for effect 225, whose chain
draws the plug lid, its light and static, the explosion, the cracked plug, rocks, dust and
the nine flying plug pieces; seven seconds in it asks for the arches' sparkle ring (314)
while its Arches and Big Steps, created invisible, gain 32 alpha a turn to 255 at nine.
The ordinary room frame waits for the sequence. Another keeper's Heart gets none of it.

**Decision.** `HeartIntroRules` posts the requests for every Heart with the owner's tag;
the Unity runner keeps the owner-only ones (225, 314) for the viewing player. The viewer's
Arches and Big Steps carry an alpha the view computes from the turn; `ClassicMeshes.SetAlpha`
hides, blends and restores. The particle model learns what the chain needs from the
binary: a Next effect created with its parent, a death effect created at removal after the
last child dies, flag `0x40` generating effects, the `GenerateRandomness` gate, and a group
art's members flung as elements at birth, each drawing its own mesh (`KmfReader` reads
GROP). Regeneration and ruin wait for the sequence, as DK2's do (hash 247).

**Consequences.** A Heart hurt in its first nine seconds regenerates nine seconds later than
before; nothing else in play moves. The model changes reach every type-4 effect: a request
with flag `0x40` is no longer dropped, every effect's `GenerateRandomness` gates its waves
(shipped construction and capture effects carry 0), and Next and death effects chain where
the data names them; presentation only, with the view's own random stream. Not built: the
two sounds, the lights, the tile redraw, and flag `0x8000`'s fog bypass. The sequence's look
awaits the owner's comparison.

**Amendment, 2026-10-14 (hash 248).** The rules compared our tick to DK2's turn, which is
the tick plus one, so the plug was asked for a tick late and the pit showed first; and the
Unity runner drew frames before any tick ran. `HeartIntroRules.Turn` keys the sequence to
the game turn, and the runner ticks once, and runs one effect update, before its first
frame: DK2 asks for the lid on every turn before the start and by nothing else, so that
it draws no frame before its first turn is STRONGLY INFERRED (its render loop is unread).

## ADR-0476 — A Portal arrival's entrance effect, animated mesh effects, and brighter additive beams
**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted; the additive doubling superseded by ADR-0492 · Research: portal-creature-action.md, heart-intro.md §4

**Context.** The owner misses two lights: the white beams from a Portal's hole as a
creature climbs out, and the white beam standing on the Heart's plug before it bursts.
`Portal_CreateArrival` (`0x004DC9A0`) asks for the creature definition's Portal Entrance
effect (`+0x776`, file byte 3894) at the spawn point before the Entrance action, when the
effects detail setting is above 2; each creature's effect chains to the Portal Beams (159,
161, 166, 168), whose element is a sixty-frame animated model (art type 6); that it plays
at ten frames a second, its descriptor's second dword, is a HYPOTHESIS fitted to its
six-second life. Ours parsed no such field, requested nothing, and drew only static meshes. The
Heart's beam (element 379, additive `Falloff`, which peaks at 68 of 255) drew at a quarter
of DK2's blaze.

**Decision.** `CreatureDef.EntranceEffectId` is read and written at byte 3894.
`PortalRules.EntranceEffect` gives the request, which `PortalSystem` posts after the
arrival, at the hole's centre on its floor with the room owner's tag; ours has no detail
setting and always asks. The catalogue lists art type 6 elements; the Unity renderer
builds every frame of such a model once and draws the frame by the particle's age at the
authored rate, looping. Every additive effect-element mesh material is drawn at twice the
texture, a presentation choice: DK2's additive texture stage is unread.

**Consequences.** Presentation only: a view effect request is neither saved nor hashed.
The scripted arrival (action 28) posts no effect yet: its path has no simulation context.
Whether DK2's beam brightness is a doubled stage or something else is open; the owner's
eye decides the look.

## ADR-0477 — Foot dust on a Dirt Path
**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted · Research: creature-movement-dust.md

**Context.** The owner misses the dust an Imp raises running over dirt. The creature
update (`0x00488930` at `0x0048A06A`) asks for effect 117, Foot Dust, when a creature's
previous and current positions lie on different tiles and its tile's terrain is id 3,
the Dirt Path: one request per crossing at the creature's position one tile up with its
heading, no test of mode, speed, kind or flight, noticed on the update after the move on
the arrived tile. The reading was complete; nothing requested it.

**Decision.** `MovementDustSystem`, just before the mover, compares each creature's tile
with the one it saw last tick and posts the request on a crossing onto a Dirt Path. Held
creatures and corpses, which have no creature update of their own here, are skipped.

**Consequences.** Presentation only: the request and the per-creature last tile are
neither saved nor hashed. DK2 tests the crossing at the update's entry, before the
previous-position refresh and the state handler, so ours differs only when a handler
moves a creature within a tick. The status-timer requests of the same effect
(creature-status-effects.md §1) are separate and unbuilt. The look, eight grey mist
puffs a crossing, awaits the owner's eye.

## ADR-0478 — Allow a small configurable extension to camera zoom-out
**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** The owner requested slightly more zoom-out distance after trying
the Classic Step5 camera.

**Decision.** DungeonRunner extends its presentation copy of the authored
maximum zoom by a configurable multiplier, default1.2. Scale1 restores the
original bound. Initial zoom, minimum, lens and wheel increments are unchanged.

**Consequences.** This is an explicit convenience deviation from the native
bound in research/classic-camera.md section3. Original data and simulation
remain unchanged; far clipping continues to follow actual zoom.

## ADR-0479 — Room ticks between the creatures and the players
**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted · Research: binary-census.md §2, §9

**Context.** `World_UpdateTurn` runs the thing pass, then `0x004EC450`, which runs every
room's `Room_Tick` (the type's handler at slot `+0x15`, then the health step), then the
player frame (Q595). Ours ran the Casino before the creatures and the Portal and room
health inside the player frame. Reading the twelve unread handlers found one unbuilt rule:
`0x004E8C60`, shared by the Library, Training Room, Guard Room and Workshop, angers a room's
place-holders every 32 turns when both alignments meet there. The rest spawn effects, several
drawing from the world's random stream.

**Decision.** A `RoomTicks` phase between `Work` and `PlayerFrame` holds the store sweep,
Heart defence, `CasinoSystem`, `PortalSystem`, the new `HatedCompanySystem` and
`RoomHealthSystem`. The Casino's lever command (`0x00513E50`) is an action of the frame's
start, so it splits out as `CasinoLeverSystem` at the old slot. The new step gives each holder without `DoesntGetAngryWithEnemies`
eight seconds of variable 78 (1200) in the Treatment bucket, complaint 7, when the room holds
an `IsEvil` creature and one without it. Hash 249, no new saved field.

**Consequences.** The Hatchery stays in the needs phase, since its system also runs the
eggs' and coops' object steps; the egg is taken to be inedible until it hatches, so laying
after the eaters should not matter. The Combat Pit stays in the thing pass and the Heart's
frame at the tick's end. Our rooms carry no id, so the step's phase is the room's lowest
tile: the rule is DK2's, but the first angry turn of a room is not. Measured on Levels 1-4
over seeds 1-20 against master 7ddf4603: wins 18/5/14/5 on both, the same seeds; one Level
3 win moves from 3592 to 3700. The new step fires in none of the 80 runs, since no room there
holds both alignments, so the reorder alone made that difference.

## ADR-0480 — The stun counts from its first call, with the dazed stars
**Date:** 2026-10-15 · **Status:** accepted · Research: hand-drop-landing.md §3, creature-status-effects.md §2

**Context.** The owner saw dropped Goblins get up fast, with no stars. The binary
(`0x004810E0`, read by disassembly) compares `now − state+0x18` with `StunDuration` as the
loader stored it in turns (`0x00493B57`: file × ticks a second >> 12), so the Goblin's 1 s is
four turns, the shortest of the creatures checked (Warlock and Troll 2 s, Bile Demon 5 s);
`CreatureStunnedTimeSeconds` (2) is only written (`Variables_SetMisc`), never read. Ours
counted the stun down in the tick it was set, one turn short of Level 1's 255 × 4. On its
first call (Age 1) the handler creates effect 101, Creature Dazed Effect (two "dazed" star
elements and a sparkle on a circular path, one wave, elements 60 updates), at the point
`0x10C(creature, 0x1388)` gives, and ties it to the creature (effect `+0x133`, `+0x135`);
`0x00434E80` moves the effect and its elements with that point. Ours never asked for it.

**Decision.** For 255 and 256, the countdown and the request wait for the turn after the
state was set; the first counted turn asks for 101 at the creature, one tile up (the height
the foot dust is asked at) plus half its eye height. Hash 250, no new saved field.

**Consequences.** A hand drop now lies 4 turns, gets up in 11 and stands from the 15th,
one turn short of DK2's, which spends the drop turn in 76; that turn is not modelled. The
effect's height is a GUESS for the unread mesh point, and the effect does not follow the
creature: a stunned creature does not move, but one lifted while stunned leaves its stars.
The skip is exact for a stun set after the victim's own update, as the hand's and
Lightning's are (the player frame). DK2's dispatcher (`0x00476FC0`) counts Age up before
each call, so a stun set earlier in the same turn than the victim's update, a boulder's or
a Reaper fireball's from a creature in an earlier slot, gets its first call that turn; ours
waits a turn for every stun.

**Amendment (2026-10-15): the point is the head, and the stars follow it.** Slot `+0x10C`
is the engine interface's `0x0059D380` (the callers' object being that interface is LIKELY):
it searches the thing's drawn mesh for the KMF CTRL point with the id asked
(`0x0059D260`). In an animation that point is a (primitive, vertex) pair evaluated at the drawn
frame (`0x005835E0`); id 5000 is the head in the creatures checked (Goblin, Warlock, Bile
Demon), at the top of a standing
creature and near the floor at the end of its knockdown. The guessed height is gone: the
simulation asks at the creature's floor position, DK2's own fallback, and ties the request
to the creature and point 5000. The KMF reader keeps CTRL, `RenderMesh` maps animated points
to vertices, the Unity scene publishes each drawn creature's head for the effects' worker
thread, and the effect model moves a tied effect and its elements with the head each update,
dropping the tie when the creature's object goes. Static-mesh points are not resolved. No
hash change.

## ADR-0481 — The original's own functions are run as a test oracle
**Date:** 2026-10-15 · **Status:** accepted · Tests: `tests/DK2.Oracle.Tests`; tool: `tools/oracle/dk2oracle.py`

**Context.** A reading of a function is somebody's reading; a C# port of a reading can drift
from the bytes in a constant, a shift's sign or an overflow, and the replay rigs show such a
slip only as distant drift. A function whose answer depends only on its arguments and the
image's own bytes can instead be run: the owner allowed the Unicorn emulator (GPLv2) to be
used but not committed (2026-10-15).

**Decision.** `DK2.Oracle.Tests` reads the install's `DKII.EXE` at test time (v1.70, MD5
checked) and holds our C# to it: tables byte for byte, functions value by value on swept
inputs, a function with several arms failing if one goes unreached (the gate walk's). The
emulator runs in `dk2oracle.py`, CPython (`py -3`, or `DK2_PYTHON`) loading `unicorn.dll`
from `DK2_UNICORN_DLL`, because a .NET host fail-fasts under Unicorn (`docs/TRAPS.md`); no
Unicorn package, binary or source enters the repository. The function tests skip without
it; the table tests need only the install. Where the original's divide faults, DK2 itself
would crash, so the input is outside what can be matched: it is counted and logged, not
compared.

**Consequences.** What has been run and what it found is in `research/emulator-oracle.md`:
four batches of pure functions, all equal where the original returns once two ports were
fixed. Running the bytes is binary evidence, so `[Dk2Behavior]` still rises no higher than
STRONGLY INFERRED (ADR-0046 rule 5); a function record may say CONFIRMED for what the
function computes, not for behaviour seen in play. A quotient past 32 bits wraps in
`Fixed16.Div` where the original faults (a zero divisor throws in both); whether any game
input reaches it was not checked.

A function that reads world state runs on one tick of a full-state capture
(`capture_memory.py`), our C# beside it on a world rebuilt from the level and the tick
(`capture_state.py`, `CapturedState`). One that reads definitions or heap a capture omits runs
on a whole-process dump (`process_dump.py`, the recorder's `--dump-ticks`), taken with the game
suspended; `dk2oracle.py` gives it an FS segment and moves its own pages clear of the game's.

## ADR-0486 — The mesh's locate is the original's cell-cache walk, and the builder keeps its slots
**Date:** 2026-10-15 · **Status:** accepted · advances ADR-0157, ADR-0461 · Research: `docs/research/navigation-partial-rebuild.md` §5, Q591

**Context.** ADR-0461 transcribed the per-tile rebuild but left where its walks
start to ours: `Locate` returned the lowest slot holding a point, and the
whole-map builder kept its own reset diagonal, corner order, split layout and
Sloan constraint insertion. The owner then ran the original on Level 10 with the
mesh probe: 141 mesh dumps and 2,132 byte changes over 1,110 ticks. Replayed
from each dump to the next through `Retriangulate`, the edits reproduced 106 of
140 intervals exactly, and the whole-map build matched the first dump in 2,674
of 2,828 triangles and 96 slots. The misses were rock quads beside a dug tile
given the other diagonal, and slot numbers.

**Decision.** `Locate` is `0x004C98B0`: a walk from a sixteen-cell cache of
last results (64-tile squares, refreshed through `0x004C97B0` when the cached
triangle died), stepping across the one edge the point lies beyond or turning
the fan (`0x004C9540`) around the corner between two, returning the first
triangle that holds the point and caching it. The cache is state, saved in
place of the locate hint and hashed, since it decides which holder of a vertex
an edit starts from. The whole-map builder takes the original's reset diagonal
(`0x004C8D10`, (x1,y0) to (x0,y1)), corner and constraint order (`0x004CCCB0`),
interior split (`0x004CA500`: the triangle keeps edge 0 and takes the point at
slot 2), edge split (`0x004CA820`: each side keeps the half from its own start)
and constraint insertion (`0x004CBD10` with the flip sweep `0x004CBBD0`) in
place of the Sloan queue, each written in the original's slot numbers through
one view of our storage (NavMesh.Slots.cs). The scanner (`0x004CE570`,
`0x004CE4E0`) was read and is ours already. Hash/save version 255.

**Consequences.** On the capture 130 of 140 intervals now reproduce the
original's dump slot for slot; the other 10 are STRONGLY INFERRED to be the
probe's timing: 9 differ only in door or dig bytes the log places within two
ticks of the dump, 1 only in which of two tiles changed in one tick was written
first. The whole-map build matches the first dump in 2,826 of 2,828 triangles
(one rock quad's diagonal) and 2,823 slots. Rerun with the old lowest-slot
locate, the same builder gives 108 of 140 and 2,795 triangles, so the dumps
confirm the walk. Routes should tie-break as the original's do (no route log
was captured); scenario hashes moved and the pins were regenerated. Residuals:
the cache carries every locate's history, route endpoints included, which only
a capture with its route log would show; that one quad; refresh batching
(ADR-0461); our guards throw where the original would loop. tools/meshreplay
replays a capture.

## ADR-0482 ? Project animated creature silhouettes through a shared GPU atlas
**Date:** 2026-10-15 ? **Status:** accepted ? Research: creature-shadows.md

**Context.** Creature shadows were absent. Native mesh-shadow generation,
projection, source selection and multiply blending are traced. Enabling Unity
shadow maps on every torch would use a different representation and cost.

**Decision.** Classic meshes project their current opaque animation triangles
into 32-pixel coverage tiles, using GPU 8x supersampling and bilinear reception.
One growable atlas and receiver mesh batch the visible projections. Up to three
nearby wall torches supply the confirmed high-quality projection and fade;
receivers use the existing floor-height query plus its native 0.01 bias.
Shadow preparation runs before the simulation worker starts.

**Consequences.** Presentation only, no hash/save changes. Bounds come from
Unity's current mesh AABB rather than the native model sphere; directly-above
lights use a finite axis fallback. Range/capacity currently use the traced
2.5/3 defaults. All opaque creature meshes participate until their native
RenderInfo enable producer is resolved; other shadow-source kinds, original
quality settings and the alternate 8-bit path remain unbuilt. Atlas dimensions
are bounded by the GPU's maximum texture size. Matched-game acceptance and
busy-view GPU profiling remain pending; the controlled GPU fixture verifies
shape, orientation, alpha, source removal and animation continuity.

## ADR-0484 - Publish selected classic point lights through tile-indexed buffers
**Date:** 2026-10-15 - **Status:** accepted - Research: classic-lighting.md section9

**Context.** Native point-light tables belong to cache tiles; a combined Unity
mesh can contain pieces from many tiles and vertices outside their source tile.
Native visibility, encounter order and source classification still require
integration before automatic publication can be faithful.

**Decision.** Keep publication explicit through `DungeonScene.SetPointLightTable`.
Use reusable CPU storage and structured GPU buffers indexed by tile. Opaque,
sorted transparent and liquid batches carry their emitting tile in UV2;
standalone meshes use their object origin. Separate shader variants bind only
the resources required by the selected lighting mode.

**Consequences.** The bridge accepts selected per-vertex point lights, not raw
authored world sources. Once active, tables replace punctual lighting for the
whole grid; empty tiles stay without punctual light through Clear, and Dispose
restores the existing path. Scene ambient/directional fallback remains separate.
No simulation changes or automatic source publisher; normal preview is unchanged.
## ADR-0483 — The approach is state 8, a walk resuming 199
**Date:** 2026-10-15 · **Status:** accepted · Amends ADR-0169

**Context.** ADR-0169 built the walk to a fight target as a flag on state 199, so every reader of
the state word saw a fighter. ADR-0366's amendment found one cost: experience paid on the walk.
DK2 enters state 8 (`0x00471D10`, `SetState(8)`, then the caller's state, 199 in practice, in the
resume slot), and its
engagement tails re-enter 199 only outside category 22 read through a walk (`0x00478050`): the
fight-starter `0x0045A550`, and SelectAVictim's thing branch, which also re-enters from state 6
resuming 251 or 202 (`0x0045E0C0`). So DK2's approach survives the every-tick reselection.

**Decision.** `ApproachRules.Enter` begins a walk into state 8 resuming 199; `End` hands back to
199 unless a disengage has idled the creature; `Unlink` and the victory leave the state alone, and
state 8 ends an approach with no target at its first step. `Approaching` is the state, out of the
hash and the snapshot. `ActivityRules` names state 8 by its resume, so the activity stays
Fighting. The engagement's 199 is gated as DK2's is; the ally arm takes the creature rule, unread.
Unread and kept as under the flag: whether state 8's mover steers with no route (199's movement
exemption stays), and `0x0048ECE0`, which DK2 calls before resuming.

**Consequences.** Level 4 seed 1's first Dwarves switch between 8 and 199 13 and 8 times in
their first 110 turns against DK2's 15 and 14, where under the flag they never left 199; ours
spend 52 of 61 ticks in 8 against DK2's 27 of 58, a residual. A same-state re-entry of 199
no longer restamps a fighter's state age. Seeds 1–20 against master d449c99d: Level 1 19 → 20,
Level 2 6 → 9, Level 3 18 → 17, Level 4 3 → 2, one seed each way on Level 4 (2 and 12 lost, 3
won); the keeper still loses a median 16 Imps a seed where DK2 loses none. Level 3 seed 8's Lord,
dead at 3596, engaged a forced door at 3601: a forced target skips the may-I-look gate, the only
test that refused a corpse. `CombatSystem` now skips corpses, as DK2's thing pass never meets one
(its dead creature is a `CDeadBody`), and the gate never moves a creature with no state (Q598); no
replay trace changes.
`HashVersion` 253, `FormatVersion` 253.

## ADR-0487 - Gather prepared light cells in native rolling order
**Date:** 2026-10-15 - **Status:** accepted - Research: classic-lighting.md section9

**Context.** Nearest-source overflow keeps equal-distance encounter order.
Flattening nearby cells in world-coordinate order changes which lights survive
after the visible-tile traversal advances horizontally.

**Decision.** `ClassicLightWindow` reads an explicit prepared-cell provider and
feeds `ClassicLightTable` without allocating candidate lists. One window follows
one visible enumeration; its caller resets it at that enumeration's boundary.
Unsigned source/table stamps and retained column dirty bits govern static
refresh; dynamic slots always rebuild. Rolling updates read seven entering
cells and retain the other42 list heads until the enumeration resets.

**Consequences.** Candidate traversal is engine-neutral and reusable by the Unity
bridge. Visibility, cache preparation, source classification and automatic
world publication remain separate integration work. No change to
the current preview or simulation.
## ADR-0485 — Only a keeper's creatures run the needs, need-anger and mood choosers
**Date:** 2026-10-15 · **Status:** accepted · Q599

**Context.** The dispatcher `0x00476FC0` tests the owner before its needs block: the hero player
(`[0x006F254C]`) skips the need-anger routine `0x00478D00`, the needs routine and the unhappy and
angry choosers; the neutral player (`[0x006F2548]`) runs `0x004790A0` instead
(creature-needs-routine.md §1). `NeedRules.IsAsked` carried that test, but only the cannot-sleep
health loss read it: Level 4's three placed Guards took lair anger, looked for lairs and
hatcheries and rolled Rebel from tick 1192 in every seed; in seed 1 one was already hurt (2700)
before the owner's drop at (24,28) that wakes them in DK2, cause not traced.

**Decision.** `NeedRules.RunsNeeds`, a keeper's creature, gates `MayAsk` (eating, sleeping,
payday), the idle lair attempt, the need charges of `CreatureAngerRules.PerSecond` and the angry
and unhappy choosers. The in-lair cooling stays for everyone: it is the lair category hooks'
(`0x004DFF00`), which run before the owner test. A creature that defects to the hero side keeps
the anger it had and gains no more. Read whole (CONFIRMED); the needs doc said STRONGLY INFERRED.

**Consequences.** Level 4 seed 1's Guards now meet the drop at the door, Guard 10 down at 5385, as
DK2's are beaten there. Seeds 1–20 against master 7c17ce08: 20/9/17/2 to 20/9/16/2; Level 4's
keeper Imp deaths 399 to 372 in all, a median of 17 a seed where DK2 loses none, now mostly to the
parties at the second Guard Room from tick 4000. `HashVersion` 254.

## ADR-0488 — A creature getting up may look for a fight
**Date:** 2026-10-15 · **Status:** accepted · Research: combat-acquisition.md §2, hand-drop-landing.md §3

**Context.** The may-look gate `0x0045A6D0` opens with `TEST [state×25 + 0x6DA8C8], 0x40` at
`0x0045A71F`, the state table's flag byte, bit 6, and refuses on it. Fifteen states carry the bit:
the stuns 209, 210, 255, 256, 263 and 264, and 153, 158, 193, 278–280, 269, 272 and 273 (dancing,
gambling, joining and idle by the table's own labels, not read). 257, getting
up, carries flag 2, so a creature rising from a drop or a shot looks for a fight while its get-up
plays. Ours refused the whole stunned activity, 255–257, and the frozen one. In Level 4 seed 1 DK2's
owner drops ten creatures beside the 3830 hero party; each goes 257 → 199 or 8 one to eight ticks
after getting up, on the hero registered on it, and all three heroes are down by about 3940
(measured in the capture, state `+0x25E`, target `+0x502`). Ours
held 257 to its end and stood in 250 until about 3940 while the party walked on to the second Guard
Room.

**Decision.** `MayLookForAFight` tests `CreatureStateFlags.NoFightLookup` (bit 6, formerly
`Unread6`) on the creature's state and the freeze timer, as the gate does, instead of the stunned
and frozen activities. The victim pick `0x00481400` at 257's end is still not built.

**Consequences.** Level 4 seeds 1–20 against master 289041ed: the western party's last hero is down
at a median of 4238, from 4301 (DK2's seed 1 about 3940); keeper Imp deaths before 4400 86 to 85.
Wins 19/4/16/1 to 19/5/16/0, within a seed each. The fight's remaining gap is head count (we drop 7
creatures to DK2's 10; the entity map's placeholders) and damage: about 1,940 in the first 50 ticks
against DK2's 7,100. `HashVersion` 257.

## ADR-0489 — A creature's spell shot leaves from its slot's origin
**Date:** 2026-10-15 · **Status:** accepted · Research: combat-spells.md §3, §7; Q398

**Context.** Action 16 (`0x00498870`) makes its shot at the caster's position plus the slot's origin
vector turned by its heading (`0x00498989`–`0x004989F5`: dx = vx·cos − vy·sin, dy = vx·sin + vy·cos,
each product shifted down sixteen, from the tables at `0x006C1488`/`0x006C1C88`); a possessed caster
adds only the height. The vector is the slot record's first twelve file bytes: the Warlock's (0, −1761,
1433), the Dark Elf's (0, −2048, 2662), half a tile ahead. Ours fired from the caster's centre and did not
parse the vector. In our Level 4 seed 1 run, three Dark Elves dropped beside a hero party at 3907–3909 fired from
0.4–0.8 tile; at 1.2 tiles a tick each shot's first sample was short of its target and the next past it,
and all three flew on to a wall.

**Decision.** `CreatureSpellSlot` carries `OriginX/Y/Z`, read and written; `FightRules.ShotOrigin`
places the shot as the binary does, flat (the height goes with the flight's, Q398).

**Consequences.** Level 4 seeds 1–20 against ADR-0488: the keeper side's shot hits 563 of 1,164 to 623
of 1,236 (48 to 50 per cent), so point-blank misses were a small share of its misses; wins 0 to 2, Imp
deaths 396 to 395, both within the seeds' spread. `HashVersion` 258.

## ADR-0490 — A hero party stands on its spawn tile's corner
**Date:** 2026-10-15 · **Status:** accepted · Research: hero-parties-and-effect-generators.md, "Where the party appears"

**Context.** Trigger action 14 (`0x00519F90`) places a party at the action point's centre tile times
4096, the tile's corner (the compiler adds and takes away `0x800`); a 2x2 Hero Gate moves it a tile right
and down, to the gate's centre point, a corner too. Ours stood the members at the tile's centre, a stated
deviation. DK2's Level 4 seed 1 capture shows the 3830 party at exactly (15.00, 29.00); its leader
reaches the next tile 18 ticks after spawning. Ours, from the centre, reached it in 7 ticks, walked on
past the western spot where the owner's drop lands, and the dropped Trolls spent the fight walking.

**Decision.** `HeroPartyRules.Spawn` puts each member, and its last position, on the corner of the tile
it is made on, except on a 3x1 gate, whose step-off takes a tile centre in DK2 too (`0x00519BB5`–
`0x00519C52`); a Tile gate's creature is made on the corner and routed to its side. CONFIRMED by the
disassembly of `0x00519F90` and `0x00519B20` and by DK2's capture.
`HeroPartyRules`' stale "no party pace" note goes: the pace is built (ADR-0216).

**Consequences.** In our Level 4 seed 1 run the leader now reaches the next tile in 13 ticks. Level 4,
seeds 1–20, against ADR-0489: keeper Imp deaths 395 to 301 (median 17.5 to 12), 104 to 78 before 4400;
the western party is down at a median of 4188, from 4232. Wins on Levels 1–4, against master
07261474: 19/6/16/2 to 17/6/14/1. Every seed's win tick moves; Level 1 loses seeds 1, 6 and 14 and gains
19, Level 3 loses five and gains three, which reads as a reshuffle, not examined. `HashVersion` 259.

## ADR-0491 — A level's VARIABLES id 77 sets creature definition fields
**Date:** 2026-10-15 · **Status:** accepted · Research: variables-corpus-sweep.md §Q84; Q84

**Context.** VARIABLES id 77 (`0x0051DD10`) looks a creature type up and stores a value into the
definition field a `CreatureStatId` selector names (`0x00494A70`); a level carries several. Level 1
gives its Lord of the Land MeleeDamage 200 and Threat 125 (file Threat 320), Level 4 Threat 150; the
others touch Health, Fear, the speeds and the hearing distance. Our reader kept one record per id and
nothing applied them. The fear accumulator (`0x0045E4F0`) reads Threat unscaled at level 1
(`0x0045E5B5`): in DK2's Level 1 capture the Lord's six Goblins take shares of 17-20 (threat 124-125),
stay under their threshold and never flee; ours took 53, fled eleven times, and the Lord walked
between them and lived.

**Decision.** `KwdVariables` keeps every id 77 record in file order (`CreatureFieldOverrides`, global
then level); `GameDatabase.ForLevel` applies them, a later record winning. Mapped are the seven
selectors the shipped levels use: 1 Health, 2 Fear, 3 Threat, 4 MeleeDamage, 21 and 22 the speeds in
file units (the setter divides by variable 19 without the loader's minimum of 1, a difference no
shipped value reaches), 30 the hearing distance (`+0x77F`) in whole tiles, stored raw; any other
throws. Id 66 (the
alliances, Q576) stays unbuilt.

**Consequences.** In our Level 1 seed 1 run the Lord's share is 20, no Goblin flees, and he dies at 1784
at (15,10), DK2's at 1777 at (15.5,11.9). Levels 1–4, seeds 1–20, against master 3a9ad262:
17/6/14/1 to 20/6/14/1; Levels 2–4 replay identically (Level 4's Lord does not fight within the
replay). `HashVersion` 261 (master took 260 first).

## ADR-0492 — The Heart plug's pieces, effect lights, and additive effect meshes at their texture
**Date:** 2026-10-16 · **Status:** accepted · Research: heart-intro.md §3, §5, §6 · Supersedes ADR-0476's doubling

**Context.** The owner found the Heart's opening too dark, as if a texture were missing. Every
texture of the chain loads; three things differ from DK2. The nine pieces of `Group_plugbroke`
(effect 215, element 396) were never born: ours tested the floor at a part's birth and the KMF
offsets put every member just under the lid, while DK2's allocator (`0x004352E0`, `0x00435F20`)
has no floor test; and 396's scale range is 0..0, the size being the member record's `0x1000`.
Resolving a member's mesh threw (`"mesh-entry"` is no `AssetRef` category), which the dead
pieces hid. The lights of effects 208 (a white flash at the burst) and 210 (a blue glow under the
sparkles) were not built. And ADR-0476 drew every additive effect mesh at twice its texture on a
guess, where the binary reading, STRONGLY INFERRED, draws it once (white diffuse, MODULATE,
ONE/ONE, one-sided; three vertex sinks and the per-vertex colour bit are unread, heart-intro.md §6).

**Decision.** A group part is born at its member's point without a floor test and at scale
`0x1000`. `AssetRef` gains the `mesh_entry` category; `InstallArtProvider.TryResolveEntry` keys
an entry by its name without the extension. Each effect instance whose light record has flag 1
or any RGB keeps a light with the fade ramp of `0x0043A2E0`, stepped after every effect update
and before removal, and ending with the instance; `ClassicPointLight.FromEffect` applies the
object descriptor rules at intensity 128/128 and `ClassicWorldLightCache.UpdateEffects` puts
the lights among each tile's dynamic sources. The Unity effects renderer advances the model
before the frame's lighting is prepared and draws additive effect meshes at their texture.

**Consequences.** Presentation only: nothing saved or hashed. The Portal beams and every other
additive effect mesh are now half as bright as under ADR-0476; the owner's look at DK2's beam
decides whether an unread link brightens it. The effect update now runs DK2's three passes (every
effect, every light, then removal; `0x0043BFE0`), so the view's random draws for death effects come
after all waves of an update, not interleaved with them. After a catch-up of several updates an
effect born in it has its light stepped once per update caught up, where DK2 would step it once.
The two sounds of the sequence remain unbuilt.

**Amendment (2026-10-16).** Opaque effect meshes now take their element's tint as added light, as
`0x00581BE0` adds RenderInfo `+0x48` (the element's RGB, `0x00435F20`; zero for an element without
art, `0x004B3610`) before the lights: the plug lid drew black, lit only at its rim by the Heart's
orange light (heart-intro.md §6). And a sprite element with art flag `0x100` is drawn as DK2's
`0x0059C720` draws it, a square of half-size scale/4096 lying flat at the element and turned by its
heading, not a billboard: the plug's light overlay (407) had stood as a pale square before the lid
one update in eight, the owner's "white flicker" (object-drawing.md §10). Fourteen elements carry
the flag, blood pools and the Portal's white disc among them; the corner light term is not added.
Last, the keeper's palette colours an element with art flag `0x2` (`0x00435F20` at `0x00436332`),
not `0x80`, the play-once bit our model had tested since 2b83ebd9: the plug's dust (381, `0x85`)
and the bed's element 162 (`0x84`) had been drawn in the keeper's colour instead of their own grey
and purple. The claim and reinforce elements carry both bits and keep the keeper's colour.

## ADR-0493 — Effect sprites take the lights and their descriptor's size
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** accepted · Research: object-drawing.md §10

**Context.** DK2 lights a whole effect sprite, billboard (`0x0057F3D0`) or flat (`0x0057FB80`),
by its tint plus the radial term of the listed lights at its centre (`0x0057C080`); ours drew the
tint alone. Its billboard (`0x0059C360`) is scale × the descriptor's width and height, lifted by
half its height under art flag `0x40`; ours drew every billboard square at the scale. 496 of 511
effect sprites have a 4096-square descriptor, so the size only changes the other 15.

**Decision.** `ClassicPointLight.RadialAt` gives the radial term; `ClassicWorldLightCache`
hands out a visible tile's table; the Unity effects renderer adds every light of the sprite's
tile to its colour, clamped at 255 per channel, for billboards and flat squares alike, and sizes
a billboard by its descriptor, raising a flag-`0x40` sprite by half its height along the camera's
up axis. That the list is the tile's whole table is INFERRED, that the shift is a lift STRONGLY
INFERRED (object-drawing.md §10).

**Consequences.** Presentation only. Sprites near torches, the Heart and effect lights are
brighter than before in every channel their tint leaves below 255 (a channel at 255 is capped); the 15 odd-sized sprites (drips, door and Horny flames, the eye glow) change
shape, and the six flag-`0x40` sprites stand on their points.

**Amendment (2026-10-21).** The light sum is withdrawn; effect sprites draw at their tint alone.
The owner reported the Heart's appearance dust turned brown, its cyan plug sparkles (384, 408)
white and too bright, and the claim mist a pale fog instead of the keeper's colour. A probe A/B
of the Heart intro tied the dust and sparkles to the added Heart lights (orange, the blue glow,
the burst's white flash), and without them the dust matched DK2's grey (SHOT0007-0013). DK2's
draws do add a list (CONFIRMED), but its filler is unread; for effects it is taken as empty
(HYPOTHESIS). Against it: the list has the tile-table layout, the items are queued on their tile
(`0x00571AE0`) for a later unread pass, and nothing else is known to fill it, so DK2 may light
them after all and our light set (or sample point, or cap) differ instead (Q609). The claim
mist's fix is inferred from the same cause, not probed. Descriptor sizing and the lift stay.

## ADR-0494 - Wall flames use a frame-independent playback clock
**Date:** 2026-10-17 - **Status:** accepted - Research: torch-animation.md

**Context.** The native torch advances once per accepted presentation frame.
Mapping that directly to Unity Update sped up playback on modern frame rates;
the owner reported fast-burning torches after61cc8748.

**Decision.** Keep native integer phase steps and independent per-torch offsets,
but drive them from an unscaled50ms playback quantum, independently of Unity FPS.
This restores the earlier20Hz adapter baseline. Do not cap the game's frame rate.

**Consequences.** This is an explicit presentation-timing deviation, not a claim
that retail DK2 renders at20FPS. A timed original-game comparison may replace
the baseline (Q604). Simulation, particles and animation phase offsets do not
change. Repeated updates/camera draws at the same clock time cannot accelerate it.

## ADR-0495 - Trigger action 20 hands over the Portal Gem, and its carrier sparkles
**Date:** 2026-10-17 - **Status:** accepted - Research: functions/0049AC80.md, functions/005A3AA0.md

**Context.** The owner saw a sparkling trail behind Level 1's Lord of the Land. Level 1's
trigger 85 fires on his creation (creature event 3) with action 20 and action 42. Creature
action 20 (`0x0049AC80` arm `0x14`) creates object 28, the Portal Gem, at the creature, owned
by its keeper, gives it to the creature (`Creature_PickUpCarriedThing`, `0x0048B350`, which
refuses a creature already carrying something) and sets creature `+0x92` bit 2 either way. Only
the renderer reads that bit: `Render_MeshEffectPoints` (`0x005A3AA0`) gives off effect 257, Gem
dust sparkles, at each mesh control point 10001 after every draw, through the view's gated
creator (`0x0043A8E0` to `0x00440420`). The Lord's walk and run meshes carry a point 10001. A Level 1 dump
with the map explored held nine 257s at the Lord and no other effect near him. The gem's own
idle effect (297, object state 50, `0x004A3C30`) is not made while it is carried. The pick-up
unlinks the gem from its tile (`Thing_UnlinkFromTile` in `0x0048B350`), and the per-tile draw
pass walks tile chains, so a carried gem is not drawn (LIKELY). Action 20 ships in 14 levels.
We left the action unperformed.

**Decision.** Perform creature action 20: spawn the gem at the creature's tile, hand it over
unless the creature already carries an object, and set `CreatureState.GemCarrier` (hashed and
saved; HashVersion and snapshot format 263). The carrier's ordinary death drop puts the gem on
its tile, as DK2's capture shows at the Lord's death. The view exposes `CreatureView.GemCarrier`;
Unity requests effect 257 at the drawn mesh's point 10001 through the same visibility test as
other effects. Its owner is the viewer, an inference: DK2 passes the render sink's word `+0xC`,
whose writer is unread. DK2 asks once per draw. Ours asks at most once per draw
and once per 50 ms presentation quantum, as ADR-0494 paces the wall flames, because retail
DK2's frame rate is open (Q604).

**Consequences.** Level 1 over 20 seeds is unchanged: 20/20, every win tick identical to master
dfa707e1. The trail density follows our quantum, not DK2's frame rate; the dump suggests about
4.5 draws per 50 ms in DK2 (Q606). A mesh with several points 10001 gives off one sparkle, since
our clip keeps one point per id. Not built: the dropped gem's state 50 (bob, spin, effect 297),
the other mesh-point effects (262, 292), the pick-up icon 5 and the action-42 slot icons (Q607).
The arm's creation of the gem goes through our object spawn, which has no failure path; DK2's
can fail and then sets nothing.

## ADR-0496 — Scripted camera paths, the letterbox and subtitles; condition 72 waits for the path
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** accepted · Research: camera-paths.md

**Context.** DK2's campaign levels open with scripted camera paths: `.KCS` files in
Paths.WAD, started by trigger action 31. The camera plays them at 30 frames a
wall-clock second inside a letterbox, with the Mentor's subtitles in the bottom bar.

The scripts wait for each path with condition 72, "the camera is still". Ours
answered that condition true at once (an assumption). Level 1's after-intro actions
therefore ran on turn 2:
- its timer 15 started about 30 s early;
- the area its fly-over reveals with action 17 was hidden again before anyone saw it.

**Decision.**
- Each keeper's state gains `CameraPathEndTick`, saved and hashed (hash and snapshot
  262). Action 31 sets it from the path's frame count, which GameDatabase reads from
  Paths.WAD. It refuses while a path plays, while possessing, or when the file is
  missing. `0x0044A370` also refuses in mode 0xB and during a timed transition
  (`+0xDD8`); those are not modelled.
- Condition 72 answers false until that tick.
- `SkipCameraPathCommand` (Escape or Space) ends the path before the turn's walk.
- Actions 24, 26, 31 and 38 emit `ScriptedViewRequest`s.
- The presentation plays them on the wall clock through `ScriptedViewDirector`: path
  playback, the counted letterbox, the speech-off subtitle queue, and action 26's
  glide.

**Consequences.**
- Level 1's opening now waits a nominal 53 ticks for the plug path and 67 more
  for the fly-over. These are DK2's wall-clock lengths at 250 ms a tick; no capture
  pins the real turn counts. Its point 2 is explored for the fly-over and hidden after
  it. Level win rates may move, toward DK2.
- The path's length is measured in game ticks, where DK2 measures wall clock; the
  two agree at normal speed.
- The state is per keeper, where DK2 has one local camera.
- Not built: the timed moves condition 72 also waits for (action 26's glide,
  action 27), the subtitle overflow scroll, speech audio, action 38's interface
  slots, and action 24's message record.

- Superseded in part by ADR-0498: the view plays the path on ticks, not the wall clock.

## ADR-0497 — One HUD that scales: DK2's interface design at any resolution
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** proposed · Presentation only · Extends ADR-0242 to the interface · Rules: `ART_DIRECTION.md` §13

**Context.** The HUD has no design; the Unity adapter draws a debug `OnGUI` overlay. The
owner (2026-10-17): no "classic" UI kept for nostalgia, but one modern interface that
scales and looks good while keeping DK2's look. DK2's interface is fixed-size bitmaps laid
out for 4:3 (owner's 1024×768 screenshot: top bar, bottom panel with a round minimap ringed
by four buttons, tabs, icon grid, portrait). DK2 already picks its `.bf4` font size by screen
width (`BitmapText`), and `0x00427BA0` places HUD widgets in a virtual space (y up to 1332),
not device pixels. OpenKeeper's minimap (`4f2ab401`) copies DK2's 128×128 raster in fixed
pixels; it shimmers when stretched and rotated, and its markers are one-pixel dots.

**Decision.**
1. One HUD, no pixel-faithful classic mode. ADR-0242's levels A–D apply to the interface as
   `ART_DIRECTION.md` §13 spells them out.
2. Nothing is sized in device pixels: reference units against a 768-high reference, scaled by
   height, with a player UI scale; DK2's anchors are kept and extra width goes to the 3D view.
3. DK2's bitmaps, read from the install, are the reference; a modern version must match them
   when reduced to their size.
4. Text is DK2's `.bf4` letterforms at any size; the minimap is drawn on the GPU from a
   per-tile class grid updated per changed tile.
5. What the HUD shows is decided in `DK2.Presentation` and tested headlessly (ADR-0408
   item 4). Unity draws it with UI Toolkit (already in the project); if the pilot finds it
   cannot draw the minimap disc with a custom shader, uGUI replaces it by amendment.
6. Order: minimap, top bar, panel. Each step is judged beside DK2 at 1024×768 and at 1440p
   or above, and the owner accepts it.

**Why.** ADR-0242's rule applied to the interface: one that looks better than DK2's is a
defect, and one that looks like DK2 at 640×480 on a 4K screen is a defect too. The install
keeps the no-redistribution rule and gives every element a reference to check against. A
per-tile grid costs one texel per changed tile; a CPU raster costs every tile each refresh.

**Consequences.**
- No HUD-mode toggle; both 3D looks (ADR-0408) sit under the same interface.
- Research before the build: the minimap draw `0x0041CC50` (only its trap arm is read), the
  rest of the HUD layout around `0x00427BA0`, where each interface bitmap lives, Q197.
- Risks: small `.bf4` glyphs may give poor distance fields (the pilot measures it); ultrawide
  layouts need per-element owner choices.
- The cursor, front end and status flowers: 2D parts now, 3D parts later (`ART_DIRECTION.md` §13).

## ADR-0498 — The view plays a camera path on the simulation's tick
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** accepted · Presentation only · Amends ADR-0496 · Research: camera-paths.md §9

**Context.** The owner saw Level 1's opening play unlike DK2's. ADR-0496's view counted
wall-clock milliseconds while condition 72 counts ticks, and the two raced:
- A slow frame advanced the path by the whole stall but the simulation by at most Unity's
  capped `deltaTime`. The opening was skipped, and the keeper view showed before the fly-over.
- Both clocks gave path 1 53 ticks, 13.25 s. At a steady frame rate, path 201's request
  could reach the view a frame before path 1 had ended there. The view discarded a request
  that arrived while a path was drawn. Read from the code, not measured.

DK2 has no such race, since its condition 72 reads the camera.

**Decision.**
- `ScriptedViewRequest` carries the tick action 31 ran on.
- `CameraPathPlayback.Seek` places the frame at `first + 0.5 + 7.5 (t - (start + 1))`, with
  `t` the last tick run plus its debt. So the path ends by `start + 1 + DurationTicks`.
- The director ends a finished path before it applies requests. A new request replaces the
  drawn path, since the simulation already refuses overlapping starts.

**Consequences.**
- A stall no longer skips the opening, and the next path follows without a gap.
- With the game paused, the path stops; whether DK2's does is unread.
- No hash change: the request is observation only.
- The owner checked it in Unity the same day.

## ADR-0499 — A portal admits a Lair creature before the first Lair
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** accepted · Hash 264 · Research: portals.md §3, records 004DC810, 00494380

**Context.** On Level 4 our keeper's Imps died in the hundreds where DK2's lost none. On seed
1 the chain runs back to the portal:
- The east-gate party (tick 3467) survived because the owner's drop had one Goblin to land
  where DK2's had two. Alone against three heroes, ours fled and the party walked on.
- The heroes then stood by the (24,37) Guard Room, and our fleeing Imps ran there to raise
  the alarm. That is DK2's rule; DK2's heroes never got within its seven tiles.
- In DK2's Level 4 capture (`reverse-engineering/dk2runs/level4-live1/seed01`) the keeper's
  portal room appears at 787 and its first non-Imp creature, a Goblin, at 887; its first Lair
  room appears at 1100. Ours refused Goblins until a Lair existed.

`0x004DC810` fails an entry only when the keeper's slab total is below its size (`JC` at
`0x004DC86B`), and the Goblin's Lair entry asks 0. The Lair's weight in `0x004DC153` is a
flat 1.0 (3.0 when the lair object, `def+0x771`, is 0x16, as the Goblin's is) with no room walk. Ours also required the room to be owned.

**Decision.** `PortalRules.IsAttracted` keeps only the size comparison. The jump table at
`0x004DC8D4` also corrects the kind numbering in the docs: kind 0 tests nothing and kind 1 is
the room test.

**Consequences.**
- Lair creatures (Goblin, Firefly) can arrive with no Lair. Every other type still needs its
  room for a non-zero weight (`AttractionBudget`), so the owner's Level 20 result stands.
- Level 4 over 20 seeds: Imp deaths 301 → 272, median 12 → 5, wins 1 → 2. Levels 1–3 stay
  at 20/6/14. Only seeds whose portal is claimed before the Lair change.
- portals.md's "Level 1 produces nothing until its keeper builds a lair" is withdrawn; no
  capture had tested it, since every other recording built the Lair first.
- Every shipped attraction entry is kind 0 or 1, so `IsAttracted` treating each enabled entry
  as a room test is exact for the shipped data; kinds 2-4 remain unbuilt.
- Open: our portal claim comes at 663–1437 against DK2's 787, and the late seeds lose the
  most Imps. Digging matches DK2; our Imps claim the tile in front of the portal late.

## ADR-0500 — Creature separation gathers candidates from native tile bounds
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** The Level8 opening exposed missed creature contacts. The port's
radial prefilter excluded neighbours before the native combined-radius check.
Binary evidence: [creature-neighbour-query.md](research/creature-neighbour-query.md).

**Decision.** Use the native inclusive tile rectangle, including its upper-Y
width-clamp quirk. Preserve the soft-force arithmetic and arrival exemptions.
The broader query also exposes a prior torture-route deviation: victim approaches
now retain the native option word 0x20, including arrival separation suppression.
The existing centre-target deviation remains; no rigid creature clearance is added.

**Consequences.** Hash/save version 265; no new saved field. Contact timing changes
across maps. Tests observe alarm responders entering their states rather than
requiring both still occupy them on one arbitrary final tick.

## ADR-0501 — Camera and creatures share a late draw clock
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** A worker wait and presentation preparation can consume much of a
frame. Counting that work on the following frame causes slow/catch-up motion
even at high median FPS; the cinematic camera also sampled an earlier fraction.
Measurements: [level8-intro-motion.md](research/level8-intro-motion.md).

**Decision.** Sample elapsed real time after worker synchronization and again
after presentation preparation, retaining time scaling and the per-frame catchup
cap. Schedule newly owed worker ticks before releasing the world. Seek the path
on the same final tick/fraction as creature drawing, without consuming view requests.

**Consequences.** Fixed simulation steps and immutable render poses remain.
Positions stay clamped to known movement intervals; no extrapolation through walls.
Worker/presentation stalls can still cost frames and remain optimization work.

## ADR-0502 — Store arrival, facing and deposit take separate updates
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** accepted; integrated by ADR-0512

**Context.** An Imp deposited and passed through states 28 and 29 within its
arrival update, whereas DK2 captures retain each state. The original's state
28 turns toward the tile centre; its helper result is an angle, not occupancy.
Evidence and measurements: [imp-task-audit.md](research/imp-task-audit.md).

**Decision.** Complete the state-6 walk before entering 28. On later updates,
28 turns until facing and enters 29; 29 deposits and returns to selection.
An invalid store returns the worker to idle with its purse intact. Preserve
the aimed job retry and the store chooser's destination rules.

**Consequences.** Hash/save version 266, no new fields. Deposit availability,
later task choices and RNG draw order can change. Tests pin the intermediate
states, turn wait, missing store and snapshot continuation.
Campaign outcomes are diagnostics under ADR-0512.

## ADR-0503 — Resolve each worker's work before updating the next worker
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** accepted; integrated by ADR-0512

**Context.** Deferring every worker's strikes until after the worker pass hides
fallen walls from later task choices and completed-action checks. Binary order
and the measured counterfactual are in [imp-task-audit.md](research/imp-task-audit.md).

**Decision.** Resolve queued tile work after each eligible Imp's update, before
the next Imp. Keep the final work pass for remaining orders. Preserve task
cleanup, action cadence and job priorities. This does not implement DK2's
action-before-state order within a single creature.

**Consequences.** Hash/save version 267, no new fields. Same-turn task races,
later choices and RNG use can change. Tests cover both worker orders and a
chooser seeing a wall fall. ADR-0512 also applies a miner's own strike before
its seam and hands checks; a complete creature action scheduler remains unbuilt.

## ADR-0504 — Retain exhausted mining actions through their animation ending
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** provisional animation-clock implementation

**Context.** A depleted seam can leave an Imp in action 2 until the looping
mining animation stops. Binary and capture evidence, scope and acceptance
results: [mining-finish.md](research/mining-finish.md).

**Decision.** Reconstruct the ordinary art-5 loop phase from the work epoch,
retain its ending deadline, and resolve the task and hands after completion.
Apply the worker's own strike before checking the seam. Keep immediate
full-hands departure when the seam remains workable.

**Consequences.** Candidate hash/save 268 adds `MiningActionEndsAt`. The focused
regressions and snapshot/hash checks pass. Reconstructing phase from work entry
does not establish interrupted or other-art behavior. Keep that model isolated;
ADR-0512 integrates the independently supported own-strike ordering correction.

## ADR-0505 — Restore native Heart routes and retain only the small core guard
**Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** The owner authorizes reverting ADR-0452 if it harms fidelity.
The captured Level4 route and frozen-world movement controls isolate its
square exclusion: [imp-boundary-route.md](research/imp-boundary-route.md).

**Decision.** Route on the navigation cache without the extra 3×3 Heart mask.
Restore ADR-0439's object-width circular core guard and approach-side target
projection. Preserve native obstacle/arrival/escape rules, Hand and path-grid
policy, task selection and authored pillar positions. Supersede ADR-0452.

**Consequences.** Hash/save version 269; no new fields. The small core guard
remains an intentional deviation and can stall a synthetic walker continuously
forced into escape mode. Core safety during that override, attacks and ordinary
arrival are tested. Exact agreement on one frozen-world walk does not establish full
campaign or visual acceptance; those remain the next checks.

## ADR-0509 — Derive steering axes from resulting velocity
**Date:** 2026-10-18 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** The integrator's axes used force or displacement instead of the
native velocity source. Evidence and acceptance are in
[steering-velocity-axes.md](research/steering-velocity-axes.md).

**Decision.** Normalize body velocity after arrival and wall clamping, then
take its perpendicular. Preserve movement order, arrival timing, task choice
and Heart policy on main. Imp candidates are assessed separately by ADR-0512.

**Consequences.** Hash/save 274, no new fields; 270–273 belong to isolated
experiments. Existing axis values in snapshots/hashes change. This correction
does not claim to resolve campaign losses or idle random-stream differences.

## ADR-0510 — Preserve the native four-turn first dig gap
**Date:** 2026-10-18 · **Status:** accepted; integrated by ADR-0512

**Context.** The earlier three-turn digging claim fails a per-worker recheck;
the original captures support a four-turn first-cycle gap. The correction and
paired acceptance are in [mining-cadence.md §5](research/mining-cadence.md#5-the-other-work-kinds-rock-and-the-state-26-read-2026-09-28).

**Decision.** Apply the minimal ordinary-dig gap correction. Do not compensate
for changed outcomes with job-priority, idle-wakeup or work-rate changes.

**Consequences.** Experimental hash/save 275 introduces no new fields; the
integrated version is 280. The bounded hit sequence is verified independently
of the changed campaign outcomes; see ADR-0512.

## ADR-0512 — Integrate verified fidelity corrections despite changed replay wins
**Date:** 2026-10-18 · **Status:** accepted; owner instruction

**Context.** Unmatched-seed command replays were incorrectly used to veto
binary-supported corrections. The owner requires verified DK2 behavior on
master regardless of lost replay wins. Audit and remaining limits:
[imp-fidelity-integration.md](research/imp-fidelity-integration.md).

**Decision.** Integrate separate store states, inter-worker work visibility,
own-strike visibility before the mining hands test, newest-first movement,
exact idle arrival, the four-turn first dig gap, fractional Create Imp positions
and scoped height-driven creation landing. Retain changed replay outcomes as
diagnostics. Do not invent priority or reinforcement-timeout compensation.

**Consequences.** Hash/save 280 adds saved creation height; older snapshots
are incompatible. Dig and mining animation-ending phase reconstructions remain
provisional because their implementation scope is incompletely validated.
Campaign wins do not establish fidelity and cannot veto a verified correction.

## ADR-0513 — Route requests and stops zero the body's velocity
**Date:** 2026-10-19 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** `Creature_RequestRoute` (`0x004D0F60`) writes the entity position and a zero
velocity into the body before every route load, found or not, and `Creature_StopMoving`
(`0x0048ECE0`, through `0x004D1070`) ends with position and zero velocity. Every
state-level route load reaches the window loader `0x004D5100` through `0x004D0F60`; only
`Follow_Path`'s three refills skip it. Ours kept velocity on both paths, so a creature
carried its old speed into the first tick of its next walk; ADR-0512 fixed two callers
inline. Records: `functions/004D0F60.md`, `functions/0048ECE0.md`.

**Decision.** `WorldSteering.TryRouteTo` and `TryRouteToStance` zero velocity as
`0x004D0F60` does; `CreatureState.StopMoving` stops at the entity position with zero
velocity for every caller. The inline copies in the idle and store arrivals, the Reaper's
departure and the torture strap-on fold into it. `FollowPathRules`' refills are unchanged.

**Consequences.** Hash/save 281, no new fields. The two native functions are CONFIRMED; that
every one of our callers corresponds to a native stop or request is LIKELY (about 30 mapped,
the rest unmapped). States 8, 199 and 200 step without a route, so a stop there is now
visible as zero velocity; their native counterparts were not individually read.

## ADR-0514 — Dig and mining actions end on a stored animation clock
**Date:** 2026-10-19 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** ADR-0512 left the dig and mining end-of-action models provisional: they
reconstructed the slot-5 animation phase from work entry, valid only for an uninterrupted
bout. DK2 keeps the phase, rate and flags on the creature and advances them every turn
([animation-clock.md](research/animation-clock.md)).

**Decision.** Store the clip on `CreatureState` and step it with `ActionAnimationClock`
(install `0x004B37D0`, advance `0x004B3C10`, keep-or-install `0x00496700`), with the runner's
handler-done bit (`+0x3AD`). The state-14 and state-26 actions end by the runner's test
(`0x00496AA0`). A handler still being called whose tile is gone, or whose own strike emptied
it, sets the stop bit and holds until complete. Otherwise the action ends at the sticky wrap. After a mining
completion, a surviving task lets full hands take the store walk (`0x00465870`).
`WorkCadence` keeps the strike times and the other kinds' action ends.

**Consequences.** Hash/save 282 adds five creature fields. Every captured dig date and mining
hold the provisional models matched is reproduced by stepping. Uncaptured histories now follow
the binary's rules instead of extrapolating. The six-turn dig modulo and the immediate mining
end are gone for creatures with slot-5 data. Replaces the provisional parts of ADR-0512.

## ADR-0515 — Idle actions play their clip; installs draw their coin
**Date:** 2026-10-19 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Our Imp idle actions held a fixed 19 (action 43) or 24 turns (44), an
inferred mapping. The re-recorded Level 4 capture shows both actions at both lengths.
DK2 plays each idle clip once on the action clock. Its install (`0x004B37D0`) draws
`rand(2)` for art flagged `0xFC00` and swaps in the alternate clip on a 1 with `0x400`
([animation-clock.md](research/animation-clock.md#idle-actions)).

**Decision.** State 12 begins actions 43 and 44 counted on slots 20 and 31
(`ActionAnimationClock.BeginCounted`), when the art is available. They end by the
runner's no-handler rule. Every install, dig and mining included, draws the coin and may
swap to `CreatureDef.AlternateArt`, loaded from `+0x1083`.

**Consequences.** Hash/save 283 adds `CreatureState.ActionCount`. The simulation stream
now takes one more draw per fresh dig, mine or idle install, which shifts every later
draw. A definition without idle art wanders instead of resting.

## ADR-0516 — Walkers and dig turners keep a gone task, as DK2's states do
**Date:** 2026-10-19 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** We dropped a worker's job the turn its task disappeared, whatever its state.
DK2's walk (state 6, `0x00470C80`) never checks its task, and the dig entry (state 13,
`0x004654F0`) checks only that the task entry is alive, which outlives a fallen wall. In
Level 4 this lost the fresh claim's raise at (33,55) in all five seeds
([imp-claim-path.md §11](research/imp-claim-path.md#11-a-wall-falling-under-walkers-2026-10-19)).

**Decision.** `ImpTaskSystem.HoldsCourse` keeps the job for a travelling worker, and for a
dig-entry worker while the tile's dig task outlives the wall. A dig whose wall has fallen
is in position within one tile on each axis, diagonals included. The entry and work states then decide as before: 14 raises
the claim, and 13 with the task gone sets 10.

**Consequences.** Hash/save 284, no new fields. A player's untag no longer stops a walker
mid-walk; it drops on arrival, as the owner observed. Builds on ADR-0305's raise.

## ADR-0517 — An alarm goes only to a Guard Room
**Date:** 2026-10-19 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** `Combat_RaiseAlarm` (`0x004752B0`) walks the owner's rooms and skips any
whose type byte `+0x18` is not 9 (`0x00475336`), the filter ADR-0473 built for its twin
`0x00460B50`. Ours took the nearest room of any type, so fleeing Imps in Level 4 raised
alarms to the Portal, Hatchery and Lair (39 to the Portal in one seed). DK2 raised one
alarm in the whole capture ([combat-alarm.md §2](research/combat-alarm.md)).

**Decision.** `FearRules.RaiseAlarm` considers Guard Rooms only; with none it raises
nothing and draws no point.

**Consequences.** Hash/save 285, no new fields. The room is still chosen by bounding-box
centre where DK2 uses the stored `+0x27` tile. The gate behind DK2's rare alarms is unread.

## ADR-0518 — Speed does not scale with level
**Date:** 2026-10-19 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Ours scaled walking and running speed by the level table's Speed row
(105% at level 2, 250% at 10), from the owner's 2026-09-04 remark that levelled Imps
are faster. `Creature_SetSpeedMode` (`0x004887D0`) reads the speed from the definition
at `creature+0x370`, one record shared by every creature of a type; `Creature_LevelUp`
(`0x0048B120`) rescales health only; none of the 17 functions that index the level table
reads the Speed or RunSpeed rows. The Level 4 capture agrees: walking Imps step 0.4617
tiles a tick at levels 1 to 8, and nine types keep one walking and one running speed.
The speed-up the owner sees is Imp Haste, cast from level 4 by the task-walk wrapper
(ADR-0385): 362 casts in the capture, 326-364 in our replays. The extra 10% at level 3
made our neighbouring claim 12 ticks where DK2's is 13, so Level 4's Imps claimed the
hero Guard Room at (24,38) 34-67 turns early, starting the Dwarves' 240-second timer
early ([creature-levels.md §3](research/creature-levels.md#3-implementation)).

**Decision.** `CreatureMovementSystem.MaxSpeedOf` takes the definition's `Speed` or
`RunSpeed`; `CreatureLevelRules.SpeedRaw` is removed. The speed effect's floor, the hero
party's pace and the Library watcher read the definition's speed too.

**Consequences.** Hash/save 286, no new fields. The `creature_level_up` event no longer
reports a speed. For the Imp, Imp Haste through `0x004651A0` is the only level-dependent
speed; whether other casters of `0x0048CAD0` gate a speed by level is unchecked.

## ADR-0519 — Tier B tries a tile's objects after its gold
**Date:** 2026-10-20 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** `0x00469580`, the per-tile chain of the imp's Tier B ring scan, runs four
handlers in order: reinforce or repair (`0x0046AEA0`), gold (`0x0046B6D0`), loose objects
(`0x0046B9C0`) and the marked Secret Door (`0x0046CB80`). Codex's 2026-10-18 re-read and
five controlled runs of the original bytes confirmed all four; `TrySweep` had the first two
