([imp-priority-checks.md](research/imp-priority-checks.md)).

**Decision.** `TrySweep` calls `TryObjectAt` on each tile after the gold step, for an imp
holding no object or creature. The Secret Door step is not built: ours never marks a Secret
Door (`0x00512D20`), so no kind-11 entry exists for it to find. The carry gate is ours, as in
`TryTakeObject`: neither `0x00469580` nor state 10 (`0x00463DF0`) tests what the imp carries,
and a carrying imp should not reach Tier B.

**Consequences.** Hash/save 287, no new fields. Tier A's kind-8 search runs the same handler
over the whole map before Tier B, so the step takes a job only when an earlier step of the same
selection changed what Tier A saw. No fixture exercises the branch; the new hash pin moved
only with the version. The Secret Door step waits
for Secret Door marking.

## ADR-0520: native wet and bloody footprint counters and parent sprites

**Status:** accepted, 2026-10-20.

**Decision.** Run the native high-setting footprint path before combat/movement,
save and hash both native byte counters, and render the stationary flat
generation-zero parent art through the existing effect sprite pipeline.
Give parent art its own `effect` asset category so it cannot collide with
generated `effect_element` art. Keep original art behind the asset provider.

**Reason.** Footprints are direct effect art, not generated elements or
animation contact events. Existing flat rendering already supplies the native
shape, heading and floor projection. Evidence and remaining native-setting,
flight and fading boundaries: [creature-footprints.md](research/creature-footprints.md).

**Consequences.** Hash/save 288; older snapshots are rejected. Direct support
is limited to static, stationary, fixed-scale flat alpha art. Native print
expiry is preserved without an invented opacity curve; visual acceptance is pending.

## ADR-0521 — Preserve creature names and blood groups in simulation state
**Date:** 2026-10-18 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Query and hover text consume the constructor's personal-name and
blood-group indices. Producing decorative random values in the UI would change
them across saves and omit the original simulation random draws. Evidence:
the records for `0x00491900`, `0x004919C0` and `0x004872A0`.

**Decision.** Store the native-width indices in `CreatureState`, hash and save
them, and initialize them with the simulation's shared `SimRandom`. Bind that
generator when `GameSimulation` takes ownership of the world. Assign existing
uninitialized creatures in acquisition order and future creatures in their
spawn path, after linking the owner list and before arming payday.

**Adaptation.** Map construction currently predates creation of the seeded
simulation, so its two identity draws per creature are reconstructed together
before the first tick. This does not reproduce interleaving with every original
constructor random call. An internal unassigned-name sentinel distinguishes
that reconstruction from a saved, initialized identity; restoring consumes no
additional identity draws. Query presentation never owns a random generator.

**Consequences.** Hash/save version 289 (275, then 283, on classic-look/step6 before master's later versions merged) also includes ADR-0295's payday stamp.
Existing random trajectories can change because missing constructor draws are
now consumed. Tests of another mechanic with scripted draws must supply an
already initialized identity instead of silently changing that mechanic's draws.

## ADR-0522 — Lighting follows visual fidelity: Unity fill by default

**Context.** Native-only lighting (`nativeInitialAmbient`) became the default on
2026-10-16 (16cf59d5), and the scene saved it on 2026-10-17 (d220c077). It uses
DK2's confirmed zero ambient and short-radius tile lights, but DK2's own fill
lights were never found. On Level 3 it left the Hero Gate roof, castle walls and
the Heart-facing faces of pillars (29,35) and (29,37) pure black. The owner's
DK2 screenshots of the same intro show them lit, fading with camera distance.

**Decision.** The owner ruled on 2026-10-20 that lighting is judged by visual
fidelity: use Unity's lighting, tuned to look like DK2. The default is the Unity
sky and sun fill (`nativeInitialAmbient` off). Native-only stays a diagnostic.

**Consequences.** Nothing renders pitch black for lack of a light. The Unity
look is flatter and less warm than DK2's, so tuning toward the owner's DK2
references (warm tint, falloff with camera distance) is open work. The native
light research in classic-lighting.md remains the reference for colours and torch
placement.

**Amendment, 2026-10-21 (owner: "DK2 has warmer light").** Against SHOT0068-0079 our
fill was about twice DK2's and cooler (DK2/ours red 0.65, green 0.55, blue 0.37), while
torch-lit faces matched. The classic shader tints the sky and sun fill (`classicFillTint`,
0.55/0.44/0.28, set by eye) and gives it only to explored tiles or ones with a submitted
terrain light (`ClassicTileFillBuffer`, a proxy for the 0x0043C310 gate). The owner
reports DK2's unexplored ground dark but not black, and revealed ground (Sight, claim
scan) as bright as explored: scanned tiles take the full fill, unlit ones a tuned
`classicUnlitFill` (0.25). A mild fade with eye distance (0.5 to 1.0) stays.
A stronger path fade was dropped the same day: probe renders showed it blacking out the
Heart intro (far plane 10 tiles), and the owner saw it snap on the Lord's zoom-out.
All are tuned values, not DK2's, set every frame from DungeonRunner (Inspector-live).

**Amendment, 2026-10-22 (owner: "unity lighting doesn't feel like DK2").** A probe render
registered pixel-for-pixel on SHOT0126 (Level 1 Heart, play camera, fog on) and divided by
an unlit render gives each game's light per surface class. With DK2's own tile lights alone
ours matches within about 0.05 per channel on floors, rock tops and walls; the fill added on
top lifted every class and, with red already clipped at 1, turned orange to yellow (green/red
0.77-0.94 against DK2's 0.57-0.83). So the fill now fades out as the shader's other light
(DK2's lights plus the ambient keys' level) brightens: times saturate(1 - luma /
`classicFillFloor`), 0.5 by default (tuned). Instance-lit models (Heart arches, steps,
creatures) keep the whole fill: under DK2's lights alone they render near black where the
owner's shots show them pale, a measured difference left after Q603, and the owner saw them
stand out at once. Terrain tops' inverted lighting normal (static-mesh-lighting.md section 1)
is for the tile lights; the fill turns a downward terrain normal back, which recovers tops
and their sloped faces but not a top quarter's vertical side.
The near-white Heart arches, steps and pit ring in SHOT0126 are the Hand's own light
(`+0x33E`, RGB 511 radius 1.75 tiles, under the cursor over explored ground), now built;
with it at the Heart the probe's steps and arch match the shot (0.95-1.0 neutral).

## ADR-0523 — Trigger action 42 marks creatures in six world slots
**Date:** 2026-10-21 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Level 1's Lord of the Land wears a star ring that cycles his level and a sword
(owner's SHOT0075/0076). Trigger 85 runs creature action 42 on his creation; it was unbuilt
(Q607). Evidence: the records for `0x0049AC80`, `0x005096A0`, `0x005096C0`, `0x00491B40`,
`0x00596770`, `0x00597270` and `0x00596850`.

**Decision.** `WorldState.HeroSlots` keeps DK2's six world records (`+0x72BD`): a creature id
for its tag and a value byte, hashed and saved (version 290). Creature action 42 with a
non-zero byte takes the first free slot with no duplicate check, nothing when all six are
full; zero frees the creature's first slot. `RemoveCreature` frees it as the death
bookkeeping does (`0x00488396`). The flower reads the slots: a hero-owned creature holding
one draws `Objective` over its centre (loaded at 0x2000, the centre at 0x1000; the drawn size
is matched to SHOT0068, not read) and takes SJ-Fighting, SJ-Prison or SJ-Torture by the value.

**Left out.** Creature `+0x3EA` bit `0x20000`, which action 42's zero clears when it found a slot and
Creature_Update sets; the record's dword at `+3`; Objective-2 (creature `+0x3F7`); the
player-context arm, which puts a player's tag in a slot (`0x004C89E4`).

**Consequences.** Hash and snapshot 290. The Lord shows his ring from creation, and
flowers now draw on camera paths, where DK2 shows his star (they had been hidden with the
HUD). The Objective quad is not doubled again for 0x2000: doubled, it was twice DK2's. That the
icon reader's list is this one is LIKELY: CWorld `+0x2EC` and `+0x2F0` are one function,
but the reader's `this+8` is not traced.

## ADR-0524 — Rooms run flames round their rims
**Date:** 2026-10-21 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** DK2 runs keeper-coloured flame tongues round every room but the Heart and the hero
gates (room-border-effects.md; the owner asked whether we had them). Room_BorderEffectTick
(`0x004E7CD0`) moves one cursor per room and asks for effect 20 on odd turns; nothing here did,
and the view dropped effect 20, a generation-0 animated sprite, with its Next effect 118.

**Decision.** `WorldState.RoomBorderCursors` keeps DK2's per-room cursor (tile, orientation,
phase; step 800), hashed and saved (version 291). `RoomBorderFlameSystem` runs in the room
ticks before health: a cursor belongs to the room holding its tile, a room without one starts at
its lowest tile (DK2: its first slab), and the walk is `0x006A22F8`'s table. The view draws a
stationary generation-0 sprite parent by `0x004347E0`'s scale arms (flags 2, 4, 0x20 with
`0x004B3B40`'s return, else one draw) and tints it by art flag 2: the owner's palette colour,
the wall clock's cycling one for the neutral player (`0x0050F880`), with no floor of 48.

**Consequences.** Hash and snapshot 291. A flame grows to 1228 in 11 updates and dies at 20,
shrunk to a fifth; its 118 throws three white sparks. Left out: the type handler's veto of the
tick (slot `+0x15` returning 0), the parent animation's start phase, and neutral cycling for
elements (claim mist keeps palette 2).

## ADR-0525 — The bottom bar shows DK2's message tabs
**Date:** 2026-10-21 · **Status:** accepted

**Context.** Menu39's message tabs, Review Objective and the message panel were unbuilt
(message-tabs.md, read 2026-10-21). The simulation already keeps DK2's message records.

**Decision.** The view reads the queue as `0x00423BD0` does: the first eight of the viewer's
records, oldest first, tabbed while NeedsTab and not dismissed. The opened and dismissed bits
(record `+0x2A`, written by the interface without a packet) and the slide stamp live in
`MessageTabsView`, not in hashed state, so the simulation and hash are unchanged. Text and
graphic come from the type table copied into `MessageTypeTable`; text resolves through
Speech.str, the level table or Text.str by the reference's band.

**Consequences.** Every message our queue posts now tabs and flashes until opened; all but the
creature-anger types 17 and 18, whose text DK2 builds from the creature, read out on hover. A reload forgets which tabs were opened or dismissed (DK2 saves the bits with the record).
Sounds, the Ally and goto buttons, and name substitution wait (message-tabs.md §8).

## ADR-0526 — A hand drop obeys DK2's drop gate
**Date:** 2026-10-23 · **Status:** accepted · supersedes ADR-0077 · Q198

**Context.** DK2 decides where the hand may put a thing in the input layer: `0x0040D8F0`
colours the drop cage and alone lets a click become a drop, through the map tests
`0x00450910` (creature) and `0x00450BE0` (object); the simulation never tests the tile again
(placement-cursor.md, "The drop cage's colour"; records `0x0040D8F0`, `0x00450910`,
`0x00450BE0`, `0x00450D40`, `0x0040AE80`, `0x00408EE0`). Ours tested `owner == player` plus
unclaimed floor for a worker (ADR-0077), and the cage asked a copy of that.

**Decision.** `HandRules.CanDrop` mirrors `0x0040D8F0` per item kind, and `HandRules.DropLands`
(the gate, then ours below) is the one rule the cage and `HandSystem.Drop` ask; the replay
rig's drop fallback asks it too. The check stays in `HandSystem`, our authoritative place.
- Allied ground is `WorldState.AreAllied` (`0x004BF3D0`, self included), never the neutral player.
  Neutral is the one id `[0x006F2548]`, player 2, as the binary compares it; a loaded map gives
  non-ownable ground to player 2, so owner 0 is not neutral.
- Nav-solid and door tiles are refused: solid terrain, and a closed, completed door, the two
  writers of bit 3 and the high nibble in our navigation bytes. An open door is floor
  (CONFIRMED: `0x004A66F0` writes the nibble only for a completed door that is not open).
- A Portal centre is a Portal (or Hero Portal) tile with its own room on all four sides,
  the `+0x0C == 4` code of `0x004EF730`; the Heart's inner 3×3 is first slab +1..+3
  (`0x004DA150`), ours the bounding box's corner; a floor slot is an interior cell
  (`0x00454110` for Prison, Temple and Combat Pit); a Combat Pit's free slot is
  `RoomNeedRules.DropTest` (`0x004D8430`).
- `HasBeenKnockedOut` (set by `0x00459560` and `0x004596D0` on entering state 216, cleared by
  nothing found) has no field here: ours is imprisoned or collapsed. Our hand holds no dead body, so `0x00450D40` has no arm.

**Past the gate.** A creature must still stand on the tile (`WorldPathGrid.IsWalkable`) unless
`DisposalRules` takes it. Once the gate has passed this refuses only structure tiles: an Imp on
its own Heart's eight platform tiles around the centre, and a non-evil worker on its own Portal
centre. The Heart refusal is the owner's 2026-09-15 observation (ADR-0148): STRONGLY INFERRED
from play. Where DK2 refuses those eight is not found: the gate's map test has no arm for them,
and no navigation-byte writer marks them (the Heart's builder writes 3 on its centre only,
structure-blocks.md §5.4).

**Consequences.** Hash and snapshot 292, behaviour only. Newly accepted: an ally's ground, a
worker on neutral-owned claimed floor, Call To Arms anywhere open. Newly refused: closed door
tiles, a Combat Pit floor slot for a worker or when the pit is full, a non-worker on another
keeper's Portal centre, Chicken and Call To Arms on a Portal centre or the Heart's inner 3×3,
an unbeaten tool in a Prison, Temple, Combat Pit or Torture Chamber. DK2's computer keeper
drops without this gate (`0x004BC710`, Q541); ours goes through it, and its targets are its
own ground.

## ADR-0530 — A room tile is refused where a trap, a door or a rival's creature stands
**Date:** 2026-10-23 · **Status:** accepted · Q501 · Research: `docs/research/bridge-placement.md` §1–2

**Context.** DK2's placement predicate `0x0044F630` asks `0x0044F800` on every arm. It walks the
tile's thing chain and refuses on a thing of class 3 (trap, `0x004A7940`) or 4 (door, `0x004A5070`)
of any owner, or a class 0 creature that is not the Imp (`+0x36F != 1`), is not the player's own
(`+0x28`, compared raw) and is not dying (`+0x3E6` bit 21). Objects, class 2, are skipped without
reading a definition. `RoomRules.CanBuild` had no such test. OpenKeeper's `c047a8b1` (2026-10)
lets only Obstacle objects block and does not test creatures; DK2 lets no object block.

**Decision.** `RoomRules.IsObstructed` mirrors `0x0044F800` over the tile chain
(`TileLink.TileIndex`), and the world overload of `CanBuild` returns the new
`RoomPlacement.Obstructed` when it holds. The per-tile overload stays free of it: a tile a dragged
span spreads to is marked without the predicate (`0x004C57F0`) and laid with it skipped, so only
seeds meet the test. Dying is `CreatureDeathRules.IsDown`, as at the door (`DoorSystem.Eligible`);
a corpse is DK2's dead-body class and is skipped.

**Consequences.** Hash and snapshot 295 (293 and 294 are taken on classic-look/step6), behaviour only. Newly refused: a room or a single bridge
tile on a trap, a door, or a rival's non-Imp creature; a span whose only seeds are obstructed.
The owner, 2026-10-23: a bridge was built over a hero standing in water as part of a longer drag,
which the spread predicts; the owner saw a single-tile placement onto such a tile refused (a hero; a rival keeper's creature is assumed the same, and the raw owner compare agrees). The owner also saw that an enemy corpse does not stop a room tile and that a door blueprint or an unbuilt trap does.
